See the [recording notes](docs/DEMO.md) for the model setup and reproduction steps.\n\n[Mobile MP4](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8014d185-346c-4954-8ff0-26c582c5093a) · [Web MP4](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0cc87de0-c3c1-4f24-b7df-e7d04bb946fd) · [Recording details and reproduction](docs/DEMO.md)\n\nThe [Jev aquarium-trip demo](docs/demos/jev-generative-ui.md) walks through a fictional school email, clarification choices, sourced exhibit cards, hands-on preference refinement, and a confirmed selection. [Watch the 83-second live Jev recording](assets/demos/2026-09-23/jev-live-web.mp4), where TypeSafe Jev makes the decisions and a scripted agent keeps the trip scenario repeatable. A [scripted-decision sample recording](assets/demos/2026-09-23/jev-web.mp4) is also available.\n\n## What it is\n\nOpenMuse is a personal-agent application with an agent computer, visible work, and rich results. It runs its own server, task worker, and browser worker. You can inspect and change the source under the MIT license.\n\nThe computer combines **persistent Chromium and an optional Linux workspace**. The agent can browse public pages, run commands in its own container, work with files, and move PDFs between the computer and the app. You can open its browser or terminal and continue the work. Graphical desktops and autonomous checkout remain future work.\n\n## Features\n\n| Surface | What runs in this alpha |\n| --- | --- |\n| **Chat** | CopilotKit headless chat with streamed AG-UI events, mailbox search and reading, send/stop in one input pill, a visible follow-up queue, retained drafts, delegated tasks, and inline email, browser, PDF, plan, and finance cards. |\n| **Agent computer** | Persistent browser profiles and takeover console; optional isolated Linux terminal, saved command receipts, editable workspace files, and PDF transfer. |\n| **Activity** | Durable task plans, progress, input requests, pause/resume/cancel/retry, approvals, and saved receipts. SQL leases recover interrupted work. |\n| **Ideas** | Suggestions with source evidence; edit, accept, or dismiss. Sent replies and completed matching work are excluded. |\n| **Goals & Tracking** | Goals and milestones; recurring public-page checks for changes, text availability, or USD price thresholds, with deduplicated alerts and failure backoff. |\n| **Documents** | Email attachment → PDF → requested form values → filled copy → reviewed reply → receipt. Native/web PDF viewing, paging, zoom, supported fields, and sharing. |\n| **Finance** | Import transaction CSV to create a spending summary with categories, transactions, and a savings-goal action. |\n| **Gmail & Calendar** | Google OAuth adapters, complete mail threads, drafts/attachments, calendar discovery, and reviewed event creation/update/deletion. Live credentials required. |\n| **Personal context** | Editable name, tone, avatar, and memories. Background-update preferences and durable in-app notifications. |\n| **Rich Threads** | CopilotKit Intelligence persistence in every mode, with a stable main conversation, side chats, renaming, archiving, restoring, and replay. A server-only project key is required. |\n\nThe [feature inventory](docs/FEATURES.md) describes implemented capabilities and planned extensions. Health/bank/social connectors, device push, voice, generated executable tools, and automatic reservations/payments are on the [roadmap](ROADMAP.md).\n\n## Quick start\n\n**Requirements:** Node 24 LTS, pnpm 11.19.0, and a CopilotKit Intelligence project key. The local sample app needs no model, Google account, or Docker.\n\n```sh\ngit clone https://github.com/CopilotKit/OpenMuse.git openmuse\ncd openmuse\npnpm install --frozen-lockfile\ncp .env.example .env\nnpx copilotkit@latest login\nnpx copilotkit@latest project select\n# Set CPK_INTELLIGENCE_API_KEY in .env to the generated server-only project key.\n# Keep the CLI-generated CPK_TELEMETRY_ID too, including in deployed server environments.\npnpm dev\n```\n\nIn another terminal:\n\n```sh\npnpm dev:web\n```\n\nOpen [localhost:8081](http://localhost:8081). The API runs at [localhost:8787/api/health](http://localhost:8787/api/health).\n\n### Try it\n\n1. In Chat, send **“Complete the permission slip”**. Open the task, supply fictional form values, inspect the saved PDF, and review the prepared reply. This writes only to the local mailbox.\n2. In **Goals → Track**, create a built-in availability watch, then change the built-in test page to trigger an alert.\n3. In **Menu → Delegate task → Finance**, use **Try example transactions** to create an interactive spending tracker.\n4. Start the [browser worker](#browser-worker) and configure a model, then ask **“Check out Hacker News for cool stuff”** or **“Summarize copilotkit.ai”**. Follow the browser inline and use **Take control** to open its session. For a model-free version of this flow, follow the [AI Mock demo setup](docs/DEMO.md#run-the-agent-browser-demo).\n\nFor iOS or Android, use `pnpm --dir apps/mobile ios` or `pnpm --dir apps/mobile android`. Xcode or Android tooling is required. The PDF reader needs an Expo development build; use [native setup](apps/mobile/README.md).\n\n## Deploy on Render\n\n[![Deploy to Render](https://render.com/images/deploy-to-render-button.svg)](https://render.com/deploy?repo=https://github.com/CopilotKit/OpenMuse)\n\n[render.yaml](render.yaml) deploys three services: the API, the web app, and a private browser. The API answers `/` with JSON, so the UI is its own static site.\n\n### First run\n\n1. Click **Deploy to Render**. Wait until `openmuse-api`, `openmuse-web`, and `openmuse-browser` are live.\n2. On `openmuse-api`, open **Environment** and copy `OPENMUSE_ACCESS_KEY`.\n3. Open the `openmuse-web` URL and sign in with that key.\n4. Send a message.\n\nThe deploy form asks for three values you provide. Render generates the other two.\n\n| Variable | Set by | If it is missing |\n|---|---|---|\n| `CPK_INTELLIGENCE_API_KEY` | You. Run `npx copilotkit@latest login`, then `npx copilotkit@latest project select`. Keep it on the server. | Chat cannot open a thread. |\n| `CPK_TELEMETRY_ID` | You. Keep the identity generated by the same project selection. | Runtime usage cannot be attributed to the Intelligence signup account. |\n| `OPENAI_API_KEY` | You. Used by the default `openai/gpt-5`. Change `MODEL` and supply the matching provider key for Anthropic or Google. | The model call fails. |\n| `OPENMUSE_ACCESS_KEY` | Render | You cannot sign in. |\n| `TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY` | Render | The API refuses to start in live mode. |\n\nHealth check: `https://<openmuse-api>/api/health`.\n\n### Services\n\n| Service | Plan | What it runs |\n|---|---|---|\n| `openmuse-api` | Standard, with a 1 GB disk at `/var/data` | The Hono API and the in-process task worker. `DATA_DIR` is `/var/data/openmuse`. |\n| `openmuse-web` | Static site | The Expo web export. `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL` is baked in at build time. |\n| `openmuse-browser` | Private service, Standard, 1 GB disk at `/data` | Playwright and Chromium. The API calls it on the private network. |\n\n**Standard** is the smallest plan that stays up. At 512 MB the process runs out of memory before it binds a port, because PGlite loads an embedded Postgres build.\n\n**The disk** holds the database, PDFs, and the signing key. A redeploy without it wipes that data. Chat threads are stored by CopilotKit Intelligence, so a thread can still load after you sign back in even when the disk was never attached.\n\n**Live mode** is required. Render binds `0.0.0.0`, and sample mode rejects any host that is not loopback. The Blueprint sets `WORKSPACE_MODE=live`.\n\n**Browsing is included, and you can take it out.** `openmuse-browser` is a private service, so it has no public URL. The API reaches it at `http://openmuse-browser:8790` with a token Render generates. If the private hostname is not `openmuse-browser`, set `BROWSER_WORKER_URL` to `http://<that-host>:8790`. To deploy without it, delete the `openmuse-browser` service and the `BROWSER_WORKER_URL` and `WORKER_TOKEN` entries on `openmuse-api`. Chat, drafts, and tasks still run. Page reads, screenshots, and **Take control** do not.\n\nThe Docker computer and Google mail or calendar need the setup in the sections below. This Blueprint does not start them.\n\n## Configure the agent and Google\n\nCopy the commented settings in [.env.example](.env.example) into your private `.env`:\n\n1. Set `AGENT_BACKEND=model`, `MODEL=provider/model-id`, and the matching provider key. CopilotKit supports the configured OpenAI, Anthropic or Google provider. Fictional data can still be used with a real model. Provider keys stay on the server.\n2. Create or select a CopilotKit Intelligence project with `npx copilotkit@latest login` and `npx copilotkit@latest project select`. Keep the generated `CPK_INTELLIGENCE_API_KEY` on the server.\n3. For personal mail/calendar, set `WORKSPACE_MODE=live`, the generated `CPK_INTELLIGENCE_API_KEY`, a random `OPENMUSE_ACCESS_KEY` of at least 24 characters, and `TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY` containing 32 random bytes encoded as base64. Restart the API.\n4. Configure a Google OAuth web client with Gmail and Calendar APIs enabled. Set `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` and `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`; register `${PUBLIC_API_URL}/api/google/callback` as its redirect URI. Configure consent/test-user access in your Google project.\n5. Open **Apps → Gmail** (or **Google Calendar**), connect read access, and grant write access when needed. Every send or calendar change still requires its own stored review. Changing/disconnecting the account invalidates pending connection-bound work.\n\nGoogle credentials are encrypted at rest. File URLs and browser consoles use short-lived signatures. This deployment uses one owner protected by a shared access key; it is not a multi-tenant authentication system. Use HTTPS and restricted network access for a remote host. Keep the default local-data mode on loopback.\n\n## Public web search\n\nWeb search is enabled by default. Set `WEB_SEARCH_ENABLED=false` on the API and any separate task worker to disable it. With a configured model, delegated tasks and built-in model chat (`AGENT_BACKEND=model`) use [Parallel's free, keyless Search MCP](https://docs.parallel.ai/integrations/mcp/search-mcp) as their built-in search provider. Ask, for example, “Find the official CopilotKit React Native setup instructions and cite the sources.” Results include source URLs and excerpts; delegated tasks save them as evidence. Scripted sample chat and external AG-UI conversations keep their existing tools.\n\nSearch sends model-generated queries and context, which may include information from your conversation or task, plus a random per-chat/task session identifier to Parallel. See [Parallel's privacy policy](https://parallel.ai/privacy-policy). Free access is rate limited; failures are reported without a paid fallback. Stopping chat or interrupting a task cancels its search.\n\n## Browser worker\n\nSet `BROWSER_WORKER_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8790` and a random `WORKER_TOKEN` of at least 32 characters in `.env`.\n\n```sh\npnpm --dir apps/worker exec playwright install chromium\npnpm dev:browser\n```\n\nOr use `docker compose --env-file .env -f infra/compose.yaml up --build -d`. The same token must reach the API and worker. Sessions have persistent Chromium profiles; the app can open a live screenshot console and import PDF downloads. Agent tools can read public pages and hand interactive work to the person. [Worker setup and boundaries](apps/worker/README.md).\n\n## Persistence and operation\n\n### Linux terminal and workspace\n\nBuild the computer image, enable it on the API, then open **Computer → Terminal → Start computer**:\n\n```sh\ndocker build -t openmuse-computer:local apps/computer\nCOMPUTER_ENABLED=true pnpm dev\n```\n\nThe API needs access to the Docker CLI and engine. Commands run in a nonroot container with no host-directory mounts or credentials. A named `/workspace` volume retains files when stopped. Terminal networking is disabled; public web access uses the browser worker. Commands have a 30-second limit and saved output/exit receipts. **Files** supports folders, text editing, and PDF transfer to/from Documents. This is a Linux container, not a full operating-system VM. [Setup, Colima option, and boundaries](docs/COMPUTER.md).\n\n### Application storage\n\nBy default, embedded PGlite, documents and the signing key live in `.openmuse/`; browser profiles live in `.openmuse/browser-profiles/`. Keep that directory private and back it up. The API hosts the task worker. The host must remain running for background work.\n\nFor a separate task worker, configure the same `DATABASE_URL`, secrets and shared `DATA_DIR` for both processes, then set `TASK_WORKER_ENABLED=false` on the API and run `pnpm dev:worker`. PGlite cannot be opened by separate processes. Production commands are `pnpm build:server`, `pnpm start` and `pnpm start:worker`. Run one API instance; task workers coordinate through SQL leases.\n\nNo hidden retry occurs after an uncertain external write. Review its provider outcome before creating a replacement. Pausing/cancelling prevents subsequent task steps; an already approved in-flight provider request may finish.\n\n## CopilotKit Rich Threads\n\nEvery deployment requires `CPK_INTELLIGENCE_API_KEY` on the API server for CopilotKit Intelligence conversation persistence and replay. Create or select a project with `npx copilotkit@latest login` and `npx copilotkit@latest project select`, set the generated server-only key, and restart the API. The native menu uses `useThreads`; rich tool results link back to saved tasks, documents, and browser sessions.\n\nIntelligence is a separate service and is not included in this repository's MIT license. No project key is shipped. [Configuration and validation boundaries](docs/RICH-THREADS.md).\n\n## Signup and runtime tracking\n\nThe CopilotKit SDK sends runtime telemetry through the shared CopilotKit sink to PostHog with `accessibility_title: \"OpenMuse\"`. Telemetry defaults to full capture; explicit SDK opt-outs and sampling settings take precedence. Keep the CLI-generated `CPK_TELEMETRY_ID` alongside the server-only project key when deploying. Intelligence records completed account signups separately; OpenMuse runtime usage can be joined to those accounts after the sink resolves the identity. [Setup, opt-out and PostHog validation](docs/TELEMETRY.md).\n\n## Architecture\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart TD\n  Client[Expo / React Native / Web] -->|AG-UI and authenticated API| API[Hono + CopilotKit runtime]\n  API --> Tasks[Durable task worker]\n  API --> Threads[CopilotKit Intelligence required in every mode]\n  API --> Store[(PGlite or PostgreSQL)]\n  Tasks --> Store\n  Tasks --> Review[Stored action review]\n  Review --> Google[Gmail / Calendar adapters]\n  Tasks --> Browser[Chromium worker + persistent profiles]\n  API --> Browser\n  API --> Computer[Optional Docker Linux computer]\n  Tasks --> Computer\n  Computer --> Volume[(Persistent workspace volume)]\n  Tasks --> Files[PDF files + structured artifacts]\n  API -. future adapter .-> OpenBot[OpenBot]\n```\n\n| Directory | Purpose |\n| --- | --- |\n| `apps/mobile` | Shared iOS, Android, and web UI with CopilotKit headless hooks. |\n| `apps/server` | API, CopilotKit runtime, identity boundary, task engine, reviews, files, and persistence. |\n| `apps/worker` | Token-protected Playwright browser service with persistent profiles. |\n| `apps/computer` | Nonroot Linux image, bounded filesystem helper, and real container verification. |\n| `packages/domain` | Shared types and request validation. |\n| `packages/integrations` | Google and browser protocol adapters. |\n| `packages/backends` | Optional OpenBot HTTP adapter and its identity boundary. |\n| `tests` | Workflow, runtime, persistence, provider-contract, and authorization tests. |\n\n### OpenBot compatibility\n\nOpenMuse's native client and personal-agent workflows are independent of OpenBot. The disabled OpenBot adapter is pinned and contract-tested against upstream interfaces. Live user/session bridging, routine mapping, and computer backend wiring remain future work. OpenBot's Intelligence runtime is not a raw AG-UI endpoint. [Integration contract](docs/OPENBOT-INTEGRATION.md).\n\n## Development\n\n```sh\npnpm lint\npnpm typecheck\npnpm test\npnpm build:server\npnpm build:web\npnpm build:ios\npnpm build:android\npnpm --dir apps/worker typecheck\npnpm test:browser\npnpm test:computer\n```\n\nPlatform build scripts export JavaScript/Hermes bundles; they do not produce signed app binaries. Browser checks use controlled HTTP fixtures; the local check requires installed Chromium, and the container check requires Docker and registry access to build its image. CI also exercises the browser and Linux computer containers. See [contribution guidance](CONTRIBUTING.md) and [verification results](docs/VERIFICATION.md).\n\n## Contributing and license\n\nIssues and pull requests are welcome. Start with [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md), [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md), and the [security policy](SECURITY.md).\n\nMIT licensed. Built by CopilotKit. Its original interface and fictional assets are included. Website, email, and document content supplies evidence, not permission to act.\n","display_url":"https://github.com/CopilotKit/openmuse/blob/main/README.md"}}

Five new checks cover email search/read ownership, disconnected mail, evidence-based demo replies, and exhibit extraction without navigation noise.\n- Biome formatting/lint, server/mobile/browser-worker TypeScript checks, and the server build pass.\n- Expo exports web, iOS Hermes, and Android Hermes bundles. Its disposable container and volume are removed after the test.\n- CI now includes a separate computer-container build/smoke job. Its YAML parses with unique keys and valid workflow triggers. The existing browser-container CI job was not rerun locally for this release; remote CI results remain separate from these local checks.\n\n## Agent browser verification\n\n- September 16: fresh native iPhone capture exercised Hacker News → CopilotKit → takeover and scrolling. A separate desktop capture exercised actual mailbox search/read → full email viewer → Monterey Bay Aquarium research → takeover. Browser results came from real Chromium; email came from the isolated fictional mailbox. The web capture reported no page errors. Live model and Google-account acceptance remain outside this recording.\n- September 16: the new capybara bundles on web, iOS and Android. Both final recordings and covers were visually inspected, and MP4/GIF dimensions, durations, and decoding were checked. All 154 tests, lint, typecheck, server build, and three platform exports pass locally. Worker/container implementation is unchanged; the earlier smoke-test evidence below is historical.\n\n- Actual CopilotKit BuiltInAgent streams `browse_web` calls and results. Tests cover successive reads, honest worker failures, cancellation, owner isolation, concurrent navigation/read pairing, and persistent per-thread profile reuse.\n- Native iPhone acceptance: ask for Hacker News highlights → fully terminate and relaunch the app → summarize CopilotKit → open **Take control**. Local chat now has a stable routed CopilotKit thread identity across app launches.\n- Inline cards show reading progress, the source title, a real browser preview, and takeover. A historical source does not display a different page after that browser moves on. Pending calls show paused status after a stopped run; takeover waits until the active chat run finishes.\n- The [AI Mock runner](DEMO.md#run-the-agent-browser-demo) drives the actual model/tool loop against a separate real Chromium worker. Its three tests verify prompt routing, current-turn tool results, failures, and model-protocol execution. Recorded responses are scripted page excerpts, not live-model reasoning.\n- Full formatting/lint, server/mobile/worker types, all 149 tests, server build, all three Expo exports, frozen lockfile validation, and the real Chromium lifecycle test passed for this change. PGlite cannot be shared across processes; use PostgreSQL for a separate worker. |\n| Document job | Background import → field input → new PDF → action review → sample sent receipt is tested without a client. The iPhone viewer displays the saved names and checkbox on a real two-page PDF. | Supported AcroForms only. OCR/scanned forms and some field types are not supported. |\n| Reviews | Ownership/hash/version binding, expiry, account changes, disconnects, concurrent decisions, uncertain writes, and cancellation are tested. | An already dispatched provider request may finish after cancellation. |\n| Gmail / Calendar | Real adapter code with controlled HTTP fixtures covers OAuth state races, scopes, complete MIME/threads/attachments, CRLF sends, calendar discovery, event CRUD, ETags, time zones, DST gaps, and unsupported recurrence. | No live Google credentials were supplied. A real-account acceptance run remains required. |\n| Browser | Actual Chromium screenshots and console displayed on iPhone and web. Hacker News and CopilotKit navigation were exercised through both clients and updated the worker's page. Ownership, authorization, URL/DNS/egress checks, failed downloads, and recovery have automated coverage. | A separate Chromium worker; no automatic booking/payment or hostile-tenant isolation. |\n| Linux computer | Native Terminal created `today.md`; Files read/save and PDF import/export/view were exercised. The real Docker smoke verifies isolation and persistence.     structured result: {"content":"# CopilotKit Rich Threads and the agent computer\n\nOpenMuse uses `@copilotkit/react-native/headless` for its custom native and web interface. Chat messages, tool cards and task-linked documents render through CopilotKit's AG-UI agent and tool hooks.\n\n## Rich Threads\n\nEvery workspace mode requires a CopilotKit Intelligence project key before the API will start. Create or select a project:\n\n```sh\nnpx copilotkit@latest login\nnpx copilotkit@latest project select\n```\n\nKeep the generated key in the API server environment and restart the API:\n\n```dotenv\nCPK_INTELLIGENCE_API_KEY=your-project-key\n```\n\nNever put the key in an `EXPO_PUBLIC_`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_`, or `VITE_` variable. The server constructs `CopilotKitIntelligence`, and `identifyUser` resolves the owner from the verified OpenMuse session. The existing deployment is a single-user workspace; its access key must not be shared as a multi-user login. See [CopilotKit's runtime setup](https://docs.copilotkit.ai/intelligence/connect-your-runtime) for project-key configuration.\n\nWith this configuration, the conversation menu uses CopilotKit's native `useThreads` hook to list, rename, archive, restore and paginate conversations. The server saves an owner-bound main thread ID and provisions it through Intelligence before the first message, so reloading during the first run retains the same conversation. Side chats create a fresh client thread ID and persist on their first run. Selecting a saved conversation mounts a private `useAgent({ agentId, runtimeAgentId, threadId })` instance and calls `copilotkit.connectAgent` to replay the thread. Visited chats remain mounted during navigation, preserving their drafts and queues. Stop explicitly requests `copilotkit.stopAgent`.\n\nThe composer stays editable during replies. Follow-ups enter a visible, removable queue and run in order after the current reply and its persistence finish. Stopping or failing a reply pauses the queue; SDK errors emitted without rejecting the run promise still stop subsequent sends. The queue lives in the open app, not a durable server inbox. Delegated tasks remain separate server work. See the [interaction design](EXPERIENCE.md).\n\nRich tool messages retain task IDs. The renderer fetches current task status, browser previews, PDF links and structured artifacts from the authenticated task endpoint. Expiring file/preview URLs are generated by the server rather than stored in thread messages. New Intelligence conversations never load or overwrite `/api/conversation`.\n\nThe API fails at startup with a missing-key error when the key is unset. Existing local sample history is not automatically uploaded to Intelligence.\n\nAutomatic thread naming is disabled; conversations can be renamed in the menu. Intelligence is a separately configured service, not bundled with this MIT-licensed application. See [headless threads](https://docs.copilotkit.ai/headless-threads) for the platform lifecycle and hosting options.\n\n## Agent computer\n\nThe Computer control below the avatar opens a persistent workspace with browser sessions and files. Browser cards show actual worker screenshots; **Open browser** opens the existing interactive console for takeover. PDFs open in the native/web readers. Tasks can read public pages, monitor changes and collect PDFs using the same worker.\n\nOpening a session renews its short-lived console access. **Refresh connection** renews access without navigating; **Reopen** keeps the saved profile and uses the address in the input. The console reports live/disconnected state, preserves unsent text after an error, and pauses preview polling when hidden. Closing a session retains its profile and downloads.\n\nRun the browser worker using the `BROWSER_WORKER_URL` and `WORKER_TOKEN` setup in the [README](../README.md). Browser profiles persist on disk. The optional [Linux computer](COMPUTER.md) adds real command execution, saved output, editable files, and PDF transfer. CopilotKit's built-in conversation and task-worker tools use this same computer; remote AG-UI backends must supply their own equivalent tools. Interactive reservations still require user takeover; autonomous booking, checkout, graphical desktops and per-user VM isolation are not implemented. The OpenBot adapter remains an extension point for other computer backends.\n\n## Validation scope\n\nThe Rich Threads route tests run against the real CopilotKit runtime with a mocked Intelligence service boundary. They cover session enforcement, owner scoping, pagination, rename, archive, rich message preservation and provider failures. They do not replace a live account test for Intelligence WebSocket persistence/replay. That test requires a configured project key.\n","title":"RICH-THREADS.md","modified_date":"2026-09-23T10:25:02Z","url":"https://github.com/CopilotKit/openmuse/blob/a4944f4c471d3dc93b8bfc060b5da309b5216ab2/docs/RICH-THREADS.md","display_url":"https://github.com/CopilotKit/openmuse/blob/a4944f4c471d3dc93b8bfc060b5da309b5216ab2/docs/RICH-THREADS.md","display_title":"RICH-THREADS.md","structuredContent":{"title":"RICH-THREADS.md","content":"# CopilotKit Rich Threads and the agent computer\n\nOpenMuse uses `@copilotkit/react-native/headless` for its custom native and web interface. Create or select a project:\n\n```sh\nnpx copilotkit@latest login\nnpx copilotkit@latest project select\n```\n\nKeep the generated key in the API server environment and restart the API:\n\n```dotenv\nCPK_INTELLIGENCE_API_KEY=your-project-key\n```\n\nNever put the key in an `EXPO_PUBLIC_`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_`, or `VITE_` variable. The server constructs `CopilotKitIntelligence`, and `identifyUser` resolves the owner from the verified OpenMuse session. The existing deployment is a single-user workspace; its access key must not be shared as a multi-user login. See [CopilotKit's runtime setup](https://docs.copilotkit.ai/intelligence/connect-your-runtime) for project-key configuration.\n\nWith this configuration, the conversation menu uses CopilotKit's native `useThreads` hook to list, rename, archive, restore and paginate conversations. The server saves an owner-bound main thread ID and provisions it through Intelligence before the first message, so reloading during the first run retains the same conversation. Side chats create a fresh client thread ID and persist on their first run. Selecting a saved conversation mounts a private `useAgent({ agentId, runtimeAgentId, threadId })` instance and calls `copilotkit.connectAgent` to replay the thread. Visited chats remain mounted during navigation, preserving their drafts and queues. Stop explicitly requests `copilotkit.stopAgent`.\n\nThe composer stays editable during replies. Browser cards show actual worker screenshots; **Open browser** opens the existing interactive console for takeover. PDFs open in the native/web readers. Tasks can read public pages, monitor changes and collect PDFs using the same worker.\n\nOpening a session renews its short-lived console access. **Refresh connection** renews access without navigating; **Reopen** keeps the saved profile and uses the address in the input. The console reports live/disconnected state, preserves unsent text after an error, and pauses preview polling when hidden. Closing a session retains its profile and downloads.\n\nRun the browser worker using the `BROWSER_WORKER_URL` and `WORKER_TOKEN` setup in the [README](../README.md). Browser profiles persist on disk. CopilotKit's built-in conversation and task-worker tools use this same computer; remote AG-UI backends must supply their own equivalent tools. items = await Sandbox.list({\n        ...opts(),\n        query: { metadata, state: [\"running\", \"paused\"] },\n      }).nextItems();\n      return items.map((item) => item.sandboxId);\n    },\n    async info(sandboxId) {\n      const { Sandbox } = await load();\n      const info = await Sandbox.getInfo(sandboxId, opts());\n      return { ...info, state: info.state === \"running\" ? \"running\" : \"paused\" };\n    },\n    async create(template, metadata) {\n      const { Sandbox } = await load();\n      const box = await Sandbox.create(template, {\n        ...opts(),\n        requestTimeoutMs: createMs,\n        metadata,\n        timeoutMs: idleMs,\n        resolution,\n        lifecycle: { onTimeout: { action: \"pause\", keepMemory: false }, autoResume: false },\n      });\n      return box.sandboxId;\n    },\n    async pause(sandboxId) {\n      const { Sandbox } = await load();\n      // Static pause: connect() would resume a box that is already paused.\n      await Sandbox.pause(sandboxId, { ...opts(), keepMemory: false });\n    },\n    async connect(sandboxId, timeoutMs) {\n      const { CommandExitError, Sandbox } = await load();\n      const box = await Sandbox.connect(sandboxId, { ...opts(), timeoutMs });\n      const setup = async (command: string, asUser: string) => {\n        try {\n          return (\n            await box.commands.run(command, {\n              user: asUser,\n              envs: { DISPLAY: display },\n              timeoutMs: 45_000,\n            })\n          ).exitCode;\n        } catch (error) {\n          if (error instanceof CommandExitError) return error.exitCode;\n          throw error;\n        }\n      };\n      return {\n        async run(command, options) {\n          return box.commands.run(command, { ...options, background: true });\n        },\n        setup,\n        async writeRootFile(path, data) {\n          await box.files.write(path, data, { user: \"root\" });\n        },\n        async readFile(path) {\n          return box.files.read(path, { format: \"bytes\", user });\n        },\n        async keepAlive(timeoutMs) {\n          await box.setTimeout(timeoutMs);\n        },\n        async stream(known) {\n          // Exit bits: 1 = x11vnc runs, 2 = noVNC listens, 4 = `known` started it.\n          const up = await setup(streamState(known ? streamTag(known) : \"-\"), user);\n is restarted.\n          // The SDK refuses to start while any x11vnc runs.\n          if (up !== 0 && (await setup(streamStop, user)) !== 0)\n            throw new Error(\"Previous desktop stream did not stop\");\n          await box.stream.start({ requireAuth: true });\n          const url = box.stream.getUrl({ authKey: box.stream.getAuthKey() });\n          await setup(`printf %s ${streamTag(url)} > ${streamTagFile}`, user);\n          return url;\n        },\n      };\n    },\n  };\n}\n\nconst stopped = () => new AppError(\"Start the computer before using its terminal or files\", 409);\n\n// Marks which URL the running stream belongs to, so a URL cached by this process is\n// never returned after another process restarted the stream with a new password.\nconst streamTagFile = \"/tmp/openmuse-stream\";\nconst streamTag = (url: string) => createHash(\"sha256\").update(url).digest(\"hex\").slice(0, 16);\nconst streamState = (tag: string) =>\n  [\n    \"v=0\",\n    \"pgrep -x x11vnc >/dev/null && v=$((v | 1))\",\n    \"netstat -tln | grep -q ':6080 ' && v=$((v | 2))\",\n    `[ \"$(cat ${streamTagFile} 2>/dev/null)\" = ${tag} ] && v=$((v | 4))`,\n '[w]ebsockify'\",\n  \"for i in $(seq 50); do pgrep -x x11vnc >/dev/null || netstat -tln | grep -q ':6080 ' || exit 0; sleep 0.1; done\",\n  \"pkill -9 -x x11vnc; pkill -9 -f '[w]ebsockify'; sleep 0.5\",\n  \"pgrep -x x11vnc >/dev/null || netstat -tln | grep -q ':6080 ' || exit 0\",\n  \"exit 1\",\n].join(\"\\n\");\n\n/** In-box wrapper for one terminal command, with the same 30 second limit as Docker.\n * Output goes to temporary files, so a background GUI app (`firefox-esr URL &`)\n * cannot hold the output stream open after the shell exits. A watchdog stops the\n * command once those files pass `ceiling` bytes, so a runaway writer cannot fill the disk. */\nexport function desktopCommand(\n  command: string,\n  limit = computerOutputLimit,\n  ceiling = diskCeiling,\n) {\n  const script = [\n    // fd 3 is the real stderr; bash's own job notices go to /dev/null.\n    \"exec 3>&2 2>/dev/null\",\n    \"o=$(mktemp -d) || exit 125\",\n    `/usr/bin/timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after=2s 30s /bin/bash --noprofile --norc -c \"$1\" >\"$o/out\" 2>\"$o/err\" </dev/null 3>&- &`,\n    \"p=$!\",\n    `{ while kill -0 $p 2>/dev/null; do [ $(( $(wc -c <\"$o/out\") + $(wc -c <\"$o/err\") )) -gt ${ceiling} ] && { : >\"$o/big\"; kill $p; break; }; sleep 0.1; done; } </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 3>&- &`,\n    \"w=$!\",\n    \"wait $p\",\n    \"s=$?\",\n    \"kill $w 2>/dev/null\",\n    // Sent first: the server's output cap is shared, and stdout alone can fill it.\n    `[ -e \"$o/big\" ] && printf 'Output exceeded the limit; the command was stopped.\\\\n' >&3`,\n    `head -c ${limit + 1} \"$o/out\"`,\n    `head -c ${limit + 1} \"$o/err\" >&3`,\n    'rm -rf \"$o\"',\n    \"exit $s\",\n  ].join(\"\\n\");\n  return `/bin/bash --noprofile --norc -c ${quote(script)} openmuse ${quote(command)}`;\n}\n\n// One GUI action, shaped like Anthropic's computer-use tool. Coordinates are native\n// screenshot pixels; the screen is `resolution` wide and high.\nexport const desktopActionSchema = z\n  .object({\n    action: z.enum([\n      \"screenshot\",\n      \"left_click\",\n      \"double_click\",\n      \"right_click\",\n      \"mouse_move\",\n      \"type\",\n      \"key\",\n      \"scroll\",\n      \"wait\",\n    ]),\n    coordinate: z\n      .array(z.number().int().min(0))\n      .length(2)\n      .optional()\n      .describe(\"[x, y] in screenshot pixels. Clicks and scroll without it use the pointer\"),\n    text: z\n      .string()\n      .min(1)\n      .max(1000)\n      .optional()\n      .describe(\"Text for type; for key, xdotool key names or combos such as Return or ctrl+l\"),\n    scroll_direction: z.enum([\"up\", \"down\", \"left\", \"right\"]).optional(),\n    scroll_amount: z.number().int().min(1).max(15).optional().describe(\"Wheel clicks, default 3\"),\n    duration: z.number().min(0.1).max(10).optional().describe(\"Seconds to wait, default 1\"),\n  })\n  .superRefine((value, ctx) => {\n    const need = (field: \"coordinate\" | \"text\" | \"scroll_direction\", present: boolean) => {\n      if (!present)\n        ctx.addIssue({ code: \"custom\", path: [field], message: `${value.action} needs ${field}` });\n    };\n    if (value.action === \"mouse_move\") need(\"coordinate\", !!value.coordinate);\n    if (value.action === \"type\" || value.action === \"key\") need(\"text\", !!value.text);\n    if (value.action === \"scroll\") need(\"scroll_direction\", !!value.scroll_direction);\n    if (value.action === \"key\" && value.text && !/^[A-Za-z0-9_+ -]+$/.test(value.text))\n      ctx.addIssue({\n        code: \"custom\",\n        path: [\"text\"],\n        message: \"Use xdotool key names, e.g. ctrl+l\",\n      });\n    const [x = 0, y = 0] = value.coordinate ?? [];\n    if (x >= resolution[0] || y >= resolution[1])\n      ctx.addIssue({\n        code: \"custom\",\n        path: [\"coordinate\"],\n        message: `The screen is ${resolution.join(\"x\")}`,\n      });\n  });\nexport type DesktopAction = z.infer<typeof desktopActionSchema>;\n\n/** Receipt line for an action, e.g. `desktop left_click (640, 400)`. */\nexport function describeDesktopAction(action: DesktopAction) {\n  return [\n    \"desktop\",\n    action.action,\n    action.coordinate && `(${action.coordinate.join(\", \")})`,\n    action.text && JSON.stringify(action.text.slice(0, 200)),\n    action.scroll_direction && `${action.scroll_direction} ${action.scroll_amount ?? 3}`,\n    action.action === \"wait\" && `${action.duration ?? 1}s`,\n  ]\n    .filter(Boolean)\n    .join(\" \");\n}\n\n/** The xdotool (or sleep) command for one action; undefined for a plain screenshot. */\nexport function desktopInput(action: DesktopAction) {\n  const [x, y] = action.coordinate ?? [];\n  const at = action.coordinate ? `mousemove --sync ${x} ${y} ` : \"\";\n  switch (action.action) {\n    case \"screenshot\":\n      return undefined;\n    case \"left_click\":\n      return `xdotool ${at}click 1`;\n    case \"double_click\":\n      return `xdotool ${at}click --repeat 2 --delay 120 1`;\n    case \"right_click\":\n      return `xdotool ${at}click 3`;\n    case \"mouse_move\":\n      return `xdotool ${at.trim()}`;\n    case \"type\":\n      return `xdotool type --delay 12 -- ${quote(action.text ?? \"\")}`;\n    case \"key\":\n      return `xdotool key -- ${(action.text ?? \"\").trim().split(/\\s+/).map(quote).join(\" \")}`;\n    case \"scroll\": {\n      const button = { up: 4, down: 5, left: 6, right: 7 }[action.scroll_direction ?? \"down\"];\n      return `xdotool ${at}click --repeat ${action.scroll_amount ?? 3} ${button}`;\n    }\n    case \"wait\":\n      return `sleep ${action.duration ?? 1}`;\n  }\n}\n\n// One fixed path: actions on a computer are serialized by the service's lease.\nconst screenshotFile = \"/tmp/openmuse-screenshot.jpg\";\n// A VNC viewer that loses focus mid-shortcut (e.g. Alt+Tab in the user's browser)\n// leaves that modifier held, and every later click, key and wheel event then becomes\n// a shortcut. Input actions release all modifiers first.\nconst releaseModifiers =\n  \"xdotool keyup Shift_L Shift_R Control_L Control_R Alt_L Alt_R Super_L Super_R Meta_L Meta_R ISO_Level3_Shift\";\n// Input, a short settle so the screen shows its effect, then a JPEG screenshot (about\n// 40 to 200 KB at 1280x800, small enough to send to the model on every action).\n// Exit 3 means the input failed, 4 the screenshot.\nconst actionScript = (input: string | undefined) =>\n  [\n    ...(input?.startsWith(\"xdotool \") ? [releaseModifiers] : []),\n    ...(input ? [`${input} || exit 3`, \"sleep 0.5\"] : []),\n    `scrot --pointer --quality 80 --overwrite ${screenshotFile} || exit 4`,\n  ].join(\"\\n\");\n\n// Starts Xvfb and Xfce when they are not running. A filesystem-only resume\n// cold-boots the VM, which drops both and the DISPLAY set at creation.\nconst sessionScript = [\n  \"pgrep -x xfce4-session >/dev/null && exit 0\",\n  // Braces keep `&` on the app alone; a backgrounded `a || b` subshell would hold the output pipe.\n  `pgrep -x Xvfb >/dev/null || { setsid Xvfb ${display} -ac -screen 0 ${resolution.join(\"x\")}x24 -retro -dpi 96 -nolisten tcp -nolisten unix </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 & }`,\n  `for i in $(seq 50); do xdpyinfo -display ${display} >/dev/null 2>&1 && break; sleep 0.2; done`,\n  \"setsid startxfce4 </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &\",\n  \"for i in $(seq 100); do pgrep -x xfce4-session >/dev/null && pgrep -x xfdesktop >/dev/null && exit 0; sleep 0.3; done\",\n  \"exit 1\",\n].join(\"\\n\");\n\nlet filesScript: Promise<string> | undefined;\n// Source runs from apps/server/src; the built server runs from the repository root.\nconst loadFilesScript = () =>\n  (filesScript ??= readFile(new URL(\"../../computer/files.py\", import.meta.url), \"utf8\").catch(() =>\n    readFile(resolve(\"apps/computer/files.py\"), \"utf8\"),\n  ));\n\n// Runs each owner's computer in one E2B Desktop sandbox, matched by metadata.\n// Paused means stopped: /workspace lives on the sandbox disk and processes end.\n// Sandbox.connect resumes a paused box, so only start() and the first attach in a\n// process connect. Later operations reuse the cached handle, which fails on a\n// paused box instead of resuming it after a Stop.\n// One cached connection per sandbox. `url` is the stream this process started and\n// `streaming` the stream check or restart in flight, shared by concurrent viewers.\ninterface Handle {\n  box: DesktopBox;\n  url?: string;\n  streaming?: Promise<string>;\n}\nexport class E2BDesktopComputer {\n  private readonly handles = new Map<string, Handle>();\n  private readonly connecting = new Map<string, Promise<Handle>>();\n  constructor(\n    private readonly config: Config,\n    private readonly driver: DesktopDriver = e2bDesktopDriver(config),\n  ) {}\n  template() {\n    const template = this.config.computerE2bTemplate ?? \"desktop\";\n    if (!/^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_./-]{0,250}$/.test(template))\n      throw new AppError(\"COMPUTER_E2B_TEMPLATE is invalid\", 503);\n    return template;\n  }\n  private async control<T>(work: () => Promise<T>) {\n    try {\n      return await work();\n    } catch (error) {\n      if (error instanceof AppError) throw error;\n      throw new AppError(\n        \"E2B desktop operation failed. Check E2B_API_KEY and COMPUTER_E2B_TEMPLATE.\",\n        503,\n      );\n    }\n  }\n  // Fail-closed analog of the Docker inspection: refuse to attach to anything this\n  // deployment did not create. \"missing\" : info.state === \"running\" ? \"running\" : \"stopped\";\n  }\n  // The service lease serializes timeout updates across API and worker processes.\n  // Read E2B's current deadline so another process's refresh is never shortened.\n  private awake(info: DesktopInfo | undefined, ms: number) {\n    return Math.max(ms, info?.state === \"running\" ? info.endAt.getTime() - Date.now() : 0);\n  }\n  private forget(id: string) {\n    this.handles.delete(id);\n  }\n  async start(labels: Record<string, string>) {\n    const existing = await this.inspect(labels);\n    const id = existing\n      ? existing.sandboxId\n      : await this.control(() => this.driver.create(this.template(), labels));\n    const info = await this.inspect(labels); // re-check before start, including the shared deadline\n    if (existing?.state !== \"running\") this.forget(id);\n    const cached = this.handles.get(id);\n    const box =\n      cached?.box ?? (await this.control(() => this.driver.connect(id, this.awake(info, idleMs))));\n    if (cached) await this.control(() => box.keepAlive(this.awake(info, idleMs)));\n    if (!cached) this.handles.set(id, { box });\n    const script = await loadFilesScript();\n    await this.control(async () => {\n      if (\n        (await box.setup(\n          `mkdir -p /workspace /opt/openmuse && chown ${user}:${user} /workspace`,\n          \"root\",\n        )) !== 0\n      )\n        throw new AppError(\"Computer workspace could not be prepared\", 503);\n      await box.writeRootFile(\"/opt/openmuse/files.py\", script);\n      if ((await box.setup(sessionScript, user)) !== 0)\n        throw new AppError(\"Computer desktop session did not start\", 503);\n    });\n  }\n  async stop(labels: Record<string, string>) {\n    const info = await this.inspect(labels);\n    if (info?.state === \"running\") {\n      this.forget(info.sandboxId);\n      await this.control(() => this.driver.pause(info.sandboxId));\n    }\n  }\n  private async attach(\n    labels: Record<string, string>,\n    keepMs = idleMs,\n    firstConnect?: (work: () => Promise<Handle>) => Promise<Handle>,\n    verified?: DesktopInfo,\n  ) {\n    const info = verified ?? (await this.inspect(labels));\n    if (info?.state !== \"running\") throw stopped();\n    const id = info.sandboxId;\n    const cached = this.handles.get(id);\n    if (cached) {\n      try {\n        await cached.box.keepAlive(this.awake(info, keepMs));\n      } catch (error) {\n        const current = await this.inspect(labels);\n        if (current?.state !== \"running\") {\n          this.forget(id);\n          throw stopped();\n        }\n        await this.control(() => Promise.reject(error));\n      }\n      return cached;\n    }\n    // First use in this process, e.g. after an API restart. Start the computer to restore it.\",\n        409,\n      );\n    }\n    const handle: Handle = { box };\n    this.handles.set(id, handle);\n    return handle;\n  }\n  /** The stream URL, shared by every viewer: concurrent requests join one stream check\n   * or restart, so two viewers never race to restart it with different passwords. */\n  async desktopUrl(\n    labels: Record<string, string>,\n    firstConnect?: (work: () => Promise<Handle>) => Promise<Handle>,\n  ) {\n    const handle = await this.attach(labels, desktopIdleMs, firstConnect);\n    handle.streaming ??= this.control(() => handle.box.stream(handle.url))\n      .then((url) => (handle.url = url))\n      .finally(() => (handle.streaming = undefined));\n    return handle.streaming;\n  }\n  /** Perform one GUI action and return the screenshot taken after it. Every X11 call\n   * sets DISPLAY itself: the SDK's screenshot and input helpers rely on the DISPLAY\n   * that Sandbox.create puts in the sandbox env, and a resumed box no longer has it. */\n  async act(\n    labels: Record<string, string>,\n    action: DesktopAction,\n    beforeInput?: () => Promise<void>,\n  ) {\n    const { box } = await this.attach(labels);\n    const input = desktopInput(action);\n    let uncertain = false;\n    if (input) {\n      await beforeInput?.();\n      const script = [\n        ...(input.startsWith(\"xdotool \") ? [releaseModifiers] : []),\n        `${input} || exit 3`,\n      ].join(\"\\n\");\n      try {\n        // xdotool dispatches sequentially: a later failure can follow a delivered\n        // click or Return. A nonzero exit cannot confirm that no input occurred.\n        uncertain = (await box.setup(script, user)) !== 0;\n      } catch {\n        // A lost response cannot tell us whether xdotool delivered the input.\n        // Capture a screenshot if possible, but never replay the input here.\n        uncertain = true;\n      }\n    }\n    const warning = uncertain\n      ? \"The desktop input outcome is unknown: it may already have been performed. Inspect a fresh screenshot before repeating the action; do not automatically retry it.\"\n      : undefined;\n    const screen = { mimeType: \"image/jpeg\" as const, width: resolution[0], height: resolution[1] };\n    try {\n      const code = await this.control(() =>\n        box.setup(actionScript(input ? \"sleep 0.5\" : undefined), user),\n      );\n      if (code !== 0) throw new AppError(\"The desktop screenshot failed\", 502);\n      const image = await this.control(() => box.readFile(screenshotFile));\n      return { ...screen, image, uncertain, warning };\n    } catch (error) {\n      if (!input) throw error;\n      return {\n        ...screen,\n        image: new Uint8Array(),\n        uncertain,\n        warning:\n          warning ??\n          \"Action performed; the screenshot could not be taken. Take a screenshot before retrying the action.\",\n      };\n    }\n  }\n\n  /** Same contract as DockerRunner: command outcomes are results, never exceptions. */\n  async run(\n    labels: Record<string, string>,\n    command: string,\n    options: {\n      cwd?: string;\n      input?: string;\n      timeoutMs: number;\n      signal?: AbortSignal;\n      maxOutputBytes?: number;\n      propagateAttachError?: boolean;\n      verified?: DesktopInfo;\n    },\n  ): Promise<DockerResult> {\n    const output = computerOutput(options.maxOutputBytes);\n    const { result, limit, finish } = output;\n    let received = 0,\n      handle: DesktopHandle | undefined,\n      overflowed = false;\n    // Terminal output is also capped in the VM; this guards filesystem responses\n    // and any unexpected output outside that wrapper.\n    const capture = (write: (data: string | Buffer) => void) => (data: string) => {\n      write(data);\n      received += Buffer.byteLength(data);\n      if (received > limit + outputCeiling && !overflowed) {\n        overflowed = true;\n        void handle?.kill().catch(() => {});\n      }\n    };\n    const { CommandExitError, InvalidArgumentError, TimeoutError } = await sdk();\n    let box: DesktopBox;\n    try {\n      ({ box } = await this.attach(labels, idleMs, undefined, options.verified));\n    } catch (error) {\n      if (options.propagateAttachError) throw error;\n      // Nothing started, so this is a plain failure and the box keeps running.\n      result.stderr =\n        error instanceof AppError ? error.message : \"The computer could not be reached.\";\n      return result;\n    }\n    const abort = () => {\n      result.interrupted = true;\n      void handle?.kill().catch(() => {});\n    };\n    options.signal?.addEventListener(\"abort\", abort, { once: true });\n    try {\n      if (options.signal?.aborted) abort();\n      if (result.interrupted) return finish();\n      try {\n        handle = await box.run(command, {\n          user,\n          cwd: options.cwd ?? \"/workspace\",\n          envs: { DISPLAY: display },\n          stdin: options.input !== undefined,\n          timeoutMs: options.timeoutMs,\n          signal: options.signal,\n          onStdout: capture(output.stdout),\n          onStderr: capture(output.stderr),\n        });\n      } catch (error) {\n        if (error instanceof InvalidArgumentError) {\n          // A missing working directory is rejected before the command starts.\n          result.exitCode = 126;\n          output.stderr(\"The working directory does not exist.\");\n          return finish();\n        }\n        throw error;\n      }\n      if (options.signal?.aborted) abort();\n      if (options.input !== undefined && !result.interrupted) {\n        // Encode once: separate string slices can split a surrogate pair, and\n        // the SDK encodes each send independently, replacing both halves.\n        const input = Buffer.from(options.input, \"utf8\");\n        for (let i = 0; i < input.length; i += stdinChunk)\n          await handle.sendStdin(input.subarray(i, i + stdinChunk));\n        await handle.closeStdin();\n      }\n      result.exitCode = (await handle.wait()).exitCode;\n    } catch (error) {\n      if (error instanceof CommandExitError) result.exitCode = error.exitCode;\n \"\\nOutput exceeded the limit; the command was stopped.\";\n    return result;\n = \"user\"; // the desktop template's uid 1000 account\nconst display = \":0\";\nexport const resolution: [number, number] = [1280, 800];\n// The SDK keeps every output byte in memory, so a command Fails on a paused box instead of resuming it. */\n  keepAlive(timeoutMs: number): Promise<void>;\n}\n/** The slice of the E2B Desktop SDK this provider uses; tests replace it with a fake. */\nexport interface DesktopDriver {\n  list(metadata: Record<string, string>): Promise<string[]>;\n  info(sandboxId: string): Promise<DesktopInfo>;\n  create(template: string, metadata: Record<string, string>): Promise<string>;\n  /** Filesystem-only pause: every process ends and the disk persists. */\n  pause(sandboxId: string): Promise<void>;\n  /** Connect, resuming a paused sandbox, and set its idle timeout. */\n  connect(sandboxId: string, timeoutMs: number): Promise<DesktopBox>;\n}\n\n// `load` is the SDK module; tests pass a fake one.\nexport function e2bDesktopDriver(config: Config, load = sdk): DesktopDriver {\n  const opts = () => ({ apiKey: config.e2bApiKey, requestTimeoutMs: controlMs });\n  return {\n    async list(metadata) {\n      const { Sandbox } = await load();\n      const items = await Sandbox.list({\n        ...opts(),\n        query: { metadata, state: [\"running\", \"paused\"] },\n      }).nextItems();\n      return items.map((item) => item.sandboxId);\n    },\n    async info(sandboxId) {\n      const { Sandbox } = await load();\n      const info = await Sandbox.getInfo(sandboxId, opts());\n      return { ...info, state: info.state === \"running\" ? \"running\" : \"paused\" };\n    },\n    async create(template, metadata) {\n      const { Sandbox } = await load();\n      const box = await Sandbox.create(template, {\n        ...opts(),\n        requestTimeoutMs: createMs,\n        metadata,\n        timeoutMs: idleMs,\n        resolution,\n        lifecycle: { onTimeout: { action: \"pause\", keepMemory: false }, autoResume: false },\n      });\n      return box.sandboxId;\n    },\n    async pause(sandboxId) {\n      const { Sandbox } = await load();\n      // Static pause: connect() would resume a box that is already paused.\n async stream(known) {\n          // Exit bits: 1 = x11vnc runs, 2 = noVNC listens, 4 = `known` started it.\n          const up = await setup(streamState(known ? streamTag(known) : \"-\"), user);\n streamTagFile = \"/tmp/openmuse-stream\";\nconst streamTag = (url: string) => createHash(\"sha256\").update(url).digest(\"hex\").slice(0, 16);\nconst streamState = (tag: string) =>\n  [\n Coordinates are native\n// screenshot pixels; the screen is `resolution` wide and high.\nexport const desktopActionSchema = z\n  .object({\n    action: z.enum([\n      \"screenshot\",\n      \"left_click\",\n      \"double_click\",\n      \"right_click\",\n      \"mouse_move\",\n      \"type\",\n      \"key\",\n      \"scroll\",\n      \"wait\",\n    ]),\n    coordinate: z\n      .array(z.number().int().min(0))\n      .length(2)\n      .optional()\n      .describe(\"[x, y] in screenshot pixels. Clicks and scroll without it use the pointer\"),\n    text: z\n      .string()\n      .min(1)\n      .max(1000)\n      .optional()\n      .describe(\"Text for type; for key, xdotool key names or combos such as Return or ctrl+l\"),\n    scroll_direction: z.enum([\"up\", \"down\", \"left\", \"right\"]).optional(),\n    scroll_amount: z.number().int().min(1).max(15).optional().describe(\"Wheel clicks, default 3\"),\n    duration: z.number().min(0.1).max(10).optional().describe(\"Seconds to wait, default 1\"),\n  })\n  .superRefine((value, ctx) => {\n    const need = (field: \"coordinate\" | \"text\" | \"scroll_direction\", present: boolean) => {\n      if (!present)\n        ctx.addIssue({ code: \"custom\", path: [field], message: `${value.action} needs ${field}` });\n    };\n    if (value.action === \"mouse_move\") need(\"coordinate\", !!value.coordinate);\n    if (value.action === \"type\" || value.action === \"key\") need(\"text\", !!value.text);\n    if (value.action === \"scroll\") need(\"scroll_direction\", !!value.scroll_direction);\n    if (value.action === \"key\" && value.text && !/^[A-Za-z0-9_+ -]+$/.test(value.text))\n      ctx.addIssue({\n        code: \"custom\",\n        path: [\"text\"],\n        message: \"Use xdotool key names, e.g. ctrl+l\",\n      });\n    const [x = 0, y = 0] = value.coordinate ?? [];\n    if (x >= resolution[0] || y >= resolution[1])\n      ctx.addIssue({\n        code: \"custom\",\n        path: [\"coordinate\"],\n        message: `The screen is ${resolution.join(\"x\")}`,\n      });\n  });\nexport type DesktopAction = z.infer<typeof desktopActionSchema>;\n\n/** Receipt line for an action, e.g. `desktop left_click (640, 400)`. */\nexport function describeDesktopAction(action: DesktopAction) {\n  return [\n    \"desktop\",\n    action.action,\n    action.coordinate && `(${action.coordinate.join(\", \")})`,\n    action.text && JSON.stringify(action.text.slice(0, 200)),\n    action.scroll_direction && `${action.scroll_direction} ${action.scroll_amount ?? 3}`,\n    action.action === \"wait\" && `${action.duration ?? 1}s`,\n  ]\n    .filter(Boolean)\n    .join(\" \");\n}\n\n/** The xdotool (or sleep) command for one action; undefined for a plain screenshot. */\nexport function desktopInput(action: DesktopAction) {\n  const [x, y] = action.coordinate ?? [];\n  const at = action.coordinate ? `mousemove --sync ${x} ${y} ` : \"\";\n  switch (action.action) {\n    case \"screenshot\":\n      return undefined;\n    case \"left_click\":\n      return `xdotool ${at}click 1`;\n    case \"double_click\":\n      return `xdotool ${at}click --repeat 2 --delay 120 1`;\n    case \"right_click\":\n      return `xdotool ${at}click 3`;\n    case \"mouse_move\":\n      return `xdotool ${at.trim()}`;\n    case \"type\":\n      return `xdotool type --delay 12 -- ${quote(action.text ?? \"\")}`;\n    case \"key\":\n      return `xdotool key -- ${(action.text ?? \"\").trim().split(/\\s+/).map(quote).join(\" \")}`;\n    case \"scroll\": {\n      const button = { up: 4, down: 5, left: 6, right: 7 }[action.scroll_direction ?? \"down\"];\n      return `xdotool ${at}click --repeat ${action.scroll_amount ?? 3} ${button}`;\n    }\n    case \"wait\":\n      return `sleep ${action.duration ?? 1}`;\n  }\n}\n\n// One fixed path: actions on a computer are serialized by the service's lease.\nconst screenshotFile = \"/tmp/openmuse-screenshot.jpg\";\n// A VNC viewer that loses focus mid-shortcut (e.g. Alt+Tab in the user's browser)\n// leaves that modifier held, and every later click, key and wheel event then becomes\n// a shortcut. A filesystem-only resume\n// cold-boots the VM, which drops both and the DISPLAY set at creation.\nconst sessionScript = [\n  \"pgrep -x xfce4-session >/dev/null && exit 0\",\n  // Braces keep `&` on the app alone; a backgrounded `a || b` subshell would hold the output pipe.\n  `pgrep -x Xvfb >/dev/null || { setsid Xvfb ${display} -ac -screen 0 ${resolution.join(\"x\")}x24 -retro -dpi 96 -nolisten tcp -nolisten unix </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 & }`,\n  `for i in $(seq 50); do xdpyinfo -display ${display} >/dev/null 2>&1 && break; sleep 0.2; done`,\n  \"setsid startxfce4 </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &\",\n  \"for i in $(seq 100); do pgrep -x xfce4-session >/dev/null && pgrep -x xfdesktop >/dev/null && exit 0; sleep 0.3; done\",\n  \"exit 1\",\n].join(\"\\n\");\n\nlet filesScript: Promise<string> | undefined;\n// Source runs from apps/server/src; the built server runs from the repository root.\nconst loadFilesScript = () =>\n  (filesScript ??= readFile(new URL(\"../../computer/files.py\", import.meta.url), \"utf8\").catch(() =>\n    readFile(resolve(\"apps/computer/files.py\"), \"utf8\"),\n  ));\n\n// Runs each owner's computer in one E2B Desktop sandbox, matched by metadata.\n// Paused means stopped: /workspace lives on the sandbox disk and processes end.\n// Sandbox.connect resumes a paused box, so only start() and the first attach in a\n// process connect. Later operations reuse the cached handle, which fails on a\n// paused box instead of resuming it after a Stop.\n// One cached connection per sandbox. `url` is the stream this process started and\n// `streaming` the stream check or restart in flight, shared by concurrent viewers.\ninterface Handle {\n  box: DesktopBox;\n  url?: string;\n  streaming?: Promise<string>;\n}\nexport class E2BDesktopComputer {\n  private readonly handles = new Map<string, Handle>();\n  private readonly connecting = new Map<string, Promise<Handle>>();\n  constructor(\n    private readonly config: Config,\n    private readonly driver: DesktopDriver = e2bDesktopDriver(config),\n  ) {}\n  template() {\n    const template = this.config.computerE2bTemplate ?? \"desktop\";\n    if (!/^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_./-]{0,250}$/.test(template))\n      throw new AppError(\"COMPUTER_E2B_TEMPLATE is invalid\", 503);\n    return template;\n  }\n  private async control<T>(work: () => Promise<T>) {\n    try {\n      return await work();\n    } catch (error) {\n      if (error instanceof AppError) throw error;\n      throw new AppError(\n        \"E2B desktop operation failed. \"missing\" : info.state === \"running\" ? \"running\" : \"stopped\";\n  }\n  // The service lease serializes timeout updates across API and worker processes.\n  // Read E2B's current deadline so another process's refresh is never shortened.\n  private awake(info: DesktopInfo | undefined, ms: number) {\n    return Math.max(ms, info?.state === \"running\" ? info.endAt.getTime() - Date.now() : 0);\n  }\n  private forget(id: string) {\n    this.handles.delete(id);\n  }\n  async start(labels: Record<string, string>) {\n    const existing = await this.inspect(labels);\n    const id = existing\n      ? existing.sandboxId\n      : await this.control(() => this.driver.create(this.template(), labels));\n    const info = await this.inspect(labels); // re-check before start, including the shared deadline\n    if (existing?.state !== \"running\") this.forget(id);\n    const cached = this.handles.get(id);\n    const box =\n      cached?.box ?? (await this.control(() => this.driver.connect(id, this.awake(info, idleMs))));\n    if (cached) await this.control(() => box.keepAlive(this.awake(info, idleMs)));\n    if (!cached) this.handles.set(id, { box });\n    const script = await loadFilesScript();\n    await this.control(async () => {\n      if (\n        (await box.setup(\n          `mkdir -p /workspace /opt/openmuse && chown ${user}:${user} /workspace`,\n          \"root\",\n        )) !== 0\n      )\n        throw new AppError(\"Computer workspace could not be prepared\", 503);\n      await box.writeRootFile(\"/opt/openmuse/files.py\", script);\n      if ((await box.setup(sessionScript, user)) !== 0)\n        throw new AppError(\"Computer desktop session did not start\", 503);\n    });\n  }\n  async stop(labels: Record<string, string>) {\n    const info = await this.inspect(labels);\n    if (info?.state === \"running\") {\n      this.forget(info.sandboxId);\n      await this.control(() => this.driver.pause(info.sandboxId));\n    }\n  }\n  private async attach(\n    labels: Record<string, string>,\n    keepMs = idleMs,\n    firstConnect?: (work: () => Promise<Handle>) => Promise<Handle>,\n    verified?: DesktopInfo,\n  ) {\n    const info = verified ?? (await this.inspect(labels));\n    if (info?.state !== \"running\") throw stopped();\n    const id = info.sandboxId;\n    const cached = this.handles.get(id);\n    if (cached) {\n      try {\n        await cached.box.keepAlive(this.awake(info, keepMs));\n      } catch (error) {\n        const current = await this.inspect(labels);\n        if (current?.state !== \"running\") {\n          this.forget(id);\n          throw stopped();\n        }\n        await this.control(() => Promise.reject(error));\n      }\n      return cached;\n    }\n    // First use in this process, e.g. after an API restart. Start the computer to restore it.\",\n        409,\n      );\n    }\n    const handle: Handle = { box };\n    this.handles.set(id, handle);\n    return handle;\n  }\n  /** The stream URL, shared by every viewer: concurrent requests join one stream check\n   * or restart, so two viewers never race to restart it with different passwords. */\n  async desktopUrl(\n    labels: Record<string, string>,\n    firstConnect?: (work: () => Promise<Handle>) => Promise<Handle>,\n  ) {\n    const handle = await this.attach(labels, desktopIdleMs, firstConnect);\n    handle.streaming ??= this.control(() => handle.box.stream(handle.url))\n      .then((url) => (handle.url = url))\n      .finally(() => (handle.streaming = undefined));\n    return handle.streaming;\n  }\n  /** Perform one GUI action and return the screenshot taken after it. Every X11 call\n   * sets DISPLAY itself: the SDK's screenshot and input helpers rely on the DISPLAY\n   * that Sandbox.create puts in the sandbox env, and a resumed box no longer has it. */\n  async act(\n    labels: Record<string, string>,\n    action: DesktopAction,\n    beforeInput?: () => Promise<void>,\n  ) {\n    const { box } = await this.attach(labels);\n    const input = desktopInput(action);\n    let uncertain = false;\n    if (input) {\n      await beforeInput?.();\n      const script = [\n        ...(input.startsWith(\"xdotool \") ? [releaseModifiers] : []),\n        `${input} || exit 3`,\n      ].join(\"\\n\");\n      try {\n        // xdotool dispatches sequentially: a later failure can follow a delivered\n        // click or Return. A nonzero exit cannot confirm that no input occurred.\n        uncertain = (await box.setup(script, user)) !== 0;\n      } catch {\n        // A lost response cannot tell us whether xdotool delivered the input.\n        // Capture a screenshot if possible, but never replay the input here.\n        uncertain = true;\n      }\n    }\n    const warning = uncertain\n      ? \"The desktop input outcome is unknown: it may already have been performed. Inspect a fresh screenshot before repeating the action; do not automatically retry it.\"\n      : undefined;\n    const screen = { mimeType: \"image/jpeg\" as const, width: resolution[0], height: resolution[1] };\n    try {\n      const code = await this.control(() =>\n        box.setup(actionScript(input ? \"sleep 0.5\" : undefined), user),\n      );\n      if (code !== 0) throw new AppError(\"The desktop screenshot failed\", 502);\n      const image = await this.control(() => box.readFile(screenshotFile));\n      return { ...screen, image, uncertain, warning };\n    } catch (error) {\n      if (!input) throw error;\n      return {\n        ...screen,\n        image: new Uint8Array(),\n        uncertain,\n        warning:\n          warning ??\n          \"Action performed; the screenshot could not be taken. Take a screenshot before retrying the action.\",\n      };\n    }\n  }\n\n  /** Same contract as DockerRunner: command outcomes are results, never exceptions. */\n  async run(\n    labels: Record<string, string>,\n    command: string,\n    options: {\n      cwd?: string;\n      input?: string;\n      timeoutMs: number;\n      signal?: AbortSignal;\n      maxOutputBytes?: number;\n      propagateAttachError?: boolean;\n      verified?: DesktopInfo;\n    },\n  ): Promise<DockerResult> {\n    const output = computerOutput(options.maxOutputBytes);\n    const { result, limit, finish } = output;\n    let received = 0,\n      handle: DesktopHandle | undefined,\n      overflowed = false;\n    // Terminal output is also capped in the VM; this guards filesystem responses\n    // and any unexpected output outside that wrapper.\n    const capture = (write: (data: string | Buffer) => void) => (data: string) => {\n      write(data);\n      received += Buffer.byteLength(data);\n      if (received > limit + outputCeiling && !overflowed) {\n        overflowed = true;\n        void handle?.kill().catch(() => {});\n      }\n    };\n    const { CommandExitError, InvalidArgumentError, TimeoutError } = await sdk();\n    let box: DesktopBox;\n    try {\n      ({ box } = await this.attach(labels, idleMs, undefined, options.verified));\n    } catch (error) {\n      if (options.propagateAttachError) throw error;\n      // Nothing started, so this is a plain failure and the box keeps running.\n      result.stderr =\n        error instanceof AppError ? \"/workspace\",\n          envs: { DISPLAY: display },\n          stdin: options.input !== undefined,\n          timeoutMs: options.timeoutMs,\n          signal: options.signal,\n          onStdout: capture(output.stdout),\n          onStderr: capture(output.stderr),\n        });\n      } catch (error) {\n        if (error instanceof InvalidArgumentError) {\n          // A missing working directory is rejected before the command starts.\n          result.exitCode = 126;\n          output.stderr(\"The working directory does not exist.\");\n          return finish();\n        }\n        throw error;\n      }\n      if (options.signal?.aborted) abort();\n      if (options.input !== undefined && !result.interrupted) {\n        // Encode once: separate string slices can split a surrogate pair, and\n        // the SDK encodes each send independently, replacing both halves.\n        const input = Buffer.from(options.input, \"utf8\");\n        for (let i = 0; i < input.length; i += stdinChunk)\n          await handle.sendStdin(input.subarray(i, i + stdinChunk));\n        await handle.closeStdin();\n      }\n      result.exitCode = (await handle.wait()).exitCode;\n    } catch (error) {\n      if (error instanceof CommandExitError) result.exitCode = error.exitCode;\n      else if (error instanceof TimeoutError && error.message.includes(\"[deadline_exceeded]\"))\n        result.timedOut = true;\n      // Any other stream loss leaves the outcome unknown; the service stops the box.\n      else result.interrupted = true;\n    } finally {\n      options.signal?.removeEventListener(\"abort\", abort);\n    }\n    finish();\n    if (overflowed) result.stderr += \"\\nOutput exceeded the limit; the command was stopped.\";\n    return result;\n  }\n}\n","display_url":"https://github.com/CopilotKit/openmuse/blob/a4944f4c471d3dc93b8bfc060b5da309b5216ab2/apps/server/src/computer-e2b-desktop.ts"}}
