    {"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Action completed."}],"structuredContent":{"content":"---\nsummary: \"Multi-agent routing: agent boundaries, channel accounts, and bindings\"\ntitle: \"Multi-agent routing\"\nsidebarTitle: \"Multi-agent routing\"\nread_when: \"You want multiple agents with separate workspaces, auth, and sessions in one Gateway process.\"\nstatus: active\n---\n\nRun multiple _isolated_ agents in one Gateway process, each with its own workspace, state directory (`agentDir`), and SQLite-backed session history, plus multiple channel accounts (e.g. two WhatsApp numbers). Inbound messages route to the right agent through **bindings**.\n\nAn **agent** is the full per-persona scope: workspace files, auth profiles, model registry, and session store. A **binding** maps a channel account (a Slack workspace, a WhatsApp number, etc.) to one of those agents.\n\nFor a focused setup guide with account and conversation examples, see [Agent bindings](/concepts/agent-bindings).\n\n## What is one agent\n\nEach agent has its own:\n\n- **Workspace**: files, `AGENTS.md`/`SOUL.md`/`USER.md`, local notes, persona rules.\n- **State directory** (`agentDir`): auth profiles, model registry, per-agent config.\n- **Session store**: chat history and routing state in `<agentDir>/openclaw-agent.sqlite`.\n\nAuth profiles are per-agent, read from `<agentDir>/openclaw-agent.sqlite`. With the default layout, that resolves to:\n\n```text\n~/.openclaw/agents/<agentId>/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite\n```\n\n<Note>\n`sessions_history` provides bounded cross-session recall without secret-masking the retained text. It strips thinking-block signatures, tool-result payload details, `<relevant-memories>` markup, tool-call XML tags (`<tool_call>`, `<function_call>`, and their plural/downgraded forms), and MiniMax tool-call XML, then truncates and caps output by byte size.\n</Note>\n\n<Warning>\nNever reuse `agentDir` across agents — it causes auth/session state collisions. When a secondary agent's local OAuth credential is expired or its refresh fails, OpenClaw reads through to the auth-inheritance owner's credential for the same profile id and adopts whichever token is freshest, without copying the refresh token into the secondary agent's store. If you want a fully independent OAuth account, sign in from that agent. If you copy credentials manually, copy only portable static `api_key` or `token` profiles — OAuth refresh material is not portable by default (`copyToAgents` can opt a profile in explicitly).\n</Warning>\n\nSkills load from each agent workspace plus shared roots such as `~/.openclaw/skills`, then filter by the effective agent skill allowlist. Use `agents.defaults.skills` for a shared baseline and `agents.entries.*.skills` for a per-agent replacement (explicit entries replace the default, they do not merge). See [Skills: per-agent vs shared](/tools/skills#per-agent-vs-shared-skills) and [Skills: agent allowlists](/tools/skills#agent-allowlists).\n\nPlugin-owned storage follows that plugin's configuration; adding a second agent\ndoes not automatically split every global plugin store. For example, configure\n[Memory Wiki per-agent vaults](/concepts/multi-agent#per-agent-memory-wiki-vaults)\nwhen personas must not share compiled wiki knowledge.\n\n<Note>\n**Workspace note:** each agent's workspace is the **default cwd**, not a hard sandbox. Relative paths resolve inside the workspace, but absolute paths can reach other host locations unless sandboxing is enabled. See [Sandboxing](/gateway/sandboxing).\n</Note>\n\n## Paths\n\n| What                             | Default                                                                                | Override                                                                                    |\n| -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| Config                           | `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`                                                            | `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`                                                                      |\n| State dir                        | `~/.openclaw`                                                                          | `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`                                                                        |\n| Default agent's workspace        | `<stateDir>/workspace` (`~/.openclaw-<profile>/workspace` for a named profile)         | `agents.entries.*.workspace`, then `agents.defaults.workspace`, or `OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE_DIR` |\n| Other agents' workspace          | `<stateDir>/workspace-<agentId>` (or `<agents.defaults.workspace>/<agentId>` when set) | `agents.entries.*.workspace`                                                                |\n| Agent dir                        | `~/.openclaw/agents/<agentId>/agent`                                                   | `agents.entries.*.agentDir`                                                                 |\n| Sessions and transcripts         | `<agentDir>/openclaw-agent.sqlite`                                                     | `agents.entries.*.agentDir`                                                                 |\n| Legacy/archive session artifacts | `~/.openclaw/agents/<agentId>/sessions`                                                | —                                                                                           |\n\n### Single-agent mode (default)\n\nIf you configure nothing, OpenClaw runs one agent:\n\n- `agentId` defaults to `main`.\n- The main session key is `agent:main:main`.\n- Workspace defaults to `<stateDir>/workspace` (`~/.openclaw/workspace` for the default install and `~/.openclaw-<profile>/workspace` for a named profile).\n- State defaults to `~/.openclaw/agents/main/agent`.\n\n## Agent helper\n\nAdd a new isolated agent:\n\n```bash\nopenclaw agents add work\n```\n\nFlags: `--role <role>`, `--workspace <dir>`, `--model <id>`, `--agent-dir <dir>`, `--bind <channel[:accountId]>` (repeatable), `--non-interactive` (requires `--workspace` unless a role is supplied).\n\nAdd `bindings` to route inbound messages (the wizard offers to do this for you), then verify:\n\n```bash\nopenclaw agents list --bindings\n```\n\nIn the Control UI, **Agents** at `/agents` shows the roster, current work status,\nand recent chat previews, with **Open chat** opening each agent's main session.\nUse **Manage agents** to configure the roster at `/settings/agents`.\n\n**Settings → Agents** updates model choices when the Gateway\npublishes a new catalog. Refreshing choices preserves your selected model,\nfallbacks, and identity draft. If the read fails, the editor shows an error and\nkeeps the previous choices until a later update succeeds. Model and fallback\nedits keep their normal automatic save behavior.\n\n### Agent provenance\n\nOpenClaw records how each configured agent was created: `operator` for CLI,\nonboarding, and Gateway requests; `agent` when the system agent requested it;\nand `template` when a Template install added it. Agent-created entries also retain the\nrequesting agent id. A configured agent can ask OpenClaw to create another\nagent through its `openclaw` tool. The system agent files the typed operation,\nshows the requesting agent id to the operator, and creates the agent only after\noperator approval. Inspect the current creation hierarchy with:\n\n```bash\nopenclaw agents list --tree\n```\n\nDeleted creators remain historical provenance. If the creator is no longer in\nthe configured roster, its children appear at the root of the tree.\n\n## Team preset\n\nCreate a small team with written role contracts and directed delegation:\n\n```bash\nopenclaw agents team create --non-interactive\nopenclaw agent --agent coordinator --message \"Research the options and draft a recommendation.\"\n```\n\nThe preset creates a chief of staff (`coordinator`), researcher, writer, and\nreviewer, each with its own workspace and completed identity. The chief of staff remains the\nhuman's point of contact: it discovers matching specialists, assigns bounded\nwork, checks their artifacts, and reports a coherent result. Specialists return\nartifacts and evidence to the coordinator without delegating further. Their\noperating programs live in `AGENTS.md`, so they also apply in spawned sessions\nthat do not load `SOUL.md` or `IDENTITY.md`.\n\nThe bundled roles are [Template sources](/cli/templates), sharing the portable\n`CLAW.md` format for identity, the `SOUL.md` body, and declared workspace\nfiles. `agents add --role <role>` loads one of these sources. With the\nTemplates surface enabled, the equivalent source path from a source\ncheckout is `openclaw templates add docs/reference/templates/roles/<role>`; follow\nthe [Template preview and consent flow](/cli/templates#inspect-and-preview).\n\nYou can also create the chief of staff or the full team from the Control UI:\nchoose **New agent** in the sidebar or Agents home, then select the role or\nsmall-team recommendation in the custodian chat. Creation uses the same role\ntemplates and waits for your approval.\n\nThe relevant per-agent delegation fragment is:\n\n```json5 validate=false\n{\n  agents: {\n    entries: {\n      coordinator: {\n        subagents: {\n          allowAgents: [\"researcher\", \"writer\", \"reviewer\"],\n          delegationMode: \"prefer\",\n        },\n      },\n      researcher: { subagents: { allowAgents: [] } },\n      writer: { subagents: { allowAgents: [] } },\n      reviewer: { subagents: { allowAgents: [] } },\n    },\n  },\n}\n```\n\n`\"prefer\"` guides the coordinator to delegate suitable work; it is prompt guidance,\nnot a scheduler. `allowAgents` controls explicit spawn targets. The preset keeps\n`agents.defaults.subagents` and `tools.*` unchanged, so existing tool availability\nand access policy still apply. Role instructions require human approval before\nexternal sends, publication, purchases, deletion, or production changes.\nThese delegation settings remain team wiring in config. The role Templates will\ncarry them once the separate Template profile support lands.\n\nThe coordinator is an explicit target. Team creation\nsets `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId` to the coordinator only when that\nowner is unset; an existing owner is preserved and reported. In an explicit fleet,\nthis also designates the default for operations that support default-agent selection.\nExplicit targets and [routing bindings](/concepts/agent-bindings) take precedence.\n\nUse `--prefix <p>` to namespace all team ids, `--coordinator <id>` to rename the\ncoordinator, and `--workspace-root <dir>` to choose the parent directory for the\nseparate workspaces. All ids are checked for conflicts before creation. See\n[`agents team create`](/cli/agents#agents-team-create) for flags and examples,\nor use the team choice during [onboarding](/start/wizard#choose-one-agent-or-a-team).\n\n## Quick start\n\n<Steps>\n  <Step title=\"Create each agent workspace\">\n    ```bash\n    openclaw agents add coding\n    openclaw agents add social\n    ```\n\n    Each agent gets its own workspace with `SOUL.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and optional `USER.md`, plus a dedicated `agentDir` and session store. By default, those agent files live under `~/.openclaw/agents/<agentId>`.\n\n  </Step>\n  <Step title=\"Create channel accounts\">\n    Create one account per agent on your preferred channels:\n\n    - Discord: one bot per agent, enable Message Content Intent, copy each token.\n    - Telegram: one bot per agent via BotFather, copy each token.\n    - WhatsApp: link each phone number per account.\n\n    ```bash\n    openclaw channels login --channel whatsapp --account work\n    ```\n\n    See channel guides: [Discord](/channels/discord), [Telegram](/channels/telegram), [WhatsApp](/channels/whatsapp).\n\n  </Step>\n  <Step title=\"Add agents, accounts, and bindings\">\n    Add agents under `agents.entries`, channel accounts under `channels.<channel>.accounts`, and connect them with `bindings` (examples below).\n  </Step>\n  <Step title=\"Restart and verify\">\n    ```bash\n    openclaw gateway restart\n    openclaw agents list --bindings\n    openclaw channels status --probe\n    ```\n  </Step>\n</Steps>\n\n## Multiple agents, multiple personas\n\nEach configured `agentId` is a distinct persona boundary for core agent state:\n\n- Different accounts per channel (per `accountId`).\n- Different personalities (per-agent `AGENTS.md`/`SOUL.md`).\n- Separate auth and sessions, with cross-agent session access on by default and governed by `tools.agentToAgent`. Narrow session visibility with `tools.sessions.visibility`, restrict agent pairs with `tools.agentToAgent.allow`, or set `tools.agentToAgent.enabled: false` to block ordinary cross-agent access. Requester-owned native subagent and ACP child sessions stay reachable under `tree` or `all` visibility; use separate gateways for strict separation.\n\nThis lets multiple people share one Gateway while keeping core agent state separate.\n\n## Per-agent Memory Wiki vaults\n\nMemory Wiki uses one global vault by default. To keep a support agent's\ncompiled knowledge separate from a marketing agent's, set\n`plugins.entries.memory-wiki.config.vault.scope` to `agent`:\n\n```json5\n{\n  plugins: {\n    entries: {\n      \"memory-wiki\": {\n        enabled: true,\n        config: {\n          vault: {\n            scope: \"agent\",\n            path: \"~/.openclaw/wiki\",\n          },\n        },\n      },\n    },\n  },\n}\n```\n\nThe configured path is the parent directory. OpenClaw appends the normalized\nagent id, producing paths such as `~/.openclaw/wiki/support` and\n`~/.openclaw/wiki/marketing`. Agent-scoped CLI and Gateway operations require\nan explicit agent when multiple agents are configured. See\n[Memory Wiki per-agent vaults](/plugins/memory-wiki#per-agent-vaults) for bridge\nfiltering, migration, and trust-boundary details.\n\n## Cross-agent memory search\n\nThe QMD cross-agent search path was removed in v2026.8.1 along with the rest\nof the QMD backend. Builtin memory does not search\nanother agent's transcript corpus; each agent searches only its own configured\nmemory and eligible same-agent session sources. Put intentionally shared\nMarkdown in an explicit shared `memory.search.extraPaths` directory when the\nsame reference material should be indexed by multiple agents. For the full\nupgrade path, see [Migrating from QMD](/concepts/memory-builtin#migrating-from-qmd).\n\n## One WhatsApp number, multiple people (DM split)\n\nRoute different WhatsApp DMs to different agents on **one** WhatsApp account by matching sender E.164 (`+15551234567`) with `peer.kind: \"direct\"`. Replies still come from the same WhatsApp number — there is no per-agent sender identity.\n\n<Note>\nDirect chats collapse to the agent's main session key by default, so true isolation requires one agent per person.\n</Note>\n\n```json5\n{\n  agents: {\n    ownership: \"explicit\",\n    defaults: {\n      authInheritance: { agentId: \"alex\" },\n      systemAgent: { agentId: \"alex\" },\n    },\n    entries: {\n      alex: { workspace: \"~/.openclaw/workspace-alex\" },\n      mia: { workspace: \"~/.openclaw/workspace-mia\" },\n    },\n  },\n  bindings: [\n    {\n      agentId: \"alex\",\n      match: { channel: \"whatsapp\", peer: { kind: \"direct\", id: \"+15551230001\" } },\n    },\n    {\n      agentId: \"mia\",\n      match: { channel: \"whatsapp\", peer: { kind: \"direct\", id: \"+15551230002\" } },\n    },\n    { agentId: \"alex\", match: { channel: \"whatsapp\", accountId: \"*\" } },\n  ],\n  talk: { agentId: \"alex\" },\n  channels: {\n    whatsapp: {\n      dmPolicy: \"allowlist\",\n      allowFrom: [\"+15551230001\", \"+15551230002\"],\n    },\n  },\n}\n```\n\nDM access control (pairing/allowlist) is global per WhatsApp account, not per agent. For shared groups, bind the group to one agent or use [Broadcast groups](/channels/broadcast-groups).\n\n## Routing rules\n\nBindings follow a fixed order, and the most-specific match wins. See [Channel routing](/channels/channel-routing#routing-rules-how-an-agent-is-chosen) for the full tier order (exact peer, parent peer, peer wildcard, guild+roles, guild, team, account, channel, fallback owner). A few rules worth calling out here:\n\n- If multiple bindings match within the same tier, the first one in config order wins.\n- With more than one configured agent and no explicit owner, a message that matches no binding is not given to an arbitrary first-listed agent. A configured `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId`, retained legacy owner, or caller-supplied owner still catches that unbound traffic; only when no binding matches and no such fallback owner remains is the message left undispatched. A channel that keeps inbound messages for retry (Telegram, for example) may then deliver it later once a binding gives that account an owner, but delivery is not guaranteed. A retryable message is dead-lettered once it reaches both the attempt limit and the minimum age (24 hours by default), and a channel like Telegram can reject an ownerless account at startup, so rebinding delivers the message only while it is still queued and the account is running.\n- If a binding sets multiple match fields (for example `peer` + `guildId`), all specified fields must match (`AND` semantics).\n- A binding that omits `accountId` matches only the default account, not every account. Use `accountId: \"*\"` for a channel-wide fallback, or `accountId: \"<name>\"` for one account. Adding the same binding again with an explicit account id upgrades the existing channel-only binding instead of duplicating it.\n\nFor existing multi-agent configs, `openclaw doctor --fix` materializes legacy ambient default routing into channel-wide bindings plus explicit Custodian, Talk, and auth-inheritance owners where needed. It resolves legacy heartbeat enrollment before converting each monitor into an ordinary automation. It also removes retired default markers from single-agent configs; the sole agent still resolves implicitly. Runtime admission requires the current roster format, so run Doctor before starting a directly replaced binary with legacy markers. The normal update flow runs the candidate Doctor.\n\nFor a multi-agent roster defined directly in the main config file without a\nlegacy `default: true` marker, Doctor adds `agents.ownership: \"explicit\"` for\nboth keyed `agents.entries` and older `agents.list` rosters, including with\n`--fix --non-interactive`. Existing bindings and per-surface owners remain\nunchanged. Last-known-good recovery applies the same ownership stamp before\nvalidating and restoring a directly authored markerless roster.\nDoctor never promotes narrower conversation bindings to account-wide ownership.\nIt does not borrow ownership from another account or channel, choose between\nconflicting owners, or assign other unowned surfaces.\n\nDuring a legacy `agents.list` migration, unbound accounts keep\ntheir historical first-agent fallback as an explicit account binding, including\nwhen narrower conversation routes name other agents. Doctor\nrecords the binding alongside the ownership stamp. Both update-channel migration\nand manual Doctor require the original roster; if it is unavailable, Doctor reports\nthat reason and leaves the bindings unchanged. An account whose owner remains\nunresolved reports the required binding and stays blocked without automatic\nrestart attempts; other accounts and the Gateway continue serving.\n\nWhen migrating a legacy `agents.list` roster without a default marker, Doctor\nalso pins the first agent's inherited workspace to `agents.entries.<id>.workspace`. Its customized instructions\nand historical `memory/` notes remain in their original directory. Explicit\nworkspaces stay authoritative. If an earlier upgrade already left two edited\nworkspaces, select the intended per-agent workspace and reconcile their contents\nfrom your backups; Doctor does not merge directories.\n\n## Multiple accounts / phone numbers\n\nChannels that support multiple accounts (e.g. WhatsApp) use `accountId` to identify each login. Each `accountId` routes to its own agent, so one server can host multiple phone numbers without mixing sessions.\n\nSet `channels.<channel>.defaultAccount` to choose the account used when `accountId` is omitted. When unset, OpenClaw falls back to `default` if present, otherwise the first configured account id (sorted).\n\nChannels supporting multiple accounts: `discord`, `feishu`, `googlechat`, `imessage`, `irc`, `line`, `mattermost`, `matrix`, `msteams`, `nextcloud-talk`, `nostr`, `signal`, `slack`, `telegram`, `whatsapp`, `zalo`, `zalouser`.\n\n## Concepts\n\n- `agentId`: one \"brain\" (workspace, per-agent auth, per-agent session store).\n- `accountId`: one channel account instance (e.g. WhatsApp account `personal` vs `biz`).\n- `binding`: routes inbound messages to an `agentId` by `(channel, accountId, peer)`, and optionally guild/team ids.\n- Direct chats collapse to `agent:<agentId>:main` by default (the per-agent [main session](/concepts/main-session)).\n\n## Platform examples\n\nThese examples select channel and service owners explicitly. Channel bindings route\nmessages; `systemAgent`, each automation job, and `talk.agentId` select their own owners.\nWhen the previous owner was not `main`, `authInheritance.agentId` preserves the\nshared credential source independently of channel routing.\n\n<AccordionGroup>\n  <Accordion title=\"Discord bots per agent\">\n    Each Discord bot account maps to a unique `accountId`. Bind each account to an agent and keep allowlists per bot.\n\n    ```json5\n    {\n      agents: {\n        ownership: \"explicit\",\n        defaults: {\n          systemAgent: { agentId: \"main\" },\n        },\n        entries: {\n          main: { workspace: \"~/.openclaw/workspace-main\" },\n          coding: { workspace: \"~/.openclaw/workspace-coding\" },\n        },\n      },\n      bindings: [\n        { agentId: \"main\", match: { channel: \"discord\", accountId: \"default\" } },\n        { agentId: \"coding\", match: { channel: \"discord\", accountId: \"coding\" } },\n        { agentId: \"main\", match: { channel: \"discord\", accountId: \"*\" } },\n      ],\n      talk: { agentId: \"main\" },\n      channels: {\n        discord: {\n          groupPolicy: \"allowlist\",\n          accounts: {\n            default: {\n              token: \"DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN_MAIN\",\n              guilds: {\n                \"123456789012345678\": {\n                  channels: {\n                    \"222222222222222222\": { enabled: true, requireMention: false },\n                  },\n                },\n              },\n            },\n            coding: {\n              token: \"DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN_CODING\",\n              guilds: {\n                \"123456789012345678\": {\n                  channels: {\n                    \"333333333333333333\": { enabled: true, requireMention: false },\n                  },\n                },\n              },\n            },\n          },\n        },\n      },\n    }\n    ```\n\n    - Invite each bot to the guild and enable Message Content Intent.\n    - Tokens live in `channels.discord.accounts.<id>.token` (default account can use `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN`).\n\n  </Accordion>\n  <Accordion title=\"Telegram bots per agent\">\n    ```json5\n    {\n      agents: {\n        ownership: \"explicit\",\n        defaults: {\n          systemAgent: { agentId: \"main\" },\n        },\n        entries: {\n          main: { workspace: \"~/.openclaw/workspace-main\" },\n          alerts: { workspace: \"~/.openclaw/workspace-alerts\" },\n        },\n      },\n      bindings: [\n        { agentId: \"main\", match: { channel: \"telegram\", accountId: \"default\" } },\n        { agentId: \"alerts\", match: { channel: \"telegram\", accountId: \"alerts\" } },\n        { agentId: \"main\", match: { channel: \"telegram\", accountId: \"*\" } },\n      ],\n      talk: { agentId: \"main\" },\n      channels: {\n        telegram: {\n          accounts: {\n            default: {\n              botToken: \"123456:ABC...\",\n              dmPolicy: \"pairing\",\n            },\n            alerts: {\n              botToken: \"987654:XYZ...\",\n              dmPolicy: \"allowlist\",\n              allowFrom: [\"tg:123456789\"],\n            },\n          },\n        },\n      },\n    }\n    ```\n\n    - Create one bot per agent with BotFather and copy each token.\n    - Tokens live in `channels.telegram.accounts.<id>.botToken` (default account can use `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`).\n    - For multiple bots in the same Telegram group, invite each bot and mention the one that should answer.\n    - Disable BotFather Privacy Mode for each group bot (`/setprivacy` -> Disable), then remove and re-add the bot so Telegram applies the setting.\n    - Allow groups with `channels.telegram.groups`, or use `groupPolicy: \"open\"` only for trusted group deployments.\n    - Put sender user IDs in `groupAllowFrom`. Group and supergroup IDs belong in `channels.telegram.groups`, not `groupAllowFrom`.\n    - Bind by `accountId` so each bot routes to its own agent.\n\n  </Accordion>\n  <Accordion title=\"WhatsApp numbers per agent\">\n    Link each account before starting the gateway:\n\n    ```bash\n    openclaw channels login --channel whatsapp --account personal\n    openclaw channels login --channel whatsapp --account biz\n    ```\n\n    `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json` (JSON5):\n\n    ```json5\n    {\n      agents: {\n        ownership: \"explicit\",\n        defaults: {\n          authInheritance: { agentId: \"home\" },\n          systemAgent: { agentId: \"home\" },\n        },\n        entries: {\n          home: {\n            name: \"Home\",\n            workspace: \"~/.openclaw/workspace-home\",\n            agentDir: \"~/.openclaw/agents/home/agent\",\n          },\n          work: {\n            name: \"Work\",\n            workspace: \"~/.openclaw/workspace-work\",\n            agentDir: \"~/.openclaw/agents/work/agent\",\n          },\n        },\n      },\n\n      // Fixed routing order: first match wins (most-specific first).\n      bindings: [\n        { agentId: \"home\", match: { channel: \"whatsapp\", accountId: \"personal\" } },\n        { agentId: \"work\", match: { channel: \"whatsapp\", accountId: \"biz\" } },\n\n        // Optional per-peer override (example: send a specific group to work agent).\n        {\n          agentId: \"work\",\n          match: {\n            channel: \"whatsapp\",\n            accountId: \"personal\",\n            peer: { kind: \"group\", id: \"1203630...@g.us\" },\n          },\n        },\n        { agentId: \"home\", match: { channel: \"whatsapp\", accountId: \"*\" } },\n      ],\n      talk: { agentId: \"home\" },\n\n      // On by default. Omitted/empty `allow` permits every agent pair;\n      // list requester and target ids to restrict access, or set enabled: false to turn it off.\n      tools: {\n        agentToAgent: {\n          allow: [\"home\", \"work\"],\n        },\n      },\n\n      channels: {\n        whatsapp: {\n          accounts: {\n            personal: {\n              // Optional override. Default: ~/.openclaw/credentials/whatsapp/personal\n              // authDir: \"~/.openclaw/credentials/whatsapp/personal\",\n            },\n            biz: {\n              // Optional override. Default: ~/.openclaw/credentials/whatsapp/biz\n              // authDir: \"~/.openclaw/credentials/whatsapp/biz\",\n            },\n          },\n        },\n      },\n    }\n    ```\n\n  </Accordion>\n</AccordionGroup>\n\n## Common patterns\n\n<Tabs>\n  <Tab title=\"WhatsApp daily + Telegram deep work\">\n    Split by channel: route WhatsApp to a fast everyday agent and Telegram to an Opus agent.\n\n    ```json5\n    {\n      agents: {\n        ownership: \"explicit\",\n        defaults: {\n          authInheritance: { agentId: \"chat\" },\n          systemAgent: { agentId: \"chat\" },\n        },\n        entries: {\n          chat: {\n            name: \"Everyday\",\n            workspace: \"~/.openclaw/workspace-chat\",\n            model: \"anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6\",\n          },\n          opus: {\n            name: \"Deep Work\",\n            workspace: \"~/.openclaw/workspace-opus\",\n            model: \"anthropic/claude-opus-4-6\",\n          },\n        },\n      },\n      bindings: [\n        { agentId: \"chat\", match: { channel: \"whatsapp\", accountId: \"*\" } },\n        { agentId: \"opus\", match: { channel: \"telegram\", accountId: \"*\" } },\n      ],\n      talk: { agentId: \"chat\" },\n    }\n    ```\n\n    These examples use `accountId: \"*\"` so the bindings keep working if you add accounts later. To route a single DM/group to Opus while keeping the rest on chat, add a `match.peer` binding for that peer — peer matches always win over channel-wide rules.\n\n  </Tab>\n  <Tab title=\"Same channel, one peer to Opus\">\n    Keep WhatsApp on the fast agent, but route one DM to Opus:\n\n    ```json5\n    {\n      agents: {\n        ownership: \"explicit\",\n        defaults: {\n          authInheritance: { agentId: \"chat\" },\n          systemAgent: { agentId: \"chat\" },\n        },\n        entries: {\n          chat: {\n            name: \"Everyday\",\n            workspace: \"~/.openclaw/workspace-chat\",\n            model: \"anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6\",\n          },\n          opus: {\n            name: \"Deep Work\",\n            workspace: \"~/.openclaw/workspace-opus\",\n            model: \"anthropic/claude-opus-4-6\",\n          },\n        },\n      },\n      bindings: [\n        {\n          agentId: \"opus\",\n          match: { channel: \"whatsapp\", accountId: \"*\", peer: { kind: \"direct\", id: \"+15551234567\" } },\n        },\n        { agentId: \"chat\", match: { channel: \"whatsapp\", accountId: \"*\" } },\n      ],\n      talk: { agentId: \"chat\" },\n    }\n    ```\n\n    Peer bindings always win, so keep them above the channel-wide rule.\n\n  </Tab>\n  <Tab title=\"Family agent bound to a WhatsApp group\">\n    Bind a dedicated family agent to a single WhatsApp group, with mention gating and a tighter tool policy:\n\n    ```json5\n    {\n      agents: {\n        entries: {\n          family: {\n            name: \"Family\",\n            workspace: \"~/.openclaw/workspace-family\",\n            identity: { name: \"Family Bot\" },\n            groupChat: {\n              mentionPatterns: [\"@family\", \"@familybot\", \"@Family Bot\"],\n            },\n            sandbox: {\n              mode: \"all\",\n              scope: \"agent\",\n            },\n            tools: {\n              allow: [\n                \"exec\",\n                \"read\",\n                \"sessions_list\",\n                \"sessions_history\",\n                \"sessions_send\",\n                \"sessions_spawn\",\n                \"session_status\",\n              ],\n              deny: [\"write\", \"edit\", \"apply_patch\", \"browser\", \"canvas\", \"nodes\", \"cron\"],\n            },\n         …6869 chars truncated…, not a hard sandbox. Relative paths resolve inside the workspace, but absolute paths can reach other host locations unless sandboxing is enabled. See [Sandboxing](/gateway/sandboxing).\n</Note>\n\n## Paths\n\n| What                             | Default                                                                                | Override                                                                                    |\n| -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| Config                           | `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`                                                            | `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`                                                                      |\n| State dir                        | `~/.openclaw`                                                                          | `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`                                                                        |\n| Default agent's workspace        | `<stateDir>/workspace` (`~/.openclaw-<profile>/workspace` for a named profile)         | `agents.entries.*.workspace`, then `agents.defaults.workspace`, or `OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE_DIR` |\n| Other agents' workspace          | `<stateDir>/workspace-<agentId>` (or `<agents.defaults.workspace>/<agentId>` when set) | `agents.entries.*.workspace`                                                                |\n| Agent dir                        | `~/.openclaw/agents/<agentId>/agent`                                                   | `agents.entries.*.agentDir`                                                                 |\n| Sessions and transcripts         | `<agentDir>/openclaw-agent.sqlite`                                                     | `agents.entries.*.agentDir`                                                                 |\n| Legacy/archive session artifacts | `~/.openclaw/agents/<agentId>/sessions`                                                | —                                                                                           |\n\n### Single-agent mode (default)\n\nIf you configure nothing, OpenClaw runs one agent:\n\n- `agentId` defaults to `main`.\n- The main session key is `agent:main:main`.\n- Workspace defaults to `<stateDir>/workspace` (`~/.openclaw/workspace` for the default install and `~/.openclaw-<profile>/workspace` for a named profile).\n- State defaults to `~/.openclaw/agents/main/agent`.\n\n## Agent helper\n\nAdd a new isolated agent:\n\n```bash\nopenclaw agents add work\n```\n\nFlags: `--role <role>`, `--workspace <dir>`, `--model <id>`, `--agent-dir <dir>`, `--bind <channel[:accountId]>` (repeatable), `--non-interactive` (requires `--workspace` unless a role is supplied).\n\nAdd `bindings` to route inbound messages (the wizard offers to do this for you), then verify:\n\n```bash\nopenclaw agents list --bindings\n```\n\nIn the Control UI, **Agents** at `/agents` shows the roster, current work status,\nand recent chat previews, with **Open chat** opening each agent's main session.\nUse **Manage agents** to configure the roster at `/settings/agents`.\n\n**Settings → Agents** updates model choices when the Gateway\npublishes a new catalog. Refreshing choices preserves your selected model,\nfallbacks, and identity draft. If the read fails, the editor shows an error and\nkeeps the previous choices until a later update succeeds. Model and fallback\nedits keep their normal automatic save behavior.\n\n### Agent provenance\n\nOpenClaw records how each configured agent was created: `operator` for CLI,\nonboarding, and Gateway requests; `agent` when the system agent requested it;\nand `template` when a Template install added it. Agent-created entries also retain the\nrequesting agent id. A configured agent can ask OpenClaw to create another\nagent through its `openclaw` tool. The system agent files the typed operation,\nshows the requesting agent id to the operator, and creates the agent only after\noperator approval. Inspect the current creation hierarchy with:\n\n```bash\nopenclaw agents list --tree\n```\n\nDeleted creators remain historical provenance. If the creator is no longer in\nthe configured roster, its children appear at the root of the tree.\n\n## Team preset\n\nCreate a small team with written role contracts and directed delegation:\n\n```bash\nopenclaw agents team create --non-interactive\nopenclaw agent --agent coordinator --message \"Research the options and draft a recommendation.\"\n```\n\nThe preset creates a chief of staff (`coordinator`), researcher, writer, and\nreviewer, each with its own workspace and completed identity. The chief of staff remains the\nhuman's point of contact: it discovers matching specialists, assigns bounded\nwork, checks their artifacts, and reports a coherent result. Specialists return\nartifacts and evidence to the coordinator without delegating further. Their\noperating programs live in `AGENTS.md`, so they also apply in spawned sessions\nthat do not load `SOUL.md` or `IDENTITY.md`.\n\nThe bundled roles are [Template sources](/cli/templates), sharing the portable\n`CLAW.md` format for identity, the `SOUL.md` body, and declared workspace\nfiles. `agents add --role <role>` loads one of these sources. With the\nTemplates surface enabled, the equivalent source path from a source\ncheckout is `openclaw templates add docs/reference/templates/roles/<role>`; follow\nthe [Template preview and consent flow](/cli/templates#inspect-and-preview).\n\nYou can also create the chief of staff or the full team from the Control UI:\nchoose **New agent** in the sidebar or Agents home, then select the role or\nsmall-team recommendation in the custodian chat. Creation uses the same role\ntemplates and waits for your approval.\n\nThe relevant per-agent delegation fragment is:\n\n```json5 validate=false\n{\n  agents: {\n    entries: {\n      coordinator: {\n        subagents: {\n          allowAgents: [\"researcher\", \"writer\", \"reviewer\"],\n          delegationMode: \"prefer\",\n        },\n      },\n      researcher: { subagents: { allowAgents: [] } },\n      writer: { subagents: { allowAgents: [] } },\n      reviewer: { subagents: { allowAgents: [] } },\n    },\n  },\n}\n```\n\n`\"prefer\"` guides the coordinator to delegate suitable work; it is prompt guidance,\nnot a scheduler. `allowAgents` controls explicit spawn targets. The preset keeps\n`agents.defaults.subagents` and `tools.*` unchanged, so existing tool availability\nand access policy still apply. Role instructions require human approval before\nexternal sends, publication, purchases, deletion, or production changes.\nThese delegation settings remain team wiring in config. The role Templates will\ncarry them once the separate Template profile support lands.\n\nThe coordinator is an explicit target. Team creation\nsets `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId` to the coordinator only when that\nowner is unset; an existing owner is preserved and reported. In an explicit fleet,\nthis also designates the default for operations that support default-agent selection.\nExplicit targets and [routing bindings](/concepts/agent-bindings) take precedence.\n\nUse `--prefix <p>` to namespace all team ids, `--coordinator <id>` to rename the\ncoordinator, and `--workspace-root <dir>` to choose the parent directory for the\nseparate workspaces. All ids are checked for conflicts before creation. See\n[`agents team create`](/cli/agents#agents-team-create) for flags and examples,\nor use the team choice during [onboarding](/start/wizard#choose-one-agent-or-a-team).\n\n## Quick start\n\n<Steps>\n  <Step title=\"Create each agent workspace\">\n    ```bash\n    openclaw agents add coding\n    openclaw agents add social\n    ```\n\n    Each agent gets its own workspace with `SOUL.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and optional `USER.md`, plus a dedicated `agentDir` and session store. By default, those agent files live under `~/.openclaw/agents/<agentId>`.\n\n  </Step>\n  <Step title=\"Create channel accounts\">\n    Create one account per agent on your preferred channels:\n\n    - Discord: one bot per agent, enable Message Content Intent, copy each token.\n    - Telegram: one bot per agent via BotFather, copy each token.\n    - WhatsApp: link each phone number per account.\n\n    ```bash\n    openclaw channels login --channel whatsapp --account work\n    ```\n\n    See channel guides: [Discord](/channels/discord), [Telegram](/channels/telegram), [WhatsApp](/channels/whatsapp).\n\n  </Step>\n  <Step title=\"Add agents, accounts, and bindings\">\n    Add agents under `agents.entries`, channel accounts under `channels.<channel>.accounts`, and connect them with `bindings` (examples below).\n  </Step>\n  <Step title=\"Restart and verify\">\n    ```bash\n    openclaw gateway restart\n    openclaw agents list --bindings\n    openclaw channels status --probe\n    ```\n  </Step>\n</Steps>\n\n## Multiple agents, multiple personas\n\nEach configured `agentId` is a distinct persona boundary for core agent state:\n\n- Different accounts per channel (per `accountId`).\n- Different personalities (per-agent `AGENTS.md`/`SOUL.md`).\n- Separate auth and sessions, with cross-agent session access on by default and governed by `tools.agentToAgent`. Narrow session visibility with `tools.sessions.visibility`, restrict agent pairs with `tools.agentToAgent.allow`, or set `tools.agentToAgent.enabled: false` to block ordinary cross-agent access. Requester-owned native subagent and ACP child sessions stay reachable under `tree` or `all` visibility; use separate gateways for strict separation.\n\nThis lets multiple people share one Gateway while keeping core agent state separate.\n\n## Per-agent Memory Wiki vaults\n\nMemory Wiki uses one global vault by default. To keep a support agent's\ncompiled knowledge separate from a marketing agent's, set\n`plugins.entries.memory-wiki.config.vault.scope` to `agent`:\n\n```json5\n{\n  plugins: {\n    entries: {\n      \"memory-wiki\": {\n        enabled: true,\n        config: {\n          vault: {\n            scope: \"agent\",\n            path: \"~/.openclaw/wiki\",\n          },\n        },\n      },\n    },\n  },\n}\n```\n\nThe configured path is the parent directory. OpenClaw appends the normalized\nagent id, producing paths such as `~/.openclaw/wiki/support` and\n`~/.openclaw/wiki/marketing`. Agent-scoped CLI and Gateway operations require\nan explicit agent when multiple agents are configured. See\n[Memory Wiki per-agent vaults](/plugins/memory-wiki#per-agent-vaults) for bridge\nfiltering, migration, and trust-boundary details.\n\n## Cross-agent memory search\n\nThe QMD cross-agent search path was removed in v2026.8.1 along with the rest\nof the QMD backend. Builtin memory does not search\nanother agent's transcript corpus; each agent searches only its own configured\nmemory and eligible same-agent session sources. Put intentionally shared\nMarkdown in an explicit shared `memory.search.extraPaths` directory when the\nsame reference material should be indexed by multiple agents. For the full\nupgrade path, see [Migrating from QMD](/concepts/memory-builtin#migrating-from-qmd).\n\n## One WhatsApp number, multiple people (DM split)\n\nRoute different WhatsApp DMs to different agents on **one** WhatsApp account by matching sender E.164 (`+15551234567`) with `peer.kind: \"direct\"`. Replies still come from the same WhatsApp number — there is no per-agent sender identity.\n\n<Note>\nDirect chats collapse to the agent's main session key by default, so true isolation requires one agent per person.\n</Note>\n\n```json5\n{\n  agents: {\n    ownership: \"explicit\",\n    defaults: {\n      authInheritance: { agentId: \"alex\" },\n      systemAgent: { agentId: \"alex\" },\n    },\n    entries: {\n      alex: { workspace: \"~/.openclaw/workspace-alex\" },\n      mia: { workspace: \"~/.openclaw/workspace-mia\" },\n    },\n  },\n  bindings: [\n    {\n      agentId: \"alex\",\n      match: { channel: \"whatsapp\", peer: { kind: \"direct\", id: \"+15551230001\" } },\n    },\n    {\n      agentId: \"mia\",\n      match: { channel: \"whatsapp\", peer: { kind: \"direct\", id: \"+15551230002\" } },\n    },\n    { agentId: \"alex\", match: { channel: \"whatsapp\", accountId: \"*\" } },\n  ],\n  talk: { agentId: \"alex\" },\n  channels: {\n    whatsapp: {\n      dmPolicy: \"allowlist\",\n      allowFrom: [\"+15551230001\", \"+15551230002\"],\n    },\n  },\n}\n```\n\nDM access control (pairing/allowlist) is global per WhatsApp account, not per agent. For shared groups, bind the group to one agent or use [Broadcast groups](/channels/broadcast-groups).\n\n## Routing rules\n\nBindings follow a fixed order, and the most-specific match wins. See [Channel routing](/channels/channel-routing#routing-rules-how-an-agent-is-chosen) for the full tier order (exact peer, parent peer, peer wildcard, guild+roles, guild, team, account, channel, fallback owner). A few rules worth calling out here:\n\n- If multiple bindings match within the same tier, the first one in config order wins.\n- With more than one configured agent and no explicit owner, a message that matches no binding is not given to an arbitrary first-listed agent. A configured `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId`, retained legacy owner, or caller-supplied owner still catches that unbound traffic; only when no binding matches and no such fallback owner remains is the message left undispatched. A channel that keeps inbound messages for retry (Telegram, for example) may then deliver it later once a binding gives that account an owner, but delivery is not guaranteed. A retryable message is dead-lettered once it reaches both the attempt limit and the minimum age (24 hours by default), and a channel like Telegram can reject an ownerless account at startup, so rebinding delivers the message only while it is still queued and the account is running.\n- If a binding sets multiple match fields (for example `peer` + `guildId`), all specified fields must match (`AND` semantics).\n- A binding that omits `accountId` matches only the default account, not every account. Use `accountId: \"*\"` for a channel-wide fallback, or `accountId: \"<name>\"` for one account. Adding the same binding again with an explicit account id upgrades the existing channel-only binding instead of duplicating it.\n\nFor existing multi-agent configs, `openclaw doctor --fix` materializes legacy ambient default routing into channel-wide bindings plus explicit Custodian, Talk, and auth-inheritance owners where needed. It resolves legacy heartbeat enrollment before converting each monitor into an ordinary automation. It also removes retired default markers from single-agent configs; the sole agent still resolves implicitly. Runtime admission requires the current roster format, so run Doctor before starting a directly replaced binary with legacy markers. The normal update flow runs the candidate Doctor.\n\nFor a multi-agent roster defined directly in the main config file without a\nlegacy `default: true` marker, Doctor adds `agents.ownership: \"explicit\"` for\nboth keyed `agents.entries` and older `agents.list` rosters, including with\n`--fix --non-interactive`. Existing bindings and per-surface owners remain\nunchanged. Last-known-good recovery applies the same ownership stamp before\nvalidating and restoring a directly authored markerless roster.\nDoctor never promotes narrower conversation bindings to account-wide ownership.\nIt does not borrow ownership from another account or channel, choose between\nconflicting owners, or assign other unowned surfaces.\n\nDuring a legacy `agents.list` migration, unbound accounts keep\ntheir historical first-agent fallback as an explicit account binding, including\nwhen narrower conversation routes name other agents. Doctor\nrecords the binding alongside the ownership stamp. Both update-channel migration\nand manual Doctor require the original roster; if it is unavailable, Doctor reports\nthat reason and leaves the bindings unchanged. An account whose owner remains\nunresolved reports the required binding and stays blocked without automatic\nrestart attempts; other accounts and the Gateway continue serving.\n\nWhen migrating a legacy `agents.list` roster without a default marker, Doctor\nalso pins the first agent's inherited workspace to `agents.entries.<id>.workspace`. Its customized instructions\nand historical `memory/` notes remain in their original directory. Explicit\nworkspaces stay authoritative. If an earlier upgrade already left two edited\nworkspaces, select the intended per-agent workspace and reconcile their contents\nfrom your backups; Doctor does not merge directories.\n\n## Multiple accounts / phone numbers\n\nChannels that support multiple accounts (e.g. WhatsApp) use `accountId` to identify each login. Each `accountId` routes to its own agent, so one server can host multiple phone numbers without mixing sessions.\n\nSet `channels.<channel>.defaultAccount` to choose the account used when `accountId` is omitted. When unset, OpenClaw falls back to `default` if present, otherwise the first configured account id (sorted).\n\nChannels supporting multiple accounts: `discord`, `feishu`, `googlechat`, `imessage`, `irc`, `line`, `mattermost`, `matrix`, `msteams`, `nextcloud-talk`, `nostr`, `signal`, `slack`, `telegram`, `whatsapp`, `zalo`, `zalouser`.\n\n## Concepts\n\n- `agentId`: one \"brain\" (workspace, per-agent auth, per-agent session store).\n- `accountId`: one channel account instance (e.g. WhatsApp account `personal` vs `biz`).\n- `binding`: routes inbound messages to an `agentId` by `(channel, accountId, peer)`, and optionally guild/team ids.\n- Direct chats collapse to `agent:<agentId>:main` by default (the per-agent [main session](/concepts/main-session)).\n\n## Platform examples\n\nThese examples select channel and service owners explicitly. Channel bindings route\nmessages; `systemAgent`, each automation job, and `talk.agentId` select their own owners.\nWhen the previous owner was not `main`, `authInheritance.agentId` preserves the\nshared credential source independently of channel routing.\n\n<AccordionGroup>\n  <Accordion title=\"Discord bots per agent\">\n    Each Discord bot account maps to a unique `accountId`. Bind each account to an agent and keep allowlists per bot.\n\n    ```json5\n    {\n      agents: {\n        ownership: \"explicit\",\n        defaults: {\n          systemAgent: { agentId: \"main\" },\n        },\n        entries: {\n          main: { workspace: \"~/.openclaw/workspace-main\" },\n          coding: { workspace: \"~/.openclaw/workspace-coding\" },\n        },\n      },\n      bindings: [\n        { agentId: \"main\", match: { channel: \"discord\", accountId: \"default\" } },\n        { agentId: \"coding\", match: { channel: \"discord\", accountId: \"coding\" } },\n        { agentId: \"main\", match: { channel: \"discord\", accountId: \"*\" } },\n      ],\n      talk: { agentId: \"main\" },\n      channels: {\n        discord: {\n          groupPolicy: \"allowlist\",\n          accounts: {\n            default: {\n              token: \"DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN_MAIN\",\n              guilds: {\n                \"123456789012345678\": {\n                  channels: {\n                    \"222222222222222222\": { enabled: true, requireMention: false },\n                  },\n                },\n              },\n            },\n            coding: {\n              token: \"DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN_CODING\",\n              guilds: {\n                \"123456789012345678\": {\n                  channels: {\n                    \"333333333333333333\": { enabled: true, requireMention: false },\n                  },\n                },\n              },\n            },\n          },\n        },\n      },\n    }\n    ```\n\n    - Invite each bot to the guild and enable Message Content Intent.\n    - Tokens live in `channels.discord.accounts.<id>.token` (default account can use `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN`).\n\n  </Accordion>\n  <Accordion title=\"Telegram bots per agent\">\n    ```json5\n    {\n      agents: {\n        ownership: \"explicit\",\n        defaults: {\n          systemAgent: { agentId: \"main\" },\n        },\n        entries: {\n          main: { workspace: \"~/.openclaw/workspace-main\" },\n          alerts: { workspace: \"~/.openclaw/workspace-alerts\" },\n        },\n      },\n      bindings: [\n        { agentId: \"main\", match: { channel: \"telegram\", accountId: \"default\" } },\n        { agentId: \"alerts\", match: { channel: \"telegram\", accountId: \"alerts\" } },\n        { agentId: \"main\", match: { channel: \"telegram\", accountId: \"*\" } },\n      ],\n      talk: { agentId: \"main\" },\n      channels: {\n        telegram: {\n          accounts: {\n            default: {\n              botToken: \"123456:ABC...\",\n              dmPolicy: \"pairing\",\n            },\n            alerts: {\n              botToken: \"987654:XYZ...\",\n              dmPolicy: \"allowlist\",\n              allowFrom: [\"tg:123456789\"],\n            },\n          },\n        },\n      },\n    }\n    ```\n\n    - Create one bot per agent with BotFather and copy each token.\n    - Tokens live in `channels.telegram.accounts.<id>.botToken` (default account can use `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`).\n    - For multiple bots in the same Telegram group, invite each bot and mention the one that should answer.\n    - Disable BotFather Privacy Mode for each group bot (`/setprivacy` -> Disable), then remove and re-add the bot so Telegram applies the setting.\n    - Allow groups with `channels.telegram.groups`, or use `groupPolicy: \"open\"` only for trusted group deployments.\n    - Put sender user IDs in `groupAllowFrom`. Group and supergroup IDs belong in `channels.telegram.groups`, not `groupAllowFrom`.\n    - Bind by `accountId` so each bot routes to its own agent.\n\n  </Accordion>\n  <Accordion title=\"WhatsApp numbers per agent\">\n    Link each account before starting the gateway:\n\n    ```bash\n    openclaw channels login --channel whatsapp --account personal\n    openclaw channels login --channel whatsapp --account biz\n    ```\n\n    `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json` (JSON5):\n\n    ```json5\n    {\n      agents: {\n        ownership: \"explicit\",\n        defaults: {\n          authInheritance: { agentId: \"home\" },\n          systemAgent: { agentId: \"home\" },\n        },\n        entries: {\n          home: {\n            name: \"Home\",\n            workspace: \"~/.openclaw/workspace-home\",\n            agentDir: \"~/.openclaw/agents/home/agent\",\n          },\n          work: {\n            name: \"Work\",\n            workspace: \"~/.openclaw/workspace-work\",\n            agentDir: \"~/.openclaw/agents/work/agent\",\n          },\n        },\n      },\n\n      // Fixed routing order: first match wins (most-specific first).\n      bindings: [\n        { agentId: \"home\", match: { channel: \"whatsapp\", accountId: \"personal\" } },\n        { agentId: \"work\", match: { channel: \"whatsapp\", accountId: \"biz\" } },\n\n        // Optional per-peer override (example: send a specific group to work agent).\n        {\n          agentId: \"work\",\n          match: {\n            channel: \"whatsapp\",\n            accountId: \"personal\",\n            peer: { kind: \"group\", id: \"1203630...@g.us\" },\n          },\n        },\n        { agentId: \"home\", match: { channel: \"whatsapp\", accountId: \"*\" } },\n      ],\n      talk: { agentId: \"home\" },\n\n      // On by default. Omitted/empty `allow` permits every agent pair;\n      // list requester and target ids to restrict access, or set enabled: false to turn it off.\n      tools: {\n        agentToAgent: {\n          allow: [\"home\", \"work\"],\n        },\n      },\n\n      channels: {\n        whatsapp: {\n          accounts: {\n            personal: {\n              // Optional override. Default: ~/.openclaw/credentials/whatsapp/personal\n              // authDir: \"~/.openclaw/credentials/whatsapp/personal\",\n            },\n            biz: {\n              // Optional override. Default: ~/.openclaw/credentials/whatsapp/biz\n              // authDir: \"~/.openclaw/credentials/whatsapp/biz\",\n            },\n          },\n        },\n      },\n    }\n    ```\n\n  </Accordion>\n</AccordionGroup>\n\n## Common patterns\n\n<Tabs>\n  <Tab title=\"WhatsApp daily + Telegram deep work\">\n    Split by channel: route WhatsApp to a fast everyday agent and Telegram to an Opus agent.\n\n    ```json5\n    {\n      agents: {\n        ownership: \"explicit\",\n        defaults: {\n          authInheritance: { agentId: \"chat\" },\n          systemAgent: { agentId: \"chat\" },\n        },\n        entries: {\n          chat: {\n            name: \"Everyday\",\n            workspace: \"~/.openclaw/workspace-chat\",\n            model: \"anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6\",\n          },\n          opus: {\n            name: \"Deep Work\",\n            workspace: \"~/.openclaw/workspace-opus\",\n            model: \"anthropic/claude-opus-4-6\",\n          },\n        },\n      },\n      bindings: [\n        { agentId: \"chat\", match: { channel: \"whatsapp\", accountId: \"*\" } },\n        { agentId: \"opus\", match: { channel: \"telegram\", accountId: \"*\" } },\n      ],\n      talk: { agentId: \"chat\" },\n    }\n    ```\n\n    These examples use `accountId: \"*\"` so the bindings keep working if you add accounts later. To route a single DM/group to Opus while keeping the rest on chat, add a `match.peer` binding for that peer — peer matches always win over channel-wide rules.\n\n  </Tab>\n  <Tab title=\"Same channel, one peer to Opus\">\n    Keep WhatsApp on the fast agent, but route one DM to Opus:\n\n    ```json5\n    {\n      agents: {\n        ownership: \"explicit\",\n        defaults: {\n          authInheritance: { agentId: \"chat\" },\n          systemAgent: { agentId: \"chat\" },\n        },\n        entries: {\n          chat: {\n            name: \"Everyday\",\n            workspace: \"~/.openclaw/workspace-chat\",\n            model: \"anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6\",\n          },\n          opus: {\n            name: \"Deep Work\",\n            workspace: \"~/.openclaw/workspace-opus\",\n            model: \"anthropic/claude-opus-4-6\",\n          },\n        },\n      },\n      bindings: [\n        {\n          agentId: \"opus\",\n          match: { channel: \"whatsapp\", accountId: \"*\", peer: { kind: \"direct\", id: \"+15551234567\" } },\n        },\n        { agentId: \"chat\", match: { channel: \"whatsapp\", accountId: \"*\" } },\n      ],\n      talk: { agentId: \"chat\" },\n    }\n    ```\n\n    Peer bindings always win, so keep them above the channel-wide rule.\n\n  </Tab>\n  <Tab title=\"Family agent bound to a WhatsApp group\">\n    Bind a dedicated family agent to a single WhatsApp group, with mention gating and a tighter tool policy:\n\n    ```json5\n    {\n      agents: {\n        entries: {\n          family: {\n            name: \"Family\",\n            workspace: \"~/.openclaw/workspace-family\",\n            identity: { name: \"Family Bot\" },\n            groupChat: {\n              mentionPatterns: [\"@family\", \"@familybot\", \"@Family Bot\"],\n            },\n            sandbox: {\n              mode: \"all\",\n              scope: \"agent\",\n            },\n            tools: {\n              allow: [\n                \"exec\",\n                \"read\",\n                \"sessions_list\",\n                \"sessions_history\",\n                \"sessions_send\",\n                \"sessions_spawn\",\n                \"session_status\",\n              ],\n              deny: [\"write\", \"edit\", \"apply_patch\", \"browser\", \"canvas\", \"nodes\", \"cron\"],\n            },\n          },\n        },\n      },\n      bindings: [\n        {\n          agentId: \"family\",\n          match: {\n            channel: \"whatsapp\",\n            peer: { kind: \"group\", id: \"120363999999999999@g.us\" },\n          },\n        },\n      ],\n    }\n    ```\n\n    Tool allow/deny lists are **tools**, not skills. If a skill needs to run a binary, check that `exec` is allowed and the binary exists in the sandbox. For stricter gating, set `agents.entries.*.groupChat.mentionPatterns` and keep group allowlists enabled for the channel.\n\n  </Tab>\n</Tabs>\n\n## Per-agent sandbox and tool configuration\n\nEach agent can have its own sandbox and tool restrictions:\n\n```json5\n{\n  agents: {\n    ownership: \"explicit\",\n    defaults: {\n      authInheritance: { agentId: \"personal\" },\n      systemAgent: { agentId: \"personal\" },\n    },\n    entries: {\n      personal: {\n        workspace: \"~/.openclaw/workspace-personal\",\n        sandbox: {\n          mode: \"off\", // No sandbox for personal agent\n        },\n        // No tool restrictions - all tools available\n      },\n      family: {\n        workspace: \"~/.openclaw/workspace-family\",\n        sandbox: {\n          mode: \"all\", // Always sandboxed\n          scope: \"agent\", // One container per agent\n          docker: {\n            // Optional one-time setup after container creation\n            setupCommand: \"apt-get update && apt-get install -y git curl\",\n          },\n        },\n        tools: {\n          allow: [\"read\"], // Only read tool\n          deny: [\"exec\", \"write\", \"edit\", \"apply_patch\"], // Deny others\n        },\n      },\n    },\n  },\n  talk: { agentId: \"personal\" },\n}\n```\n\n<Note>\n`setupCommand` lives under `sandbox.docker` and runs once on container creation. Per-agent `sandbox.docker.*` overrides are ignored when the resolved scope is `\"shared\"`.\n</Note>\n\nThis gives you:\n\n- **Security isolation**: restrict tools for untrusted agents.\n- **Resource control**: sandbox specific agents while keeping others on host.\n- **Flexible policies**: different permissions per agent.\n\n<Note>\n`tools.elevated` has both a global gate (`tools.elevated.enabled`/`allowFrom`) and a per-agent gate (`agents.entries.*.tools.elevated.enabled`/`allowFrom`). The per-agent gate can only further restrict the global one — both must allow a sender for elevated commands to run. For group targeting, use `agents.entries.*.groupChat.mentionPatterns` so @mentions map cleanly to the intended agent.\n</Note>\n\nSee [Multi-agent sandbox and tools](/tools/multi-agent-sandbox-tools) for detailed examples.\n\n## Related\n\n- [ACP agents](/tools/acp-agents) — running external coding harnesses\n- [Channel routing](/channels/channel-routing) — how messages route to agents\n- [Parallel specialist lanes](/concepts/parallel-specialist-lanes) — splitting one job across role-scoped agents\n- [Presence](/concepts/presence) — agent presence and availability\n- [Session](/concepts/session) — session isolation and routing\n- [Sub-agents](/tools/subagents) — spawning background agent runs\n- [`openclaw agents`](/cli/agents) — create and inspect agents from the CLI\n","display_url":"https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/9312f263af4a3095d11f059e8637acf427701a96/docs/concepts/multi-agent.md"}},"isError":false}

## Assistant

I found a useful first slice to reuse: OpenMuse’s task worker already handles queued work, input/approval waits, and lease-based recovery. I’m testing that code in a small home-service spike, rather than copying its whole single-owner application.

The local npm registry is unreachable, so I’ll keep the smoke test model-free and use the available Node runtime. That can validate worker behavior and home persistence; live-model quality and the full phone connection will remain separate acceptance steps.

    import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
    import type { AgentTask, RunEvent } from "../../../../packages/domain/src/agent.ts";
    import type { Store } from "../db.ts";
    import { backgroundFailure } from "../log.ts";
    
    export class LostLeaseError extends Error {
      constructor() {
        super("Task was paused, cancelled or taken over by another worker");
        this.name = "LostLeaseError";
      }
    }
    export interface TaskContext {
      signal: AbortSignal;
      guard(): Promise<void>;
      checkpoint(patch: Partial<AgentTask>): Promise<AgentTask>;
      event(kind: RunEvent["kind"], title: string, detail?: string): Promise<void>;
    }
    export type TaskHandler = (
      owner: string,
      task: AgentTask,
      context: TaskContext,
    ) => Promise<Partial<AgentTask>>;
    export class TaskWorker {
      private timer?: ReturnType<typeof setInterval>;
      private ticking = false;
      private stopping = false;
      private active = new Map<string, AbortController>();
      // Tasks this worker has started and not yet settled, including ones still being claimed.
      private inFlight = new Set<string>();
      lastTickAt?: string;
      constructor(
        private readonly db: Store,
        private readonly execute: TaskHandler,
        private readonly options: {
          now?: () => number;
          leaseMs?: number;
          pollMs?: number;
          settled?: (owner: string, task: AgentTask) => Promise<void>;
        } = {},
      ) {}
      private now() {
        return this.options.now?.() ?? Date.now();
      }
      get running() {
        return Boolean(this.timer);
      }
      start() {
        if (this.timer) return;
        this.stopping = false;
        this.timer = setInterval(() => {
          // Timer callbacks cannot await runs; each run owns its durable error state.
          void this.tick().catch((error) => backgroundFailure("task worker tick", error));
        }, this.options.pollMs ?? 1000);
        void this.tick().catch((error) => backgroundFailure("initial task worker tick", error));
      }
      async stop() {
        this.stopping = true;
        if (this.timer) clearInterval(this.timer);
        this.timer = undefined;
        for (const controller of this.active.values()) controller.abort();
        while (this.inFlight.size || this.ticking) await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 10));
      }
      abort(taskId: string) {
        this.active.get(taskId)?.abort();
      }
      async tick() {
        if (this.stopping) return;
        if (this.running)
          await this.db.put("system", "worker-status", {
            id: "tasks",
            lastTickAt: new Date(this.now()).toISOString(),
          });
        if (this.ticking) return;
        this.ticking = true;
        this.lastTickAt = new Date(this.now()).toISOString();
        const started: Promise<void>[] = [];
        try {
          const records = await this.db.scan<AgentTask>("tasks");
          const due = records.filter(
            ({ value: t }) =>
              !this.inFlight.has(t.id) &&
              (t.status === "queued" ||
                (t.status === "scheduled" && Date.parse(t.nextRunAt ?? "") <= this.now()) ||
                (t.status === "running" && Date.parse(t.leaseUntil ?? "") <= this.now()) ||
                t.status === "waiting_approval"),
          );
          const eligible = [];
          for (const record of due) {
            if (this.inFlight.size + eligible.length >= 3) break;
            if (record.value.status === "waiting_approval") {
              const action = record.value.actionId
                ? await this.db.get<{ status: string; expiresAt?: string }>(
                    record.owner,
                    "actions",
                    record.value.actionId,
                  )
                : null;
              if (
                record.value.actionId &&
                action?.status === "awaiting_review" &&
                Date.parse(action.expiresAt ?? "") <= this.now()
              )
                await this.db.compareAndSwap(
                  record.owner,
                  "actions",
                  record.value.actionId,
                  { status: "awaiting_review", expiresAt: action.expiresAt },
                  { status: "expired" },
                );
              else if (action && ["awaiting_review", "executing"].includes(action.status)) continue;
            }
            eligible.push(record);
          }
          // Runs outlive the tick, so a long task does not stop later ticks from starting queued work.
          for (const { owner, value } of eligible) {
            this.inFlight.add(value.id);
            started.push(this.run(owner, value).finally(() => this.inFlight.delete(value.id)));
          }
        } finally {
          this.ticking = false;
        }
        await Promise.all(started);
      }
      private async run(owner: string, previous: AgentTask) {
        if (this.stopping) return;
        const leaseId = randomUUID(),
          leaseMs = this.options.leaseMs ?? 60000;
        const expected: Record<string, unknown> = {
          status: previous.status,
          leaseId: previous.leaseId ?? null,
        };
        if (previous.status === "running") expected.leaseUntil = previous.leaseUntil;
        let task = await this.db.compareAndSwap<AgentTask>(owner, "tasks", previous.id, expected, {
          status: "running",
          leaseId,
          leaseUntil: new Date(this.now() + leaseMs).toISOString(),
          updatedAt: new Date(this.now()).toISOString(),
          attempts: previous.attempts + 1,
        });
        if (!task) return;
        const controller = new AbortController();
        this.active.set(task.id, controller);
        const taskId = task.id;
        const guard = async () => {
          const latest = await this.db.get<AgentTask>(owner, "tasks", taskId);
          if (controller.signal.aborted || latest?.leaseId !== leaseId || latest.status !== "running")
            throw new LostLeaseError();
        };
        const checkpoint = async (patch: Partial<AgentTask>) => {
          if (controller.signal.aborted) throw new LostLeaseError();
          const next = await this.db.compareAndSwap<AgentTask>(
            owner,
            "tasks",
            taskId,
            { leaseId, status: "running" },
            { ...patch, updatedAt: new Date(this.now()).toISOString() },
          );
          if (!next) throw new LostLeaseError();
          task = next;
          return next;
        };
        const event = async (kind: RunEvent["kind"], title: string, detail = "") => {
          await guard();
          await this.db.put(owner, "run-events", {
            id: randomUUID(),
            taskId,
            date: new Date(this.now()).toISOString(),
            kind,
            title,
            detail,
          });
        };
        const startedAt = new Date(this.now()).toISOString();
        const heartbeat = setInterval(
          () => {
            void this.db
              .compareAndSwap(
                owner,
                "tasks",
                taskId,
                { leaseId, status: "running" },
                { leaseUntil: new Date(this.now() + leaseMs).toISOString() },
              )
              .then((value) => {
                if (!value) controller.abort();
              })
              .catch(() => controller.abort());
          },
          Math.max(10, Math.floor(leaseMs / 3)),
        );
        try {
          await this.db.put(owner, "runs", {
            id: leaseId,
            taskId,
            startedAt,
            status: "running",
          });
          const result = await this.execute(owner, task, {
            signal: controller.signal,
            guard,
            checkpoint,
            event,
          });
          await checkpoint({ ...result, leaseId: null, leaseUntil: null });
          await this.db.put(owner, "runs", {
            id: leaseId,
            taskId,
            startedAt,
            finishedAt: new Date(this.now()).toISOString(),
            status: result.status ?? task.status,
          });
        } catch (error) {
          if (error instanceof LostLeaseError || controller.signal.aborted) {
            await this.db.compareAndSwap(
              owner,
              "tasks",
              taskId,
              { leaseId, status: "running" },
              { status: "queued", leaseId: null, leaseUntil: null },
            );
          } else {
            const detail = error instanceof Error ? error.message : "Task execution failed";
            await event("error", "Task needs attention", detail).catch((error) =>
              backgroundFailure("record task error", error),
            );
            await this.db.compareAndSwap(
              owner,
              "tasks",
              taskId,
              { leaseId, status: "running" },
              {
                status: "failed",
                error: detail,
                leaseId: null,
                leaseUntil: null,
                updatedAt: new Date(this.now()).toISOString(),
              },
            );
          }
          await this.db.compareAndSwap(
            owner,
            "runs",
            leaseId,
            { status: "running" },
            {
              status: controller.signal.aborted ? "interrupted" : "failed",
              finishedAt: new Date(this.now()).toISOString(),
            },
          );
        } finally {
          clearInterval(heartbeat);
          this.active.delete(taskId);
        }
        const settled = await this.db.get<AgentTask>(owner, "tasks", taskId);
        if (settled && this.options.settled) await this.options.settled(owner, settled);
      }
    }

    Add: /Users/kgensupertramp/Desktop/me/infra-server/vendor/openmuse/apps/server/src/log.ts
    /** Background errors are visible without logging provider payloads or credential-bearing URLs. */
    export function backgroundFailure(phase: string, error: unknown) {
      const rawCode =
        error instanceof Error && "code" in error
          ? (error as Error & { code?: unknown }).code
          : undefined;
      const code =
        typeof rawCode === "string" && /^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,64}$/.test(rawCode) ? rawCode : undefined;
      console.error({
        timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
        context: { phase },
        error: error instanceof Error ? error.name : "Background operation failed",
        ...(code ? { code } : {}),
      });
    }
    
    /** Provider failures keep status and request ID for support, never bodies or credentials. */
    export function providerFailure(phase: string, error: unknown) {
      const detail = error && typeof error === "object" ? (error as Record<string, unknown>) : {};
      console.error({
        timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
        context: {
          phase,
          ...(typeof detail.status === "number" ? { status: detail.status } : {}),
          ...(typeof detail.requestId === "string" ? { requestId: detail.requestId } : {}),
        },
        error: error instanceof Error ? error.name : "Provider request failed",
      });
    }

    import { DatabaseSync } from 'node:sqlite';
    
    // Integration fixture only. This implements the small Store interface consumed
    // by the unchanged upstream worker using Node's built-in SQLite. It is not our
    // selected production schema, household authorization service, or model memory.
    export class HomeStore {
      constructor(path) {
        this.db = new DatabaseSync(path);
        this.db.exec(`
          PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL;
          PRAGMA busy_timeout=5000;
          CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS records (
            owner TEXT NOT NULL, kind TEXT NOT NULL, id TEXT NOT NULL,
            data TEXT NOT NULL, updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
            PRIMARY KEY(owner,kind,id)
          );
        `);
      }
      async get(owner, kind, id) {
        const row = this.db.prepare('SELECT data FROM records WHERE owner=? AND kind=? AND id=?')
          .get(owner, kind, id);
        return row ? JSON.parse(row.data) : null;
      }
      async put(owner, kind, value) {
        this.db.prepare(`INSERT INTO records VALUES(?,?,?,?,?)
          ON CONFLICT(owner,kind,id) DO UPDATE SET data=excluded.data,updated_at=excluded.updated_at`)
          .run(owner, kind, value.id, JSON.stringify(value), Date.now());
        return structuredClone(value);
      }
      async scan(kind) {
        return this.db.prepare('SELECT owner,data FROM records WHERE kind=? ORDER BY updated_at,id')
          .all(kind).map(row => ({ owner: row.owner, value: JSON.parse(row.data) }));
      }
      async list(owner, kind) {
        return this.db.prepare('SELECT data FROM records WHERE owner=? AND kind=? ORDER BY updated_at,id')
          .all(owner, kind).map(row => JSON.parse(row.data));
      }
      async compareAndSwap(owner, kind, id, expected, patch) {
        this.db.exec('BEGIN IMMEDIATE');
        try {
          const row = this.db.prepare('SELECT data FROM records WHERE owner=? AND kind=? AND id=?')
            .get(owner, kind, id);
          const value = row ? JSON.parse(row.data) : null;
          // Match the upstream worker's flat expected-field contract. JSON null is
          // significant: absent fields do not satisfy an expected null.
          const matches = value && Object.entries(expected).every(([key, wanted]) =>
            Object.hasOwn(value, key) && JSON.stringify(value[key]) === JSON.stringify(wanted));
          let next = null;
          if (matches) {
            next = { ...value, ...patch };
            this.db.prepare('UPDATE records SET data=?,updated_at=? WHERE owner=? AND kind=? AND id=?')
              .run(JSON.stringify(next), Date.now(), owner, kind, id);
          }
          this.db.exec('COMMIT');
          return next;
        } catch (error) {
          this.db.exec('ROLLBACK');
          throw error;
        }
      }
      async close() { this.db.close(); }
    }

    import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
    import { TaskWorker } from '../../vendor/openmuse/apps/server/src/engine/worker.ts';
    
    export { TaskWorker };
    
    // A trusted owner/session is supplied by the test harness, not authenticated
    // here. Real backend/home identity verification is a separate integration gate.
    export async function submit(store, owner, conversationId, prompt, input = {}) {
      const now = new Date().toISOString();
      const task = {
        id: randomUUID(), title: 'Synthetic integration task', prompt, kind: 'agent',
        status: 'queued', plan: [], evidence: [],
        input: { ...input, conversationId }, state: {},
        createdAt: now, updatedAt: now, attempts: 0,
        leaseId: null, leaseUntil: null, artifactIds: [],
      };
      await store.put(owner, 'tasks', task);
      return task;
    }
    
    export async function answer(store, owner, taskId, value) {
      if (typeof value !== 'string' || !value.trim()) throw new Error('Answer required');
      const task = await store.get(owner, 'tasks', taskId);
      if (!task) throw new Error('Task not found');
      return store.compareAndSwap(owner, 'tasks', taskId, { status: 'waiting_input' }, {
        status: 'queued', input: { ...task.input, answer: value }, question: null,
      });
    }
    
    // Deterministic fixture: deliberately no model calls, shell execution, browser,
    // external service, or simulated claim that this is a general-purpose agent.
    export async function fixtureHandler(store, owner, task, context) {
      if (task.input.needsAnswer && !task.input.answer) {
        await context.event('status', 'Waiting for an answer');
        return { status: 'waiting_input', question: 'Which format should I use?' };
      }
      await context.guard();
      const artifact = {
        id: randomUUID(), taskId: task.id, conversationId: task.input.conversationId,
        text: `${task.prompt}${task.input.answer ? ` (${task.input.answer})` : ''}`,
      };
      await store.put(owner, 'artifacts', artifact);
      await context.event('result', 'Synthetic artifact saved');
      return { status: 'succeeded', artifactIds: [artifact.id], result: artifact.text };
    }
    
    export function fixtureWorker(store, options = {}) {
      return new TaskWorker(store, (owner, task, context) =>
        fixtureHandler(store, owner, task, context), options);
    }
