    import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
    import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
    import { mkdtemp, rm } from 'node:fs/promises';
    import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
    import { join } from 'node:path';
    import test from 'node:test';
    import { HomeStore } from './home-store.mjs';
    import { submit, answer, fixtureWorker, TaskWorker } from './home-tasks.mjs';
    
    async function home(t) {
      const dir = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), 'me-home-test-'));
      const path = join(dir, 'home.sqlite');
      const stores = [];
      const open = () => {
        const store = new HomeStore(path);
        stores.push(store);
        return store;
      };
      t.after(async () => {
        for (const store of stores) {
          try { await store.close(); } catch { /* An explicit restart already closed it. */ }
        }
        await rm(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
      });
      return { path, open, store: open() };
    }
    
    test('one input wait allows other users/conversations to finish with scoped records', async t => {
      const { store } = await home(t);
      const waiting = await submit(store, 'alice', 'a-1', 'private draft', { needsAnswer: true });
      const a2 = await submit(store, 'alice', 'a-2', 'private report');
      const b1 = await submit(store, 'bob', 'b-1', 'private notes');
      const b2 = await submit(store, 'bob', 'b-2', 'private list');
      const worker = fixtureWorker(store);
      await worker.tick();
      await worker.tick();
      assert.equal((await store.get('alice', 'tasks', waiting.id)).status, 'waiting_input');
      for (const [owner, task] of [['alice', a2], ['bob', b1], ['bob', b2]]) {
        const saved = await store.get(owner, 'tasks', task.id);
        assert.equal(saved.status, 'succeeded');
        const artifact = await store.get(owner, 'artifacts', saved.artifactIds[0]);
        assert.equal(artifact.conversationId, task.input.conversationId);
        assert.equal(await store.get(owner === 'alice' ? 'bob' : 'alice', 'artifacts', artifact.id), null);
      }
      await assert.rejects(answer(store, 'bob', waiting.id, 'stolen answer'), /Task not found/);
      assert.equal((await store.list('alice', 'tasks')).length, 2);
      assert.equal((await store.list('bob', 'tasks')).length, 2);
    });
    
    test('waiting input and artifacts persist across closing/reopening the home database', async t => {
      const { store, open } = await home(t);
      const task = await submit(store, 'alice', 'chat-1', 'make a draft', { needsAnswer: true });
      await fixtureWorker(store).tick();
      await store.close();
      const restarted = open();
      assert.equal((await restarted.get('alice', 'tasks', task.id)).status, 'waiting_input');
      assert.ok(await answer(restarted, 'alice', task.id, 'MP4'));
      assert.equal(await answer(restarted, 'alice', task.id, 'duplicate answer'), null);
      await fixtureWorker(restarted).tick();
      const saved = await restarted.get('alice', 'tasks', task.id);
      assert.equal(saved.status, 'succeeded');
      assert.equal(saved.attempts, 2);
      assert.equal((await restarted.get('alice', 'artifacts', saved.artifactIds[0])).text,
        'make a draft (MP4)');
    });
    
    test('separate worker/store instances race for a single claim without duplicate execution', async t => {
      const { store, open } = await home(t);
      const task = await submit(store, 'alice', 'chat-1', 'run once');
      let executions = 0;
      const handler = async () => {
        executions++;
        await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 20));
        return { status: 'succeeded' };
      };
      await Promise.all([
        new TaskWorker(store, handler).tick(),
        new TaskWorker(open(), handler).tick(),
      ]);
      assert.equal(executions, 1);
      assert.equal((await store.get('alice', 'tasks', task.id)).attempts, 1);
    });
    
    test('an actual child-process crash leaves a checkpoint recoverable after lease expiry', async t => {
      const { store, path } = await home(t);
      const child = spawnSync(process.execPath, [
        '--experimental-transform-types', '--disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning',
        new URL('./crash-fixture.mjs', import.meta.url).pathname, path,
      ], { encoding: 'utf8', timeout: 15000 });
      assert.equal(child.status, 77, child.stderr);
      const id = child.stdout.trim();
      const interrupted = await store.get('alice', 'tasks', id);
      assert.equal(interrupted.status, 'running');
      assert.equal(interrupted.state.stage, 'checkpoint-before-crash');
      const worker = new TaskWorker(store, async (_owner, task) => {
        assert.equal(task.state.stage, 'checkpoint-before-crash');
        return { status: 'succeeded', result: 'recovered' };
      }, { now: () => Date.parse(interrupted.leaseUntil) + 1 });
      await worker.tick();
      const recovered = await store.get('alice', 'tasks', id);

      });
      await worker.tick();
      assert.deepEqual(executed, [['bob', other.id]]);
      await store.compareAndSwap('alice', 'actions', 'action-1', { status: 'awaiting_review' },
        { status: 'approved' });
      await worker.tick();
      assert.deepEqual(executed[1], ['alice', waiting.id]);

    test('cancellation aborts active work and rejects its late checkpoint/result', async t => {
      const { store } = await home(t);
      const task = await submit(store, 'alice', 'chat-1', 'cancel me');
      let entered;
      const started = new Promise(resolve => { entered = resolve; });
      let release;
      const gate = new Promise(resolve => { release = resolve; });
      const worker = new TaskWorker(store, async (_owner, _task, context) => {
        entered();
        await gate;
        await context.guard();
        return { status: 'succeeded' };
      });
      const running = worker.tick();
      await started;
      await store.compareAndSwap('alice', 'tasks', task.id, { status: 'running' },
        { status: 'cancelled', leaseId: null, leaseUntil: null });
      worker.abort(task.id);
      release();
      await running;
      assert.equal((await store.get('alice', 'tasks', task.id)).status, 'cancelled');
    });

      const { store } = await home(t);
      const task = await submit(store, 'alice', 'chat-1', 'pause me');

Extend, override, or replace any piece.\n\n**Principles:**\n\n- **Opinionated** — defaults tuned for long-horizon, multi-step work\n- **Extensible** — override or replace any piece without forking\n- **Model-agnostic** — works with any LLM that supports tool calling: frontier, open-weight, or local\n- **Production-ready** — built on LangGraph (streaming, persistence, checkpointing) with first-class tracing, evaluation, and deployment via LangSmith\n\n**Features include:**\n\n- **Sub-agents** — delegate tasks to agents with isolated context windows\n- **Filesystem** — read, write, edit, or search over pluggable local, sandboxed, or remote backends\n- **Context management** — summarize long threads and offload tool outputs to disk\n- **Shell access** — run commands in your sandbox of choice\n- **Persistent memory** — pluggable state and store backends for cross-session recall\n- **Human-in-the-loop** — approve, edit, or reject tool calls before they run\n- **Skills** — reusable behaviors the agent can load on demand\n- **Tools** — bring your own functions or any MCP server\n\nDeep Agents is available as a JavaScript/TypeScript library — see [deepagents.js](https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagentsjs).\n\n> [!NOTE]\n> **Deep Agents Code** — a pre-built coding agent in your terminal, similar to Claude Code or Cursor, powered by any LLM. Install with `curl -LsSf https://langch.in/dcode | bash`. See the [documentation](https://docs.langchain.com/deepagents-code) for the full feature set.\n\n## Quickstart\n\n```bash\nuv add deepagents\n```\n\n```python\nfrom deepagents import create_deep_agent\n\nagent = create_deep_agent(\n    model=\"openai:gpt-6-astra\",\n    system_prompt=\"You are a research assistant.\",\n)\nresult = agent.invoke({\"messages\": \"Research LangGraph and write a summary\"})\n```\n\nThe agent can plan, read/write files, and manage its own context. Add your own tools, swap models, customize prompts, configure sub-agents, and more. See the [documentation](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/deepagents/overview) for full details.\n\n> [!TIP]\n> For developing, debugging, and deploying AI agents and LLM applications, see [LangSmith](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/home).\n\n## FAQ\n\n### How is this different from LangGraph or LangChain?\n\nLangGraph is the graph runtime. LangChain's `create_agent` is a minimal agent harness on top of it. Deep Agents is a more opinionated harness on top of `create_agent` — same building blocks, but with filesystem, sub-agents, context management, and skills bundled in. For how the three relate, see the [LangChain ecosystem overview](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/concepts/products).\n\n### Does this work with open-weight or local models?\n\nYes. Any model that supports tool calling works — frontier APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google), open-weight models hosted on providers like Baseten or Fireworks, and self-hosted models via Ollama, vLLM, or llama.cpp. Use any [LangChain chat model](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/models).\n\n### Can I use this in production?\n\nYes! Deep Agents is built on LangGraph, designed for production agent deployments. Pair it with [LangSmith](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/home) for tracing, evaluation, and monitoring.     structured result: {"content":"# The agent computer\n\nOpenMuse combines a persistent browser with an optional Linux workspace for commands and files. The app and CopilotKit tools use the same authenticated computer service, so you can inspect what the agent ran and continue working with its results.\n\n## Start the Linux workspace\n\nThe API host needs Docker CLI access to a running Docker engine. Build the image from this repository:\n\n```sh\ndocker build -t openmuse-computer:local apps/computer\n```\n\nEnable it on the API and any separate task worker, then restart them:\n\n```dotenv\nCOMPUTER_ENABLED=true\nCOMPUTER_IMAGE=openmuse-computer:local\n```\n\nOpen **Computer → Terminal → Start computer**. Run `pwd` or `python3 --version`. Commands execute inside the Linux container with `/workspace` as their default working directory. Their output, exit code, and status appear in command history.\n\nIf Docker is unavailable, the app reports the connection error. There is no fallback that executes commands on the API host.\n\n### Optional isolated runtime on macOS\n\nColima is an open-source way to run Docker in a Linux VM. A separate profile keeps OpenMuse independent of other Docker workloads:\n\n```sh\nbrew install colima\ncolima start openmuse --cpus 2 --memory 3 --disk 12 --root-disk 12 \\\n  --vm-type vz --activate=false --mount none --ssh-config=false\nDOCKER_CONTEXT=colima-openmuse docker build -t openmuse-computer:local apps/computer\nDOCKER_CONTEXT=colima-openmuse COMPUTER_ENABLED=true pnpm dev\n```\n\nThe explicit context applies to that command and its child processes. It does not change the default Docker context. Stop this VM with `colima stop openmuse` when you no longer need it.\n\n### Run the computer on an E2B desktop (optional)\n\nInstead of Docker, each owner's computer can be an [E2B Desktop](https://e2b.dev/docs) sandbox: a Linux VM with an Xfce desktop, Firefox ESR, Google Chrome and LibreOffice. The API host needs no Docker engine, and you can watch and control the desktop from the app.\n\n```dotenv\nCOMPUTER_ENABLED=true\nCOMPUTER_PROVIDER=e2b-desktop\nE2B_API_KEY=e2b_...            # API and task worker only; never passed into the sandbox\nCOMPUTER_DEPLOYMENT_ID=...     # required and unique per install, e.g. `openssl rand -hex 12`\n# COMPUTER_E2B_TEMPLATE=desktop  # default; or a custom template built from it\n# E2B_DOMAIN=...                 # only for a non-default E2B cluster\n```\n\n`config.ts` never lets `.env` override a variable that is already set, so unset any `E2B_API_KEY`, `E2B_DOMAIN` or `E2B_API_URL` exported in your shell for another cluster before `pnpm dev`.\n\nOpen **Computer → Start computer**. A **Desktop** tab appears next to Browser, Terminal and Files while the computer runs. On web it embeds the live stream; on iOS and Android, **Open desktop** opens it in the system browser. The stream URL is returned only to the signed-in owner. Treat it as a bearer secret: anyone holding it gets full keyboard and mouse control until the next Stop. It carries a VNC password, and VNC authentication uses only its first 8 characters.\n\nHow it maps to the Docker contract:\n\n- **One sandbox per owner and deployment**, found by sandbox metadata across your whole E2B team. That is why `COMPUTER_DEPLOYMENT_ID` is required for this provider: two installs with the same id would share a sandbox. The app refuses to attach to a sandbox whose metadata, template or lifecycle it did not set.\n- **`/workspace` persists; processes do not.** Stop is a filesystem-only pause: every command and desktop app ends, and files are kept. After 15 idle minutes the sandbox pauses the same way. Commands and file operations count as activity; working inside the desktop does not. Opening the Desktop tab keeps the computer awake for 30 minutes, and the tab extends that every 2 minutes while it is visible, for up to an hour. A desktop opened in another browser tab or from the mobile app pauses about 30 minutes after the last refresh, so come back to the Desktop tab to extend it. Start resumes the sandbox and relaunches the desktop session. A paused sandbox is kept until you delete it; deleting it in the E2B dashboard deletes its `/workspace`.\n- **Commands** run as the template's `user` account (uid 1000) in `/workspace`, with the same 30-second limit, exit code 124 on timeout and 128 KB output cap. File operations reuse `apps/computer/files.py` over stdin.\n- **GUI apps from the terminal.** Commands run with `DISPLAY=:0`, so `firefox-esr https://copilotkit.ai >/dev/null 2>&1 &` opens on the desktop. Output is collected into temporary files, so a backgrounded app does not keep the command open, and it keeps running after the command returns. Discard a background app's output as shown: otherwise it keeps writing to a deleted temporary file for as long as it runs. A command whose output passes 32 MB is stopped.\n- **Command history is per provider.** Receipts from the Docker computer are not shown for the desktop, and the other way around.\n\n#### The agent sees and drives the desktop\n\nWith this provider the agent gets one more tool, `use_desktop`, in chat and in delegated tasks. It mirrors the shape of Anthropic's computer-use tool:\n\n| Action | Arguments | xdotool call |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `screenshot` | none | none |\n| `left_click`, `double_click`, `right_click` | optional `coordinate` `[x, y]` | `mousemove --sync x y click 1` (`--repeat 2`, button 3) |\n| `mouse_move` | `coordinate` | `mousemove --sync x y` |\n| `type` | `text` (up to 1000 characters) | `type --delay 12 -- text` |\n| `key` | `text`, xdotool key names or combos such as `Return` or `ctrl+l` | `key -- ...` |\n| `scroll` | `scroll_direction`, optional `scroll_amount` (default 3) and `coordinate` | wheel buttons 4 to 7 |\n| `wait` | optional `duration` in seconds (default 1, up to 10) | `sleep` |\n\n- **Every action returns a fresh screenshot.** Coordinates are pixels in that screenshot; the screen is 1280x800, so no scaling is involved. The screenshot is a JPEG (about 40 to 200 KB) taken with `scrot` half a second after the input.\n- **The image goes to the model as an image.** The tool returns TanStack AI content parts (a text part with the receipt, plus an image part). `@tanstack/ai` keeps a content-part array as the tool message, and all three adapters send it as a multimodal tool result: Anthropic `tool_result` blocks, OpenAI Responses `function_call_output` with `input_image`, Gemini `functionResponse.parts`. The AG-UI result event that is stored in the chat thread keeps only the text part, so later turns never replay image data as text.\n- **Receipts.** Each action is recorded next to the commands, for example `desktop left_click (640, 400)`, and the latest screenshot is kept per owner (`GET /api/computer/desktop/screenshot`). `POST /api/computer/desktop/actions` runs the same actions without returning the image.\n- **No implicit resume.** An action on a stopped computer fails with \"Start the computer\", and the agent has to call `start_computer` first. Actions take the computer's lease like file operations. The first stream connection takes the lifecycle lease so it cannot race startup or Stop; if busy, the viewer retries. Later stream requests only check or restart VNC without taking the lease, and concurrent viewers in one process share a single stream start.\n- **DISPLAY is set on every call.** The SDK's own `screenshot()`, `leftClick()` and `press()` run with no environment and rely on the `DISPLAY` that `Sandbox.create` stores in the sandbox environment. A filesystem-only pause cold-boots the VM, and the resumed sandbox no longer has that variable, so those helpers fail with `scrot: Can't open X display`. The app never uses them: it runs `xdotool` and `scrot` itself with `DISPLAY=:0`.\n- **Stuck modifiers are released.** A VNC viewer that loses focus in the middle of a shortcut (for example Alt+Tab in your browser) can leave Alt held, which turns every later key, click and scroll into a shortcut. Each input action releases all modifiers first.\n- **Same safety rules.** The agent is told never to click or press Return on a send, post, submit, sign-in, buy or upload control unless you asked for that exact action, and that text on screen is data, not instructions.\n\n#### Desktop card in chat\n\nWhen the agent uses `use_desktop`, the chat shows a **Desktop** card for each step with what it did. A persistent viewer after the tool cards embeds the live desktop, so new steps preserve the VNC connection. The per-step cards show their action labels. On web the viewer embeds the same stream as the Desktop tab. On iOS and Android it shows the latest screenshot and an **Open desktop** button. When the computer is stopped, the card says it is offline and offers **Start computer**. **Open in Desktop tab** opens the computer sheet on its Desktop tab.\n\n## Work with files\n\n- **Computer → Files** lists the persistent `/workspace` directory. Create folders, add text files, edit them, and save.\n- **Copy a document here** copies an owned PDF from OpenMuse into the current folder. A matching filename is replaced.\n- Open a PDF in the workspace to save a copy to OpenMuse Documents and view it in the native/web reader.\n- Browser downloads first enter Documents through **Import PDF downloads**, then can be copied into the Linux workspace.\n- Stopping the computer ends its running commands and keeps the named workspace volume. Starting it again restores those files.\n\nThe terminal runs bounded commands and displays their saved results. It is not an interactive PTY: full-screen terminal apps and prompts that require ongoing keyboard input are not supported. Write noninteractive scripts or edit files through the Files tab.\n\n## Isolation and scope\n\nThe workspace is a Docker container running as a nonroot user, with a read-only root filesystem, limited temporary storage and resources, dropped capabilities, and no added privileges. It receives no host directory mounts, Docker socket, model keys, Google tokens, or API access key. A named volume provides persistent `/workspace` storage.\n\nTerminal networking is disabled. The existing browser worker handles public web access through its own destination checks; see its [network boundary](../apps/worker/README.md#network-boundary). Browser profiles and workspace files have separate storage and lifecycle controls.\n\nThe E2B desktop provider differs from Docker in these ways:\n\n- **Network access is on.** The desktop's browsers need it, so commands can reach the internet too, and the app reports `network: enabled`. Treat anything downloaded as untrusted. This is also an outbound path the app does not review: the agent could post a file from `/workspace` or submit a form in Firefox, and only the app's own tools (`prepare_email`, `prepare_event`) require approval. The agent is told never to send, post or submit from the computer without an explicit request; that is an instruction, not an enforced boundary.\n- **Isolation comes from the VM.** Each owner gets a dedicated VM instead of a container on a shared kernel. Inside it there is no read-only root filesystem, capability drop or pids limit, and the template's `user` account has passwordless sudo.\n- **Every listening port is public.** Public traffic is enabled for the direct desktop iframe. Any service listening in the VM is reachable without app authentication at `https://<port>-<sandboxId>.e2b.app`; the sandbox ID is visible in the stream URL. Running `python3 -m http.server 8000` from `/workspace` exposes workspace files. Do not leave servers running, and stop temporary services as soon as they are no longer needed. The VNC password protects VNC only, not other services.\n- **Files live with E2B.** Workspace files are stored with E2B, outside your host. Your E2B plan's runtime limits apply.\n\nThe E2B API key stays on the API host.\n\nThis is a self-hosted, single-owner computer environment. Docker isolation does not provide a dedicated operating-system VM or a hostile-tenant security guarantee. The optional Colima VM provides the Linux host on macOS; the application still manages a Docker container within it.\n","title":"COMPUTER.md","modified_date":"2026-10-02T21:50:26Z","url":"https://github.com/CopilotKit/openmuse/blob/a4944f4c471d3dc93b8bfc060b5da309b5216ab2/docs/COMPUTER.md","display_url":"https://github.com/CopilotKit/openmuse/blob/a4944f4c471d3dc93b8bfc060b5da309b5216ab2/docs/COMPUTER.md","display_title":"COMPUTER.md","structuredContent":{"title":"COMPUTER.md","content":"# The agent computer\n\nOpenMuse combines a persistent browser with an optional Linux workspace for commands and files. The app and CopilotKit tools use the same authenticated computer service, so you can inspect what the agent ran and continue working with its results.\n\n## Start the Linux workspace\n\nThe API host needs Docker CLI access to a running Docker engine. Build the image from this repository:\n\n```sh\ndocker build -t openmuse-computer:local apps/computer\n```\n\nEnable it on the API and any separate task worker, then restart them:\n\n```dotenv\nCOMPUTER_ENABLED=true\nCOMPUTER_IMAGE=openmuse-computer:local\n```\n\nOpen **Computer → Terminal → Start computer**. Run `pwd` or `python3 --version`. Commands execute inside the Linux container with `/workspace` as their default working directory. Their output, exit code, and status appear in command history.\n\nIf Docker is unavailable, the app reports the connection error. There is no fallback that executes commands on the API host.\n\n### Optional isolated runtime on macOS\n\nColima is an open-source way to run Docker in a Linux VM. A separate profile keeps OpenMuse independent of other Docker workloads:\n\n```sh\nbrew install colima\ncolima start openmuse --cpus 2 --memory 3 --disk 12 --root-disk 12 \\\n  --vm-type vz --activate=false --mount none --ssh-config=false\nDOCKER_CONTEXT=colima-openmuse docker build -t openmuse-computer:local apps/computer\nDOCKER_CONTEXT=colima-openmuse COMPUTER_ENABLED=true pnpm dev\n```\n\nThe explicit context applies to that command and its child processes. It does not change the default Docker context. Stop this VM with `colima stop openmuse` when you no longer need it.\n\n### Run the computer on an E2B desktop (optional)\n\nInstead of Docker, each owner's computer can be an [E2B Desktop](https://e2b.dev/docs) sandbox: a Linux VM with an Xfce desktop, Firefox ESR, Google Chrome and LibreOffice. The API host needs no Docker engine, and you can watch and control the desktop from the app.\n\n```dotenv\nCOMPUTER_ENABLED=true\nCOMPUTER_PROVIDER=e2b-desktop\nE2B_API_KEY=e2b_...            # API and task worker only; never passed into the sandbox\nCOMPUTER_DEPLOYMENT_ID=...     # required and unique per install, e.g. `openssl rand -hex 12`\n# COMPUTER_E2B_TEMPLATE=desktop  # default; or a custom template built from it\n# E2B_DOMAIN=...                 # only for a non-default E2B cluster\n```\n\n`config.ts` never lets `.env` override a variable that is already set, so unset any `E2B_API_KEY`, `E2B_DOMAIN` or `E2B_API_URL` exported in your shell for another cluster before `pnpm dev`.\n\nOpen **Computer → Start computer**. A **Desktop** tab appears next to Browser, Terminal and Files while the computer runs. On web it embeds the live stream; on iOS and Android, **Open desktop** opens it in the system browser. The stream URL is returned only to the signed-in owner. Treat it as a bearer secret: anyone holding it gets full keyboard and mouse control until the next Stop. It carries a VNC password, and VNC authentication uses only its first 8 characters.\n\nHow it maps to the Docker contract:\n\n- **One sandbox per owner and deployment**, found by sandbox metadata across your whole E2B team. That is why `COMPUTER_DEPLOYMENT_ID` is required for this provider: two installs with the same id would share a sandbox. The app refuses to attach to a sandbox whose metadata, template or lifecycle it did not set.\n- **`/workspace` persists; processes do not.** Stop is a filesystem-only pause: every command and desktop app ends, and files are kept. After 15 idle minutes the sandbox pauses the same way. Commands and file operations count as activity; working inside the desktop does not. Opening the Desktop tab keeps the computer awake for 30 minutes, and the tab extends that every 2 minutes while it is visible, for up to an hour. A desktop opened in another browser tab or from the mobile app pauses about 30 minutes after the last refresh, so come back to the Desktop tab to extend it. Start resumes the sandbox and relaunches the desktop session. A paused sandbox is kept until you delete it; deleting it in the E2B dashboard deletes its `/workspace`.\n- **Commands** run as the template's `user` account (uid 1000) in `/workspace`, with the same 30-second limit, exit code 124 on timeout and 128 KB output cap. File operations reuse `apps/computer/files.py` over stdin.\n- **GUI apps from the terminal.** Commands run with `DISPLAY=:0`, so `firefox-esr https://copilotkit.ai >/dev/null 2>&1 &` opens on the desktop. Output is collected into temporary files, so a backgrounded app does not keep the command open, and it keeps running after the command returns. Discard a background app's output as shown: otherwise it keeps writing to a deleted temporary file for as long as it runs. A command whose output passes 32 MB is stopped.\n- **Command history is per provider.** Receipts from the Docker computer are not shown for the desktop, and the other way around.\n\n#### The agent sees and drives the desktop\n\nWith this provider the agent gets one more tool, `use_desktop`, in chat and in delegated tasks. It mirrors the shape of Anthropic's computer-use tool:\n\n| Action | Arguments | xdotool call |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `screenshot` | none | none |\n| `left_click`, `double_click`, `right_click` | optional `coordinate` `[x, y]` | `mousemove --sync x y click 1` (`--repeat 2`, button 3) |\n| `mouse_move` | `coordinate` | `mousemove --sync x y` |\n| `type` | `text` (up to 1000 characters) | `type --delay 12 -- text` |\n| `key` | `text`, xdotool key names or combos such as `Return` or `ctrl+l` | `key -- ...` |\n| `scroll` | `scroll_direction`, optional `scroll_amount` (default 3) and `coordinate` | wheel buttons 4 to 7 |\n| `wait` | optional `duration` in seconds (default 1, up to 10) | `sleep` |\n\n- **Every action returns a fresh screenshot.** Coordinates are pixels in that screenshot; the screen is 1280x800, so no scaling is involved. The screenshot is a JPEG (about 40 to 200 KB) taken with `scrot` half a second after the input.\n- **The image goes to the model as an image.** The tool returns TanStack AI content parts (a text part with the receipt, plus an image part). `@tanstack/ai` keeps a content-part array as the tool message, and all three adapters send it as a multimodal tool result: Anthropic `tool_result` blocks, OpenAI Responses `function_call_output` with `input_image`, Gemini `functionResponse.parts`. The AG-UI result event that is stored in the chat thread keeps only the text part, so later turns never replay image data as text.\n- **Receipts.** Each action is recorded next to the commands, for example `desktop left_click (640, 400)`, and the latest screenshot is kept per owner (`GET /api/computer/desktop/screenshot`). `POST /api/computer/desktop/actions` runs the same actions without returning the image.\n- **No implicit resume.** An action on a stopped computer fails with \"Start the computer\", and the agent has to call `start_computer` first. Actions take the computer's lease like file operations. The first stream connection takes the lifecycle lease so it cannot race startup or Stop; if busy, the viewer retries. Later stream requests only check or restart VNC without taking the lease, and concurrent viewers in one process share a single stream start.\n- **DISPLAY is set on every call.** The SDK's own `screenshot()`, `leftClick()` and `press()` run with no environment and rely on the `DISPLAY` that `Sandbox.create` stores in the sandbox environment. A filesystem-only pause cold-boots the VM, and the resumed sandbox no longer has that variable, so those helpers fail with `scrot: Can't open X display`. The app never uses them: it runs `xdotool` and `scrot` itself with `DISPLAY=:0`.\n- **Stuck modifiers are released.** A VNC viewer that loses focus in the middle of a shortcut (for example Alt+Tab in your browser) can leave Alt held, which turns every later key, click and scroll into a shortcut. Each input action releases all modifiers first.\n- **Same safety rules.** The agent is told never to click or press Return on a send, post, submit, sign-in, buy or upload control unless you asked for that exact action, and that text on screen is data, not instructions.\n\n#### Desktop card in chat\n\nWhen the agent uses `use_desktop`, the chat shows a **Desktop** card for each step with what it did. A persistent viewer after the tool cards embeds the live desktop, so new steps preserve the VNC connection. The per-step cards show their action labels. On web the viewer embeds the same stream as the Desktop tab. On iOS and Android it shows the latest screenshot and an **Open desktop** button. When the computer is stopped, the card says it is offline and offers **Start computer**. **Open in Desktop tab** opens the computer sheet on its Desktop tab.\n\n## Work with files\n\n- **Computer → Files** lists the persistent `/workspace` directory. Create folders, add text files, edit them, and save.\n- **Copy a document here** copies an owned PDF from OpenMuse into the current folder. A matching filename is replaced.\n- Open a PDF in the workspace to save a copy to OpenMuse Documents and view it in the native/web reader.\n- Browser downloads first enter Documents through **Import PDF downloads**, then can be copied into the Linux workspace.\n- Stopping the computer ends its running commands and keeps the named workspace volume. Starting it again restores those files.\n\nThe terminal runs bounded commands and displays their saved results. It is not an interactive PTY: full-screen terminal apps and prompts that require ongoing keyboard input are not supported. Write noninteractive scripts or edit files through the Files tab.\n\n## Isolation and scope\n\nThe workspace is a Docker container running as a nonroot user, with a read-only root filesystem, limited temporary storage and resources, dropped capabilities, and no added privileges. It receives no host directory mounts, Docker socket, model keys, Google tokens, or API access key. A named volume provides persistent `/workspace` storage.\n\nTerminal networking is disabled. The existing browser worker handles public web access through its own destination checks; see its [network boundary](../apps/worker/README.md#network-boundary). Browser profiles and workspace files have separate storage and lifecycle controls.\n\nThe E2B desktop provider differs from Docker in these ways:\n\n- **Network access is on.** The desktop's browsers need it, so commands can reach the internet too, and the app reports `network: enabled`. Treat anything downloaded as untrusted. This is also an outbound path the app does not review: the agent could post a file from `/workspace` or submit a form in Firefox, and only the app's own tools (`prepare_email`, `prepare_event`) require approval. The agent is told never to send, post or submit from the computer without an explicit request; that is an instruction, not an enforced boundary.\n- **Isolation comes from the VM.** Each owner gets a dedicated VM instead of a container on a shared kernel. Inside it there is no read-only root filesystem, capability drop or pids limit, and the template's `user` account has passwordless sudo.\n- **Every listening port is public.** Public traffic is enabled for the direct desktop iframe. Any service listening in the VM is reachable without app authentication at `https://<port>-<sandboxId>.e2b.app`; the sandbox ID is visible in the stream URL. Running `python3 -m http.server 8000` from `/workspace` exposes workspace files. Do not leave servers running, and stop temporary services as soon as they are no longer needed. The VNC password protects VNC only, not other services.\n- **Files live with E2B.** Workspace files are stored with E2B, outside your host. Your E2B plan's runtime limits apply.\n\nThe E2B API key stays on the API host.\n\nThis is a self-hosted, single-owner computer environment. Docker isolation does not provide a dedicated operating-system VM or a hostile-tenant security guarantee. The optional Colima VM provides the Linux host on macOS; the application still manages a Docker container within it.\n","display_url":"https://github.com/CopilotKit/openmuse/blob/a4944f4c471d3dc93b8bfc060b5da309b5216ab2/docs/COMPUTER.md"}}

    # Third-party source
    
    `vendor/openmuse` contains an unmodified subset of
    [CopilotKit/openmuse](https://github.com/CopilotKit/openmuse), pinned in
    `vendor/openmuse/upstream.json`. Its MIT license and copyright notice are retained
    in `vendor/openmuse/LICENSE`. These files retain their upstream license; Me's root
    Apache-2.0 license does not replace it.
    
    Imported files: `apps/server/src/engine/worker.ts`, `apps/server/src/log.ts`, and
    `LICENSE`. Local adapters/tests live outside the vendor directory. No upstream
    patches are applied. The worker's type-only imports are erased by Node's
    TypeScript transformation; this spike does not import the full upstream
    application or its dependencies. It is not a substitute for upstream's complete
    typecheck/build/test suite.
    
    Checksums detect local drift and identify reviewed source; they do not establish
    upstream authorship or prove source is safe. Updates run compatibility tests and
    are proposed for review. They are not automatically merged or installed on homes.

    #!/usr/bin/env python3
    """Verify/refresh a fixed, unpatched OpenMuse subset and prepare review bundles.
    
    Only these paths may change. Downloads finish before the checkout is mutated.
    Candidate code is tested in a separate read-only CI job from PR publishing.
    """
    import argparse
    import hashlib
    import json
    import os
    from pathlib import Path
    import re
    import shutil
    import sys
    import urllib.request
    
    ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
    VENDOR = Path('vendor/openmuse')
    REPOSITORY = 'CopilotKit/openmuse'
    FILES = ('LICENSE', 'apps/server/src/log.ts', 'apps/server/src/engine/worker.ts')
    SHA = re.compile(r'[0-9a-f]{40}')
    DIGEST = re.compile(r'[0-9a-f]{64}')
    LIMIT = 1024 * 1024
    
    
    def digest(data):
        return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
    
    
    def manifest_at(base):
        path = base / 'upstream.json'
        if path.is_symlink():
            raise ValueError('Manifest must be a regular file')
        manifest = json.loads(path.read_text())
        if manifest.get('schema') != 1 or manifest.get('repository') != REPOSITORY:
            raise ValueError('Unsupported manifest or upstream repository')
        if manifest.get('branch') != 'main' or not SHA.fullmatch(manifest.get('revision', '')):
            raise ValueError('Expected main and an immutable full commit SHA')
        if set(manifest.get('files', {})) != set(FILES):
            raise ValueError('Manifest paths differ from the fixed import allowlist')
        if not all(isinstance(v, str) and DIGEST.fullmatch(v) for v in manifest['files'].values()):
            raise ValueError('Invalid source digest')
        return manifest
    
    
    def verify_base(base):
        manifest = manifest_at(base)
        for name in FILES:
            path = base / name
            if path.is_symlink() or any(p.is_symlink() for p in path.parents):
                raise ValueError(f'Symlink in imported path: {name}')
            if digest(path.read_bytes()) != manifest['files'][name]:
                raise ValueError(f'Local drift or damaged source: {name}')
        return manifest
    
    
    def download(url):
        request = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={'User-Agent': 'mehomeai-upstream-check/1'})
        with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=25) as response:
            data = response.read(LIMIT + 1)
        if len(data) > LIMIT:
            raise ValueError('Upstream response exceeds size limit')
        data.decode('utf-8')
        return data
    
    
    def latest_revision(fetch=download):
        body = json.loads(fetch(f'https://api.github.com/repos/{REPOSITORY}/commits/main'))
        revision = body.get('sha', '')
        if not SHA.fullmatch(revision):
            raise ValueError('GitHub did not return an immutable commit SHA')
        return revision
    
    
    def write_snapshot(base, manifest, sources):
        for name, content in sources.items():
            path = base / name
            path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            path.write_bytes(content)
        (base / 'upstream.json').write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2) + '\n')
    
    
    def refresh(root, revision, fetch=download):
        current = verify_base(root / VENDOR)
        if not SHA.fullmatch(revision):
            raise ValueError('Supply a full lowercase commit SHA')
        if revision == current['revision']:
            return False, current
        sources = {name: fetch(f'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/{REPOSITORY}/{revision}/{name}')
                   for name in FILES}
        # A large/binary response cannot become part of the text-only import.
        for content in sources.values():
            if len(content) > LIMIT:
                raise ValueError('Upstream source exceeds size limit')
            content.decode('utf-8')
        if not sources['LICENSE'].strip():
            raise ValueError('Upstream license is empty')
        updated = {**current, 'revision': revision,
                   'files': {name: digest(content) for name, content in sources.items()}}
        write_snapshot(root / VENDOR, updated, sources)
        return True, updated
    
    
    def export_bundle(root, destination):
        base = root / VENDOR
        manifest = verify_base(base)
        if destination.exists():
            raise ValueError('Bundle destination must not already exist')
        sources = {name: (base / name).read_bytes() for name in FILES}
        destination.mkdir(parents=True)
        write_snapshot(destination, manifest, sources)
    
    
    def promote_bundle(root, source):
        verify_base(root / VENDOR)
        if source.is_symlink() or any(path.is_symlink() for path in source.rglob('*')):
            raise ValueError('Bundle must not contain symlinks')
        actual = {p.relative_to(source).as_posix() for p in source.rglob('*') if p.is_file()}
        if actual != set(FILES) | {'upstream.json'}:
            raise ValueError('Bundle contains unexpected or missing paths')
        manifest = verify_base(source)
        sources = {name: (source / name).read_bytes() for name in FILES}
        write_snapshot(root / VENDOR, manifest, sources)
        return manifest
    
    
    def main():
        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
        parser.add_argument('command', choices=['verify', 'check', 'update', 'promote'])
        parser.add_argument('--revision', help='Full immutable SHA; omitted means check main')
        parser.add_argument('--bundle', type=Path, help='Export directory, or input for promote')
        args = parser.parse_args()
        if args.command == 'promote':
            if not args.bundle:
                parser.error('promote requires --bundle')
            manifest = promote_bundle(ROOT, args.bundle)
            print(f"Promoted fixed-path candidate {manifest['revision']}")
            return
        current = verify_base(ROOT / VENDOR)
        if args.command == 'verify':
            print(f"Source hashes verified: {REPOSITORY}@{current['revision']}")
            return
        revision = args.revision or latest_revision()
        if not SHA.fullmatch(revision):
            raise ValueError('Invalid revision')
        changed = revision != current['revision']
        if args.command == 'update':
            changed, _ = refresh(ROOT, revision)
            if args.bundle and changed:
                export_bundle(ROOT, args.bundle)
        print(json.dumps({'current': current['revision'], 'candidate': revision, 'changed': changed}))
        if output := os.environ.get('GITHUB_OUTPUT'):
            with open(output, 'a') as handle:
                handle.write(f'changed={str(changed).lower()}\nrevision={revision}\n')
    
    
    if __name__ == '__main__':
        try:
            main()
        except (ValueError, OSError, KeyError, json.JSONDecodeError) as error:
            print(f'Upstream check failed: {error}', file=sys.stderr)
            sys.exit(1)

    name: Evaluate OpenMuse upstream update
    
    on:
      schedule:
        - cron: '17 9 * * 1'
      workflow_dispatch:
        inputs:
          revision:
            description: 'Optional full upstream commit SHA; empty checks main'
            required: false
            type: string
    
    permissions:
      contents: read
    
    concurrency:
      group: upstream-openmuse
      cancel-in-progress: false
    
    jobs:
      candidate:
        name: Test upstream without publishing credentials
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 10
        outputs:
          changed: ${{ steps.update.outputs.changed }}
          revision: ${{ steps.update.outputs.revision }}
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
            with:
              persist-credentials: false
          - uses: actions/setup-node@249970729cb0ef3589644e2896645e5dc5ba9c38 # v6
            with:
              node-version: 24.18.0
          - name: Verify updater before downloading code
            run: python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py' -v
          - name: Prepare fixed-path upstream candidate
            id: update
            env:
              REQUESTED_REVISION: ${{ inputs.revision }}
            shell: bash
            run: |
              args=()
              if [ -n "$REQUESTED_REVISION" ]; then
                args+=(--revision "$REQUESTED_REVISION")
              fi
              python3 scripts/upstream.py update "${args[@]}" --bundle "$RUNNER_TEMP/upstream-candidate"
          - name: Verify and test candidate
            if: steps.update.outputs.changed == 'true'
            run: |
              python3 scripts/upstream.py verify
              npm run test:spike
              npm run demo:spike
          - name: Save only candidate source data
            if: steps.update.outputs.changed == 'true'
            uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4
            with:
              name: openmuse-candidate
              path: ${{ runner.temp }}/upstream-candidate
              if-no-files-found: error
              retention-days: 7
    
      propose:
        name: Open a review PR without executing candidate code
        needs: candidate
        if: needs.candidate.outputs.changed == 'true'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 5
        permissions:
          contents: write
          pull-requests: write
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
            with:
              persist-credentials: false
          - uses: actions/download-artifact@634f93cb2916e3fdff6788551b99b062d0335ce0 # v5
            with:
              name: openmuse-candidate
              path: ${{ runner.temp }}/upstream-candidate
          - name: Validate candidate data with the approved updater
            run: python3 scripts/upstream.py promote --bundle "$RUNNER_TEMP/upstream-candidate"
          - name: Propose a source-pin update
            env:
              GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
              REVISION: ${{ needs.candidate.outputs.revision }}
            shell: bash
            run: |
              branch="upstream/openmuse-$REVISION"
              if gh pr view "$branch" --json number >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo 'An update PR already exists for this revision.'
                exit 0
              fi
              git config user.name 'github-actions[bot]'
              git config user.email '41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com'
              git checkout -b "$branch"
              git add -- vendor/openmuse
              git diff --cached --quiet && exit 0
              git commit -m "chore: evaluate OpenMuse $REVISION"
              gh auth setup-git
              git push origin "$branch"
              cat > "$RUNNER_TEMP/upstream-pr.md" <<'BODY'
              Refresh the fixed, unpatched OpenMuse worker subset and its source hashes.
    
              The candidate passed the model-free home integration suite and demonstration
              before publishing. Candidate tests run separately from this write-token job.
    
              Review the source/license diff, household isolation implications, missing
              imports, and API changes. These tests do not cover a live model, browser,
              phone/backend transport, production authorization, or upstream's full build.
    
              This PR does not merge or deploy automatically. GitHub-token-created PRs
              may not trigger push/PR workflows: manually dispatch CI on this branch
              or use a dedicated GitHub App if independently triggered PR checks are required.
              BODY
              printf '\nCandidate run: %s/%s/actions/runs/%s\n' "$GITHUB_SERVER_URL" "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" >> "$RUNNER_TEMP/upstream-pr.md"
              gh pr create --base "$GITHUB_BASE_REF" --head "$branch" --title "chore: evaluate OpenMuse $REVISION" --body-file "$RUNNER_TEMP/upstream-pr.md"

    import copy
    import importlib.util
    import json
    from pathlib import Path
    import tempfile
    import unittest
    
    SPEC = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('upstream', Path(__file__).with_name('upstream.py'))
    upstream = importlib.util.module_from_spec(SPEC)
    SPEC.loader.exec_module(upstream)
    
    
    class UpstreamTests(unittest.TestCase):
        def setUp(self):
            self.temp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
            self.addCleanup(self.temp.cleanup)
            self.root = Path(self.temp.name) / 'repo'
            self.base = self.root / upstream.VENDOR
            self.base.mkdir(parents=True)
            self.sources = {name: f'synthetic source: {name}\n'.encode() for name in upstream.FILES}
            self.manifest = {
                'schema': 1, 'repository': upstream.REPOSITORY, 'branch': 'main',
                'revision': 'a' * 40,
                'files': {name: upstream.digest(data) for name, data in self.sources.items()},
            }
            upstream.write_snapshot(self.base, self.manifest, self.sources)
    
        def test_verify_and_detect_local_patch(self):
            upstream.verify_base(self.base)
            (self.base / 'LICENSE').write_text('changed')
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, 'Local drift'):
                upstream.verify_base(self.base)
    
        def test_reject_path_expansion_and_other_repository(self):
            for field, value in [('repository', 'other/repo'), ('files', {'../../outside': '0' * 64})]:
                manifest = copy.deepcopy(self.manifest)
                manifest[field] = value
                (self.base / 'upstream.json').write_text(json.dumps(manifest))
                with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                    upstream.manifest_at(self.base)
    
        def test_reject_branch_name_instead_of_immutable_revision(self):
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, 'full lowercase'):
                upstream.refresh(self.root, 'main')
    
        def test_refuse_to_overwrite_local_changes_before_network_call(self):
            (self.base / 'LICENSE').write_text('local patch')
            calls = []
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                upstream.refresh(self.root, 'b' * 40, lambda url: calls.append(url))
            self.assertEqual(calls, [])
    
        def test_failed_download_does_not_partially_update_snapshot(self):
            def fetch(url):
                if url.endswith('log.ts'):
                    raise OSError('synthetic network failure')
                return b'new upstream content\n'
            with self.assertRaises(OSError):
                upstream.refresh(self.root, 'b' * 40, fetch)
            self.assertEqual(upstream.verify_base(self.base), self.manifest)
    
        def test_candidate_bundle_promotion_preserves_exact_source_bytes(self):
            candidate = Path(self.temp.name) / 'candidate'
            data = b'updated synthetic source\n'
            changed, manifest = upstream.refresh(self.root, 'b' * 40, lambda _url: data)
            self.assertTrue(changed)
            upstream.export_bundle(self.root, candidate)
            # Reconstruct the approved baseline to exercise the separate publishing job.
            upstream.write_snapshot(self.base, self.manifest, self.sources)
            upstream.promote_bundle(self.root, candidate)
            self.assertEqual(upstream.verify_base(self.base), manifest)
            self.assertEqual((self.base / 'apps/server/src/engine/worker.ts').read_bytes(), data)
    
        def test_publishing_rejects_extra_files_and_tampered_bundles(self):
            candidate = Path(self.temp.name) / 'candidate'
            upstream.export_bundle(self.root, candidate)
            extra = candidate / 'workflow.yml'
            extra.write_text('not permitted')
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, 'unexpected'):
                upstream.promote_bundle(self.root, candidate)
            extra.unlink()
            (candidate / 'LICENSE').write_text('tampered')
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, 'Local drift'):
                upstream.promote_bundle(self.root, candidate)
            self.assertEqual(upstream.verify_base(self.base), self.manifest)
    
        def test_publishing_rejects_symlinks(self):
            candidate = Path(self.temp.name) / 'candidate'
            upstream.export_bundle(self.root, candidate)
            license_path = candidate / 'LICENSE'
            license_path.unlink()
            license_path.symlink_to(self.base / 'LICENSE')
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, 'symlinks'):
                upstream.promote_bundle(self.root, candidate)
    
    
    if __name__ == '__main__':
        unittest.main()

    Add: /Users/kgensupertramp/Desktop/me/infra-server/docs/reuse-spike.md
    # First home-service reuse spike
    
    ## What runs
    
    The unchanged OpenMuse `TaskWorker` and logging helper are imported from
    `CopilotKit/openmuse@a4944f4c471d3dc93b8bfc060b5da309b5216ab2`. This is actual
    upstream implementation, not a rewritten scheduler. Attribution, license, and
    checksums are retained in `vendor/openmuse` and `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.
    
    Node 24 transforms the upstream TypeScript at runtime. Type-only imports are
    erased, so this narrow worker slice does not require the complete upstream
    application, model adapters, CopilotKit account, or database packages.
    
    `spikes/openmuse/home-store.mjs` is a small integration adapter around Node's
    built-in SQLite. It implements only the Store methods the worker consumes. This
    is test glue, not the chosen production schema or a replacement for the upstream
    PostgreSQL store. The production storage decision remains open.
    
    `home-tasks.mjs` supplies synthetic owner/session inputs and a deterministic
    handler. A task either asks a fixed question or creates a synthetic artifact.
    This intentionally does not call a model, launch arbitrary commands, browse,
    authenticate a person, or perform a real external action.
    
    ## Executed local evidence
    
    Eight integration tests passed on Node 24.18.0 on the development Mac:
    
    - Two users with two conversations each preserve owner-scoped task/artifact
      records while one task waits for input and others finish.
    - Closing/reopening the database preserves the question and accepts an answer;
      an immediate duplicate answer does not create another run.
    - Two worker/store instances racing for a queued task execute it once in this
      in-process test. This is not a claim of universal exactly-once side effects.
    - A child process checkpoints a running task and exits abruptly. Another worker
      recovers its state after simulated lease expiry.
    - Pending approvals do not occupy a worker slot; a resolved approval becomes
      eligible. This tests scheduling, not a real approval-enforcement boundary.
    - Cancellation prevents the blocked handler's late result from overwriting it.
    - A stale worker cannot checkpoint over a paused task.
    - A handler failure is recorded and is not silently re-executed as queued work.
    
    The executable demo also passed: independent Alice/Bob work completes, the home
    database is reopened, and Alice's persisted waiting task resumes after her answer.
    Eight separate Python tests passed for source drift detection, update staging,
    immutable pins, fixed paths, and candidate-bundle validation.
    
    The fixture trusts its owner argument. Its owner-scoped storage checks do not
    establish household authentication, authorization, root-user protection, or
    privacy of a full installed system. Conversation IDs are labels carried by task
    inputs/artifacts, not a completed conversation/message service.
    
    ## Why this slice
    
    The inspected worker already has persisted leases, input/approval states, events,
    checkpoints, cancellation guards, and multiple eligible task execution. Reusing
    it tests a concrete home-infrastructure requirement with no need to first port a
    mobile app or accept a hosted thread service.
    
    The upstream worker caps in-flight tasks at three, scans task records, keys local
    active work by task ID, and does not provide Me's household fair scheduling,
    resource classes, or a validated dependency DAG in this slice. It assumes task
    IDs are unique across owners; our fixture uses home-generated UUIDs. Its retry
    and lease behavior cannot make arbitrary external side effects exactly once.
    These are review items before production adoption, not hidden implementation
    claims. Keep real tool effects behind the home broker and action ledger.
    
    ## Next gates
    
    1. Test an actual agent/model adapter against the home task contract, with honest
       model/network dependencies and completion evidence.
    2. Add the phone → hosted backend → home protocol with authenticated identities,
       acknowledgments, event replay, and offline delivery behavior.
    3. Build the household conversation/data service and approval broker, reusing
       existing implementations/libraries where they fit.
    4. Have `setup-infra` install/pair the tested home services on a declared platform.
    5. Exercise real browser/code/render workers and their isolation/resource limits.
    
    No claim is made that the full OpenMuse app, its complete upstream typecheck,
    Docker workers, phone UI, live model, hosted relay, or home installer was run.
    The local npm registry was unreachable during this session; Docker was not on
    PATH. This dependency-free slice was run rather than substituting invented
    results for those wider integration checks.

    # Keeping upstream improvements flowing
    
    ## Imported subset and ownership
    
    The source pin and SHA-256 inventory live in `vendor/openmuse/upstream.json`.
    Only the worker, logging helper, and license are imported. Do not edit those files
    in place. Put Me adapters and integration tests outside the vendor directory.
    If a necessary upstream patch arises, first try an adapter or an upstream fix;
    otherwise record a reproducible patch separately before changing this zero-patch
    update policy.
    
    This mechanism refreshes existing imported files; it does not magically adopt
    new capabilities, dependencies, screens, or source paths. The update PR links to
    the full upstream commit comparison so reviewers can identify useful new work.
    New imports require an explicit allowlist/license/test change.
    
    ## Automation included
    
    Normal CI verifies source hashes and runs the Python updater tests, real-worker
    integration tests, and model-free demo. The scheduled workflow runs Mondays at
    09:17 UTC and supports manual dispatch with an optional full upstream SHA.
    
    Its first job has read-only repository permissions and no model, household,
    deployment, or publishing credentials. It resolves upstream `main`, downloads a
    fixed file list at that immutable commit, and runs the compatibility suite. Only
    a passing candidate produces an artifact bundle. A failing candidate stops the
    workflow and does not open an update PR.
    
    A separate job, on a fresh runner, uses the approved updater to validate that
    bundle's paths, hashes, revision and contents. It does not execute the candidate
    code. It commits only `vendor/openmuse` to a revision-specific branch and opens a
    review PR. There is no automatic merge, deployment, or home update.
    
    GitHub Actions dependencies also have a weekly Dependabot configuration. Pins
    are exact commits; action upgrades arrive for review independently of OpenMuse.
    
    ## Activation and GitHub behavior
    
    These workflows must first be committed/pushed and merged to the repository's
    default branch. No workflow was remotely enabled, dispatched, or published by
    this local implementation.
    
    The repository/organization must permit GitHub Actions to create pull requests.
    The proposal job explicitly requests contents/PR write permissions. If policy
    forbids PR creation, the candidate test job can still run and retain its bundle;
    the proposal job will fail visibly rather than pretending the PR was opened.
    
    PRs created with `GITHUB_TOKEN` normally do not trigger ordinary push/PR workflow
    runs. Candidate checks already execute before proposal; maintainers should
    manually dispatch `CI` on the proposal branch if independent branch checks are
    required. A narrowly scoped GitHub App is a later option for automatic PR-check
    triggering; no personal token is required or requested by this prototype.
    
    Review license changes, new imports/dependencies, task-state semantics, side
    effects, resource behavior, and data access before merging. A source-compatible
    worker is only one part of overall product compatibility.
    
    ## Local operation
    
    ```sh
    # Offline verification and regression checks
    python3 scripts/upstream.py verify
    python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py' -v
    npm run test:spike
    
    # Network required: inspect latest main without changing source
    python3 scripts/upstream.py check
    
    # Network required: update the fixed subset to a reviewed full commit SHA
    python3 scripts/upstream.py update --revision FULL_40_CHARACTER_COMMIT_SHA
    ```
    
    An update refuses to overwrite drifted vendor source. Downloads finish before
    the source snapshot is changed. An interrupted filesystem write can leave a
    failed checksum; recover the reviewed snapshot from Git rather than continuing
    with a partially changed tree. This is a development updater, not a household
    release installer or transactional database migration tool.
    
    ## Product release integration
    
    Upstream integration and household deployment are separate stages:
    
    ```text
    upstream commit -> candidate tests -> review PR -> reviewed integration
    -> phone/backend/home/installer contract tests -> signed/versioned release
    -> staged household update with compatible migrations and recovery
    ```
    
    Only the source-candidate stages are implemented here. The product release
    manifest, signed distribution, full cross-repo tests, installer rollout, and
    data-compatible rollback remain work for the integrated product milestone.

    # Reuse audit and first integration evidence
    
    Status: source audit plus executed model-free home-worker spike, 2026-11-02
    (America/Los_Angeles). Inspected commits may be dated 2026-11-03 UTC. No final
    production framework, database, phone framework, or hardware selection is implied.
    
    Requirements: [product architecture](product-architecture.md) and
    [whole-product delivery](product-delivery-plan.md): user-owned home execution and
    data, multiple private household users/conversations, hosted Me coordination,
    phone interaction, and installation/upgrade tooling.
    
    ## Recommendation
    
    Reuse existing software at the largest boundary that fits the household privacy
    and deployment model; keep Me adapters separate from imported source.
    
    - **OpenClaw is a strong complete home-assistant baseline to trial next.** Its
      gateway, agent/session scopes and protocol may replace substantial runtime and
      infrastructure work. Separate agent workspaces do not establish hard user
      isolation. A per-user service boundary is an option to measure.
    - **OpenMuse is a concrete mobile/workflow donor.** Its full application's
      required external thread service and single-owner login require adaptation for
      Me. Reuse compatible modules without inheriting those assumptions. Its task
      worker is the first executed slice.
    - **Deep Agents is the embeddable-harness alternative** if integrating a complete
      gateway adds more complexity than it saves. It provides agent-loop behavior;
      home identity/data/client integration remains work for Me.
    
    These are source-based engineering assessments. No live-model benchmark between
    the complete products was run; there is no measured overall winner.
    
    ## Pinned source inventory
    
    | Source | Inspected revision | Reuse opportunity | Main integration gap |
    | --- | --- | --- | --- |
    | [CopilotKit/openmuse](https://github.com/CopilotKit/openmuse/tree/a4944f4c471d3dc93b8bfc060b5da309b5216ab2) | `a4944f4c471d3dc93b8bfc060b5da309b5216ab2` | Native UI, task/approval views, worker, browser/computer adapters | Single-owner auth, external chat storage, durable follow-ups, household resource policy |
    | [openclaw/openclaw](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/tree/9312f263af4a3095d11f059e8637acf427701a96) | `9312f263af4a3095d11f059e8637acf427701a96` | Home gateway, sessions/agents, protocol, tools | Trusted gateway boundary versus private family users; sandbox and plugin/account state |
    | [langchain-ai/deepagents](https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/tree/5829691de8f43d201f9534fb731643223c0bbccc) | `5829691de8f43d201f9534fb731643223c0bbccc` | Embeddable planning/tool/context/skill harness | Household data, home API, installation and phone integration |
    
    The inspected projects identify their relevant project code as MIT-licensed;
    services, model weights, optional dependencies and assets need their own review.
    Preserve original notices. This is not blanket clearance for a complete product.
    
    ## Source findings
    
    OpenMuse's [thread documentation](https://github.com/CopilotKit/openmuse/blob/a4944f4c471d3dc93b8bfc060b5da309b5216ab2/docs/RICH-THREADS.md)
    requires CopilotKit Intelligence in every mode, describes a single-user workspace,
    and places chat follow-up queues in the open client. Server-side delegated tasks
    are separate. Replacing chat persistence requires engineering, not just a flag.
    
    Its [computer documentation](https://github.com/CopilotKit/openmuse/blob/a4944f4c471d3dc93b8bfc060b5da309b5216ab2/docs/COMPUTER.md)
    describes different Docker/E2B lifecycle and network boundaries. The cloud adapter
    is not Me's default home executor; reused tools must obey home permissions.
    
    OpenClaw's [multi-agent documentation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/9312f263af4a3095d11f059e8637acf427701a96/docs/concepts/multi-agent.md)
    defines per-agent scopes but explains that workspace paths are not sandboxes and
    plugin storage may remain global. Its [gateway protocol](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/9312f263af4a3095d11f059e8637acf427701a96/docs/gateway/protocol.md)
    is an integration surface to examine before writing an equivalent protocol.
    
    Deep Agents' [README](https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/blob/5829691de8f43d201f9534fb731643223c0bbccc/README.md)
    distinguishes its harness from LangGraph's runtime. Select one agent-loop owner;
    do not combine overlapping engines by default. The inspected package requires
    Python 3.11 or later; OpenClaw declares specific Node 24/26 ranges. Validate the
    actual selected release on declared home hardware.
    
    ## Reused code and executed evidence
    
    `infra-server/vendor/openmuse` contains the actual unchanged task worker, logging
    helper and MIT license from the OpenMuse pin. An inventory records exact hashes.
    The worker runs against a small built-in Node SQLite adapter in
    `infra-server/spikes/openmuse`. That is integration glue, not a new scheduler or
    the production storage implementation. Upstream's PostgreSQL store remains an
    available production integration option once its dependencies are installed.
    
    Eight integration tests passed: owner/conversation-scoped records across two
    users/four chats, input waits while other work completes, reopening persistence,
    competing worker claims, real child-process crash recovery after lease expiry,
    approval eligibility, cancellation/stale-writer fencing, and failure recording.
    Some behaviors share a test; there are eight executable cases, not eight fully
    implemented product features. The synthetic home demo also passed.
    
    Eight Python tests passed for source hashes, immutable pins, fixed paths,
    download staging, and candidate-bundle validation. These checks run offline.
    
    Limits: owner identity is trusted fixture input; conversation IDs are labels.
    This does not prove authentication, authorization, full conversation storage,
    model quality, phone/backend relay, real approvals, browser/code/render workers,
    full upstream build/typecheck, Docker, or installation. The npm registry was
    unreachable from the shell and Docker was not on PATH; those results were not
    invented or inferred from the narrower test.
    
    The imported worker caps in-flight work at three, scans task records, keys local
    active work by task ID, and does not supply Me's household fairness/resource
    classes or a validated dependency graph in this slice. Task IDs must be unique
    across owners; the fixture uses home-generated UUIDs. Lease recovery cannot make
    arbitrary external side effects exactly once. These are production review items.
    
    ## Reuse across Me repositories
    
    | Repository | Prefer to reuse | Me-specific integration |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | `phone-app` | Existing native/chat/task/approval components | Pairing, household/session UX, authorized home events/results |
    | `backend-server` | Authentication, transport and notification libraries | Account-to-home registration, routing, privacy boundaries |
    | `infra-server` | Gateway/runtime where suitable, workers, storage/service tooling | Home household data/access, resource policy, backend connection |
    | `agentic-framework` | One harness, browser/coding/creative tools | Scoped capability composition and completion checks |
    | `setup-infra` | Packaging/service/isolation/backup mechanisms | Supported configuration, pairing, upgrades and recovery |
    | `feed-algorithm` | Applicable ranking/retrieval components | Family goal controls and authorized inputs |
    | `web-app` | Existing website/demo | Accurate supported features, hardware/setup and onboarding |
    
    The spike does not obligate production to run OpenMuse and OpenClaw schedulers
    together. If a complete gateway owns execution, use its lifecycle or one explicit
    adapter. Disposable experiments should reduce custom code, not add permanent
    duplicate services.
    
    ## Upstream integration included
    
    `infra-server` now has hash verification, fixed-file update tooling, compatibility
    CI, a weekly candidate workflow and Actions Dependabot configuration. Tests run
    under read-only permissions. A separate publisher validates candidate data and
    can open a review PR without executing imported code under its write token.
    
    Only adopted files refresh automatically. PRs link the full upstream comparison
    for feature discovery; new files/tools/dependencies/permissions need explicit
    adoption. No automatic merge, home deployment, or production upgrade exists.
    Workflows remain local until committed/pushed and merged. Repository settings
    must permit automated PR creation. The precise mechanism and limitations are
    documented in `infra-server/docs/upstream-updates.md`.
    
    ## Next integrated trial
    
    Use the same home user/session/task contract to trial a complete home gateway
    against an embeddable harness. Require two users/multiple chats, a persisted
    question alongside independent work, a real model/tool output, restart/reconnect
    recovery, and denied cross-user access. Measure hardware and adaptation effort
    before selecting the production base.
    
    In parallel, prototype hosted-backend ↔ home messaging and the conversation/data
    service. Reuse an existing gateway protocol if it meets Me's identity/privacy
    boundary. Adapt existing phone components after that contract stabilizes.

    +and the upstream-update tooling.
    
     ## Scope
    
     Infrastructure provisioning, service operation, observability, and recovery.
    
    +The service runs on the user's separate home computer and hosts private household
    +data and agent execution. Me's hosted application backend lives in
    +`backend-server`. See [the reuse spike](docs/reuse-spike.md) for exact boundaries,
    +checks, and the next integration gates.
    +
    +## Run the reuse spike
    +
    +Use Node.js 24.18.x and Python 3. No npm dependencies or model credentials are
    +needed; no installation command is required.
    +
    +```sh
    +python3 scripts/upstream.py verify
    +python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py' -v
    +npm run test:spike
    +npm run demo:spike
    +```
    +
    +The demo uses synthetic owners/conversations and a temporary local database,
    +then removes its data. It makes no model or external-service calls.
    +
    +## Upstream integration
    +
    +Imported source stays unchanged under `vendor/openmuse` with its MIT license,
    +commit pin, and SHA-256 inventory. Local adapters stay outside that directory.
    +See [third-party notices](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) and
    +[update operation](docs/upstream-updates.md).
    +
    +After these changes are merged into the repository's default branch, the weekly
    +workflow can test newer upstream source and propose a review PR. It does not
    +automatically merge changes or update home installations.
    +
     ## Contributing
    
     Start with the [contribution guide](https://github.com/mehomeai/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md),
    name: Evaluate OpenMuse upstream update
    
    on:
      schedule:
        - cron: '17 9 * * 1'
      workflow_dispatch:
        inputs:
          revision:
            description: 'Optional full upstream commit SHA; empty checks main'
            required: false
            type: string
    
    permissions:
      contents: read
    
    concurrency:
      group: upstream-openmuse
      cancel-in-progress: false
    
    jobs:
      candidate:
        name: Test upstream without publishing credentials
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 10
        outputs:
          changed: ${{ steps.update.outputs.changed }}
          revision: ${{ steps.update.outputs.revision }}
          previous_revision: ${{ steps.update.outputs.previous_revision }}
          base_revision: ${{ steps.baseline.outputs.revision }}
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}
              persist-credentials: false
          - name: Record the exact baseline tested
            id: baseline
            run: printf 'revision=%s\n' "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          - uses: actions/setup-node@249970729cb0ef3589644e2896645e5dc5ba9c38 # v6
            with:
              node-version: 24.18.0
          - name: Verify updater before downloading code
            run: python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py' -v
          - name: Prepare fixed-path upstream candidate
            id: update
            env:
              REQUESTED_REVISION: ${{ inputs.revision }}
            shell: bash
            run: |
              args=()
              if [ -n "$REQUESTED_REVISION" ]; then
                args+=(--revision "$REQUESTED_REVISION")
              fi
              python3 scripts/upstream.py update "${args[@]}" --bundle "$RUNNER_TEMP/upstream-candidate"
          - name: Verify and test candidate
            if: steps.update.outputs.changed == 'true'
            run: |
              python3 scripts/upstream.py verify
              npm run test:spike
              npm run demo:spike
          - name: Save only candidate source data
            if: steps.update.outputs.changed == 'true'
            uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4
            with:
              name: openmuse-candidate
              path: ${{ runner.temp }}/upstream-candidate
              if-no-files-found: error
              retention-days: 7
    
      propose:
        name: Open a review PR without executing candidate code
        needs: candidate
        if: needs.candidate.outputs.changed == 'true'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 5
        permissions:
          contents: write
          pull-requests: write
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
            with:
              ref: ${{ needs.candidate.outputs.base_revision }}
              persist-credentials: false
          - uses: actions/download-artifact@634f93cb2916e3fdff6788551b99b062d0335ce0 # v5
            with:
              name: openmuse-candidate
              path: ${{ runner.temp }}/upstream-candidate
          - name: Validate candidate data with the approved updater
            env:
              REVISION: ${{ needs.candidate.outputs.revision }}
            run: python3 scripts/upstream.py promote --bundle "$RUNNER_TEMP/upstream-candidate" --revision "$REVISION"
          - name: Propose a source-pin update
            env:
              GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
              REVISION: ${{ needs.candidate.outputs.revision }}
              BASE_BRANCH: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}
              PREVIOUS_REVISION: ${{ needs.candidate.outputs.previous_revision }}
            shell: bash
            run: |
              branch="upstream/openmuse-$REVISION"
              if gh pr view "$branch" --json number >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo 'An update PR already exists for this revision.'
                exit 0
              fi
              git config user.name 'github-actions[bot]'
              git config user.email '41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com'
              git checkout -b "$branch"
              git add -- vendor/openmuse
              git diff --cached --quiet && exit 0
              git commit -m "chore: evaluate OpenMuse $REVISION"
              gh auth setup-git
              git push origin "$branch"
              cat > "$RUNNER_TEMP/upstream-pr.md" <<'BODY'
              Refresh the fixed, unpatched OpenMuse worker subset and its source hashes.
    
              The candidate passed the model-free home integration suite and demonstration
              before publishing. Candidate tests run separately from this write-token job.
    
              This refresh imports only the listed worker files. New upstream UI,
              tools, and features need explicit adoption and their own acceptance checks.
    
              Review the source/license diff, household isolation implications, missing
              imports, and API changes. These tests do not cover a live model, browser,
              phone/backend transport, production authorization, or upstream's full build.
    
              This PR does not merge or deploy automatically. GitHub-token-created PRs
              may not trigger push/PR workflows: manually dispatch CI on this branch
              or use a dedicated GitHub App if independently triggered PR checks are required.
              BODY
              printf '\nFull upstream comparison: https://github.com/CopilotKit/openmuse/compare/%s...%s\n' "$PREVIOUS_REVISION" "$REVISION" >> "$RUNNER_TEMP/upstream-pr.md"
              printf '\nCandidate run: %s/%s/actions/runs/%s\n' "$GITHUB_SERVER_URL" "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" >> "$RUNNER_TEMP/upstream-pr.md"
              gh pr create --base "$BASE_BRANCH" --head "$branch" --title "chore: evaluate OpenMuse $REVISION" --body-file "$RUNNER_TEMP/upstream-pr.md"
