                               "config.json or service.env"},
        }
    
    
    def render_service_env(*, db_path: Path, host: str, port: int,
                           allow_remote: bool = False,
                           allow_code_exec: bool = False) -> str:
        """Render config/service.env. Non-secret values only, always."""
        lines = [
            "# Generated by setup-infra (rerunnable; safe to regenerate).",
            "# Non-secret values only. Secrets are exported in the operator shell,",
            "# never stored here, and never committed.",
            f"HOME_DB={db_path}",
            f"HOME_HOST={host}",
            f"HOME_PORT={port}",
            f"ME_RUNTIME_ALLOW_REMOTE={'1' if allow_remote else ''}",
            f"ME_RUNTIME_ALLOW_CODE_EXEC={'1' if allow_code_exec else ''}",
            "#",
            "# Explicit opt-in remote model (synthetic tests only, never household data):",
            "#   export ME_RUNTIME_ALLOW_REMOTE=1",
            "#   export ME_RUNTIME_MODEL_API_KEY='<value>'  # shell only; never store",
        ]
        return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
    
    
    def _is_denied(path: Path) -> str | None:
        text = os.path.normpath(str(path))

    export function resolveRuntimeCommand(env = process.env) {

        }

    function flag(name, fallback = null) {
      const hit = process.argv.find((arg) => arg.startsWith(`${name}=`));
      return hit ? hit.slice(name.length + 1) : fallback;
    }
    
    function usage() {
      console.log(`me-home usage:
      node --experimental-transform-types src/cli.mjs start [--db=<path>] [--host=127.0.0.1] [--port=7070]
      node --experimental-transform-types src/cli.mjs bootstrap --user=<id> [--db=<path>] [--ttl-ms=900000] [--name=<display>]
      node --experimental-transform-types src/cli.mjs seed-dev [--db=<path>]
    
    start binds loopback (${DEFAULT_HOST}) by default. bootstrap/seed-dev touch the
    SQLite file directly on this host; they never traverse the network.
    seed-dev creates DEVELOPMENT-ONLY fixture users alice/bob for local tests.
    
    Task execution env (see docs/home-h2-handoff.md):
      HOME_MODEL_PROVIDER=local|fixture|openai|anthropic (required for task runs)
      HOME_ALLOW_FIXTURE_MODEL=1 (fixture only, dev/tests)
      ME_RUNTIME_CMD="python3 -m me_runtime.bridge" (default; tests use the fixture bridge)`);
    }
    
    function die(message) {
      console.error(`error: ${message}`);
      process.exit(2);
    }
    
    function parsePort(raw, fallback) {
      if (raw == null) return fallback;
      if (!/^\d+$/.test(raw)) die(`--port must be an integer 1..65535 (got ${JSON.stringify(raw)})`);
      const port = Number(raw);
      if (port < 1 || port > 65535) die(`--port must be an integer 1..65535 (got ${raw})`);
      return port;
    }
    
    function parseTtlMs(raw, fallback) {
      if (raw == null) return fallback;
      if (!/^\d+$/.test(raw)) die(`--ttl-ms must be a positive integer of milliseconds (got ${JSON.stringify(raw)})`);
      const ttl = Number(raw);
      if (ttl <= 0 || ttl > 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000) die('--ttl-ms must be within 1ms..24h');
      return ttl;
    }
    
    function parseUser(raw) {
      if (raw == null || raw === '') die('bootstrap requires --user=<id>');
      if (!/^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,128}$/.test(raw)) die('--user must be 1..128 chars of letters, digits, . _ -');

    from __future__ import annotations
    
    import itertools
    import os
    import sys
    from dataclasses import dataclass
    from typing import Any
    
    from langchain_core.callbacks import CallbackManagerForLLMRun
    from langchain_core.language_models.chat_models import BaseChatModel
    from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage, BaseMessage, HumanMessage

    class ModelError(Exception):
        def __init__(self, code: str, message: str) -> None:
            super().__init__(message)
            self.code = code
    
    
    @dataclass
    class ModelConfig:
        provider: str
        model: str
        endpoint: str | None = None
        api_key_env: str | None = None
        use_responses_api: bool = False
    
    
    def model_config_from(obj: dict[str, Any]) -> ModelConfig:
        if not isinstance(obj, dict):
            raise ModelError("invalid_request", "model must be an object")
        provider = obj.get("provider")
        model = obj.get("model")
        if not provider or not isinstance(provider, str):
            raise ModelError("invalid_request", "model.provider is required")
        if not model or not isinstance(model, str):
            raise ModelError("invalid_request", "model.model is required")
        return ModelConfig(
            provider=provider,
            model=model,
            endpoint=obj.get("endpoint"),
            api_key_env=obj.get("api_key_env"),
            use_responses_api=bool(obj.get("use_responses_api", False)),
        )
    
    
    def _require_remote_opt_in(provider: str, api_key_env: str | None) -> str:
        if os.environ.get("ME_RUNTIME_ALLOW_REMOTE") != "1":
            raise ModelError(
                "model_not_configured",
                f"remote provider {provider!r} requires "
                "ME_RUNTIME_ALLOW_REMOTE=1 (explicit opt-in)")
        env_name = api_key_env or "ME_RUNTIME_MODEL_API_KEY"
        key = os.environ.get(env_name)
        if not key:
            raise ModelError("model_not_configured",
                             f"remote provider {provider!r} needs {env_name} set")
        return key
    
    
    def build_chat_model(cfg: ModelConfig):
        """Return a LangChain chat model for the configured provider."""
        provider = cfg.provider
        if provider == "fixture":
            return FixtureChatModel()
        if provider == "local":
            from langchain_ollama import ChatOllama
            base_url = (cfg.endpoint or os.environ.get(
                "ME_RUNTIME_LOCAL_ENDPOINT", "http://127.0.0.1:11434"))
            return ChatOllama(model=cfg.model, base_url=base_url,
                              temperature=0.2)
        if provider == "openai":
            # Any provider=openai use — even a localhost URL — requires the
            # explicit remote opt-in so a remote URL can never be mislabelled
            # to skip privacy checks.
            key = _require_remote_opt_in("openai", cfg.api_key_env)
            from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
            kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {
                "model": cfg.model, "api_key": key, "temperature": 0.2}
            if cfg.endpoint:
                kwargs["base_url"] = cfg.endpoint
            if cfg.use_responses_api:
                try:
                    kwargs["use_responses_api"] = True
                    return ChatOpenAI(**kwargs)
                except TypeError:
                    del kwargs["use_responses_api"]
                    print("[runtime] installed langchain-openai does not "
                          "accept use_responses_api; using Chat Completions",
                          file=sys.stderr)
            return ChatOpenAI(**kwargs)
        if provider == "anthropic":
            key = _require_remote_opt_in("anthropic", cfg.api_key_env)
            from langchain_anthropic import ChatAnthropic
            kwargs = {"model": cfg.model, "api_key": key, "temperature": 0.2}
            if cfg.endpoint:
                kwargs["base_url"] = cfg.endpoint
            return ChatAnthropic(**kwargs)
        raise ModelError("invalid_request",
                         f"unknown model.provider {provider!r}")

                    "internal", "cancelled")
    
    
    def _tool_error_code(content: str) -> str:
        head = (content or "")[:300]
        for code in _KNOWN_CODES:
            if code in head:
                return code
        return "tool_error"

    # Production tunnel boundary (Cloudflare, named tunnel)
    
    Design boundary for the future production home endpoint. **Nothing here is
    provisioned by the dev setup**: `me_setup.py` leaves `tunnel.mode: disabled`,
    creates no tunnel, publishes no route, and stores no provider credentials.
    This document tells a future production installer what to use and what to
    avoid, per `infra-server/docs/connection-and-pairing.md` (read that first).
    
    ## Required shape
    
    - **Named tunnel via `cloudflared` outbound connector**, owned by the household's
      own Cloudflare account. The home initiates outbound connections only; no
      inbound firewall hole, no home listener on a public interface.
    - **Durable hostname** (e.g. `home.<family-domain>`). Quick Tunnels
      (`trycloudflare.com`) are documented by Cloudflare for development/testing
      only and must never back a household deployment.
    - **Protection before route**: create Cloudflare Access protection first, then
      publish the application route. Start closed on failure. If Access is used,
      validate its token at the origin as Cloudflare documents; Access checks do
      **not** replace Me's own paired-device + household/user authorization.
    - **Origin scope**: publish only the intended home application gateway. Model,
      database, worker, and management services bind private interfaces. The same
      device/user checks apply to event streams, artifacts, browser previews, and
      uploads — not just chat.
    - **Supported provider tooling only**: `cloudflared` releases and Cloudflare
      Zero Trust dashboard/API. No custom tunnel protocol, no ad-hoc signature
      scheme for pairing (use maintained auth libraries + platform key storage).
    
    ## Credential separation (normative)
    
    | Credential | Holder | May it reach a phone? | Rotation |
    | --- | --- | --- | --- |
    | Cloudflare account / API / zone admin | Trusted provisioning only (least privilege) | Never | Independent |
    | Tunnel connector credential (`cert.json` / token) | Home connector host only, `secrets/` mode `0600` | Never — not in pairing QR, not an API token | Authenticated rotation |
    | Home installation identity | Home service; public parts registered with backend/paired clients | Public identity reference only | Authenticated rotation + recovery |
    | Pairing invitation secret | Single-use exchange, setup/authorized admin → phone | Yes (one invitation, short-lived, high-entropy) | Expires/consumed atomically |
    | Phone device key / enrollment | That phone (private key stays on device); home stores verifier | Device-bound credential only | Per-device revoke/rotate |
    | Home API session token | Authorized phone, audience = that home/API | Short-lived session use | Renew via device credential |
    
    Service tokens (client-ID/secret), if ever used for edge integration, are
    per-device scoped, stored, rotated, and revoked per device — never one shared
    fleet secret baked into the app. Provider credential headers stay distinct
    from home API authorization headers, and secrets never appear in logs.
    
    ## Pairing admission without weakening the boundary
    
    A not-yet-paired phone must reach enrollment without already holding the normal
    edge credential. Options: backend-mediated enrollment, or a tightly limited
    pairing endpoint with its own short-lived admission. Never bypass protection
    for the whole home API to make pairing work. Anonymous health responses reveal
    only minimal readiness.
    
    ## Production installer expectations (future, not claimed)
    
    A production installer built on this boundary must additionally cover: stable
    hostname recovery, connector credential rotation, hostname/key rotation that is
    itself authenticated, revocation propagation windows (including backend-issued
    revocation while the home is offline), offline behavior (honest offline state),
    backup/restore of household data, and release compatibility between the
    installer, home service, backend, and phone. The dev setup in this repository
    claims none of that; it validates prerequisites and writes local config only.
    
    ## Optional named-tunnel adapter (setup-infra task S2)
    
    `scripts/me_lifecycle.py tunnel` is a real configuration/launch adapter over an
    existing `cloudflared` binary plus an externally supplied least-privileged
    credential file. It writes config and optionally launches the connector; it
    never provisions accounts, hostnames, or DNS.
    
    ```sh
    # 1. Provision OUTSIDE this tooling (Cloudflare dashboard/API, your own team):
    #    named tunnel + stable hostname + least-privileged credential JSON file.
    #    Place the file at <data-dir>/secrets/tunnel-cred.json with mode 0600.
    chmod 0600 secrets/tunnel-cred.json
    
    # 2. Fail-closed configure: requires --hostname (real FQDN; trycloudflare.io
    #    and bare names refused), --credential-file (must exist, must be 0600),
    #    --access-team (Zero Trust team slug), and --pairing-admission
    #    {backend-mediated|limited-pairing-service}. Writes config/cloudflared.yml
    #    (0600, path reference only) and records protection in config.json.
    python3 scripts/me_lifecycle.py tunnel configure --hostname home.example.com \
      --credential-file secrets/tunnel-cred.json \
      --access-team myteam --pairing-admission backend-mediated
    
    # 3. Launch (foreground, or --detach with pidfile discipline):
    python3 scripts/me_lifecycle.py tunnel run
    ```
    
    Guarantees: credential content is never logged, never in argv (only `--config`
    path), never in a phone QR; `tunnel run` without a configured tunnel or
    without `cloudflared` exits `4` (parked) instead of inventing connectivity;
    no Quick Tunnel support (`--dev`-style ephemeral tunnels are not offered).
    No Access authentication is invented here: the adapter requires the operator
    to declare the Access team + pairing admission and documents that Cloudflare
    Access protection must exist before any route is published, with origin-side
    paired-device enforcement unchanged.

    def _validate_request(obj: object) -> dict:
        if not isinstance(obj, dict):
            raise ValueError("request must be a JSON object")
        if obj.get("bridge") != BRIDGE:
            raise ValueError("bridge must be 'runtime-bridge-v1'")
        op = obj.get("op", "run")
        if op not in ("run", "resume"):
            raise ValueError("op must be 'run' or 'resume'")
        for f in ("run_id", "user_id", "conversation_id"):
            v = obj.get(f)
            if not v or not isinstance(v, str):
                raise ValueError(f"{f} is required")
        ws = obj.get("workspace")
        if not ws or not isinstance(ws, str):
            raise ValueError("workspace is required")
        if op == "run" and not obj.get("request"):
            raise ValueError("request text is required for op=run")
        caps = obj.get("capabilities")
        if not isinstance(caps, dict):
            raise ValueError("capabilities object is required")
        if not isinstance(obj.get("model"), dict):
            raise ValueError("model object is required")
        budgets = obj.get("budgets") or {}
        if not isinstance(budgets, dict):
            raise ValueError("budgets must be an object")
        return obj

    """Guarded web fetch (curl-backed) + offline browser renderer.
    
    Transport policy (every hop, redirects included):
    - scheme http/https only; URLs with credentials or explicit non-default
      ports are rejected;
    - host must match `network_egress_allowlist` (exact or leading-dot suffix);
    - the host is resolved and EVERY returned address must be globally
      routable (private/loopback/link-local/multicast/reserved/unspecified
      all fail closed); unresolvable hosts fail closed;
    - DNS is pinned per hop: curl `--resolve host:port:ip` dials the vetted
      address while SNI/TLS verification still uses the hostname (maintained
      curl TLS; no custom TLS code);
    - redirects are followed manually (max 3), each target re-validated;
    - body capped at 500_000 bytes via curl `--max-filesize`, timeouts bounded.
    
    `browser_open` is a REAL but deliberately limited offline renderer: the
    page is fetched through the vetted broker above, then rendered by headless
    Chromium with JavaScript disabled and every subrequest aborted
    (no navigation, no websockets/service workers, no downloads, no home
    network access from page content). Full interactive automation requires
    an isolated/proxied sandbox that does not exist here, so anything beyond
    offline rendering fails closed with `prerequisite_missing`. This is
    documented as limited rendering, not full automation.

    def host_allowed(url: str, allowlist: list) -> bool:
        try:
            host = (urlparse(url).hostname or "").lower()
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
            return False
        for entry in allowlist or []:
            e = (entry or "").strip().lower()
            if not e:
                continue
            if e.startswith("."):
                if host.endswith(e):
                    return True
            elif host == e:
                return True
        return False
    
    
    def _validate_url(url: str, allowlist: list) -> tuple[str, str, int]:
        """Return (host, scheme, port) or raise ToolDeniedError."""
        try:
            parts = urlparse(url)
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
            raise ToolDeniedError("capability_denied",
                                  f"unparseable URL: {exc}") from exc
        scheme = (parts.scheme or "").lower()
        if scheme not in ("http", "https"):
            raise ToolDeniedError("capability_denied",
                                  f"unsupported scheme: {scheme!r}")
        if parts.username or parts.password:
            raise ToolDeniedError("capability_denied",
                                  "URLs with credentials are rejected")
        host = parts.hostname or ""
        if not host:
            raise ToolDeniedError("capability_denied", "URL has no host")
        port = parts.port or ALLOWED_PORTS[scheme]
        if port != ALLOWED_PORTS[scheme]:
            raise ToolDeniedError("capability_denied",
                                  f"non-default port rejected: {port}")
        if not host_allowed(url, allowlist):
            raise ToolDeniedError(
                "capability_denied",
                f"host {host!r} not in network_egress_allowlist; "
                "approvals cannot expand the allowlist")
        return host, scheme, port
    
    
    def _resolve_addrs(host: str, port: int) -> list[str]:
        """Raw DNS resolution (seam for deterministic tests)."""
        try:
            infos = socket.getaddrinfo(host, port, type=socket.SOCK_STREAM)
        except OSError as exc:
            raise ToolDeniedError("capability_denied",
                                  f"DNS resolution failed for {host!r}: "
                                  f"{exc}") from exc
        return [info[4][0] for info in infos]
    
    
    def _resolve_global(host: str, port: int) -> list[str]:
        """Resolve host; return global IPs or raise (fail closed)."""
        addrs: list[str] = []
        for ip_str in _resolve_addrs(host, port):
            try:
                ip = ipaddress.ip_address(ip_str)
            except ValueError as exc:
                raise ToolDeniedError("capability_denied",
                                      f"unparseable address for {host!r}") from exc
            if not ip.is_global:
                raise ToolDeniedError(
                    "capability_denied",
                    f"non-global destination refused for {host!r}: {ip_str}")
            if ip_str not in addrs:
                addrs.append(ip_str)
        if not addrs:
            raise ToolDeniedError("capability_denied",
                                  f"no addresses for {host!r}")

    def _run_curl(args: list[str], timeout_s: float) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
        return subprocess.run(args, capture_output=True, timeout=timeout_s)
    
    
    def _curl_path() -> str:
        path = shutil.which("curl")
        if not path:
            raise ToolDeniedError(
                "prerequisite_missing",
                "curl transport not available (provisioned by setup-infra)")
        return path
    
    
    def broker_fetch(url: str, allowlist: list) -> tuple[int, str, str]:
        """Vetted fetch. Returns (status, final_url, text). Raises ToolDeniedError."""
        curl = _curl_path()
        current = url
        for _hop in range(MAX_REDIRECTS + 1):
            host, scheme, port = _validate_url(current, allowlist)
            pinned = _resolve_global(host, port)[0]
            args = [curl, "-sS", "--proto", "=http,=https",
                    "--max-redirs", "0",
                    "--connect-timeout", str(CONNECT_TIMEOUT_S),
                    "--max-time", str(MAX_TIME_S),
                    "--max-filesize", str(MAX_BODY_BYTES),
                    "--resolve", f"{host}:{port}:{pinned}",
                    "-D", "-", "-o", "-", "-w", "\n%{http_code}",
                    "--user-agent", "me-runtime/0.2",
                    current]
            try:
                proc = _run_curl(args, MAX_TIME_S + 10)
            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as exc:
                raise ToolDeniedError("tool_error",
                                      "fetch timed out") from exc
            if proc.returncode == 63:
                raise ToolDeniedError("tool_error",
                                      f"response exceeded {MAX_BODY_BYTES} bytes; "
                                      "truncated fetch refused")
            if proc.returncode != 0:
                raise ToolDeniedError(
                    "tool_error",
                    f"fetch failed: {(proc.stderr or b'')[:300].decode(errors='replace')}")
            out = proc.stdout or b""
            try:
                body, _, code = out.rpartition(b"\n")
                status = int(code.strip())
            except ValueError as exc:
                raise ToolDeniedError("tool_error",
                                      "fetch returned unreadable status") from exc
            # Split dumped headers from body on first blank line.
            headers, _, payload = body.partition(b"\r\n\r\n")
            if status in (301, 302, 303, 307, 308):
                location = None
                for line in headers.decode("latin-1").splitlines():
                    if line.lower().startswith("location:"):
                        location = line.split(":", 1)[1].strip()
                        break
                if not location:
                    raise ToolDeniedError("tool_error",
                                          "redirect without Location")
                current = urljoin(current, location)
                continue
            if status >= 400:
                raise ToolDeniedError(
                    "tool_error",
                    f"HTTP {status} for {current[:200]}")
            text = payload[:MAX_BODY_BYTES].decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
            return status, current, text
        raise ToolDeniedError("tool_error",
                              f"too many redirects (>{MAX_REDIRECTS})")

    def _popen_bounded(cmd: list[str], timeout_s: float,
                       cancelled) -> tuple[int, str, str]:
        """Run cmd, streaming stdout/stderr with caps while it runs.
    
        Returns (returncode, stdout_tail, stderr_tail). Raises
        subprocess.TimeoutExpired on timeout; checks `cancelled` while polling.
        """
        proc = subprocess.Popen(cmd, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
                                stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
        out_chunks: list[bytes] = []
        err_chunks: list[bytes] = []
        out_len = 0
        err_len = 0
    
        def _drain(stream, chunks: list[bytes], cap: int, counter: str):
            nonlocal out_len, err_len
            while True:
                data = stream.read(65536)
                if not data:
                    break
                chunks.append(data)
                if counter == "out":
                    out_len += len(data)
                else:
                    err_len += len(data)
                # Drop oldest chunks past the cap (bounded memory).
                total = sum(len(c) for c in chunks)
                while total > cap and len(chunks) > 1:
                    total -= len(chunks.pop(0))
    
        tout = threading.Thread(target=_drain,
                                args=(proc.stdout, out_chunks, STDOUT_CAP, "out"),
                                daemon=True)
        terr = threading.Thread(target=_drain,
                                args=(proc.stderr, err_chunks, STDERR_CAP, "err"),
                                daemon=True)
        tout.start()
        terr.start()
        deadline = time.time() + timeout_s
        while True:
            try:
                rc = proc.wait(timeout=0.2)
                break
            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:

    The current CI checks repository hygiene; it does not validate a working product.

    Agent execution, tool permissions, orchestration, and model integration.
    
    ## Product architecture and reuse work
    
    The agent executes on the user's separate home computer alongside `infra-server`,
    which hosts household data and multiple users/conversations. `backend-server`
    coordinates accounts and home access; setup should provision a protected tunnel
    endpoint and one-time phone enrollment. Direct versus relayed private traffic
    remains a transport decision. `setup-infra` installs and maintains the home environment.
    
    Start with [product architecture](docs/product-architecture.md), the

    # infra-server
    
    Infrastructure services for the Me Home AI platform.
    
    Part of [Me Home AI](https://github.com/mehomeai), a privacy-first home agentic system.
    Learn about the vision at [Me — Your intelligence. Yours.](https://mehomeai.replit.app/me/).
    
    ## Status
    
    This repository contains an initial, model-free home-service reuse spike. It runs
    the actual pinned OpenMuse task worker against a local SQLite integration fixture.
    It is not the production home server, a supported household installation, or a
    live AI agent. CI checks repository hygiene, source provenance, worker behavior,
    and the upstream-update tooling.
    
    ## Scope
    
    Infrastructure provisioning, service operation, observability, and recovery.
    
    The service runs on the user's separate home computer and hosts private household
    data and agent execution. Me's hosted application backend lives in
    `backend-server`. See [the reuse spike](docs/reuse-spike.md) for exact boundaries,
    checks, and the next integration gates.
    
    The proposed [home connection and phone pairing flow](docs/connection-and-pairing.md)
    covers a protected tunnel endpoint, one-time enrollment, per-device access, and
    the hosted backend's coordination role. It is a design, not deployed connectivity.
    
    ## Run the reuse spike
    
    Use Node.js 24.18.x and Python 3. No npm dependencies or model credentials are
    needed; no installation command is required.
    
    ```sh
    python3 scripts/upstream.py verify
    python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py' -v
    npm run test:spike
    npm run demo:spike
    ```
    
    The demo uses synthetic owners/conversations and a temporary local database,
    then removes its data. It makes no model or external-service calls.

    ## Status
    
    This repository provides the rerunnable development setup and managed lifecycle
    for the Me home service: `scripts/me_setup.py` (prerequisites, config,
    non-secret environment; tested by `scripts/test_me_setup.py`) and
    `scripts/me_lifecycle.py` (managed start/status/stop, home-CLI bootstrap,
    verified SQLite backup/restore, optional fail-closed named-tunnel adapter,
    service-unit generation; tested by `scripts/test_me_lifecycle.py`, including a

    (`infra-server/contracts/home-api-v1.md`) and the H2 runtime bridge
    (`agentic-framework/docs/runtime-bridge-v1.md`), records local-first
    model configuration, and documents the production tunnel boundary in
    `docs/production-tunnel-boundary.md`. No root, no global install, no public
    endpoint; service units and tunnel launches are explicit operator actions.
    
    ```sh
    python3 scripts/me_setup.py setup [--data-dir DIR] [--port N]
    python3 scripts/me_setup.py check [--data-dir DIR]
    python3 scripts/me_lifecycle.py start|status|stop|bootstrap|backup|restore|tunnel|service ...
    python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py' -v
    ```

    and [`docs/production-tunnel-boundary.md`](docs/production-tunnel-boundary.md)

    def port_free(host: str, port: int) -> tuple[bool, str]:
        try:
            family = socket.AF_INET6 if ":" in host else socket.AF_INET
            with socket.socket(family, socket.SOCK_STREAM) as s:
                if family == socket.AF_INET:
                    s.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
                s.bind((host, port))
            return True, "bindable"
        except OSError as exc:
            return False, f"not bindable: {exc}"

    def _curl_env() -> dict[str, str]:
        """Environment for curl: proxy variables stripped.
    
        A proxy would bypass `--resolve` DNS pinning, so no `*_PROXY` value
        (any case) is inherited; `--noproxy '*'` is also passed explicitly.
        """
        return {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items()
                if not k.upper().endswith("_PROXY")}
    
    
    def _curl_bounded(args: list[str], timeout_s: float
                      ) -> tuple[int, bytes, bytes]:
        """Run curl, streaming stdout/stderr with hard caps WHILE running.
    
        Independent of server chunking/content-length: the process is killed
        as soon as the combined output exceeds CURL_TOTAL_CAP or the deadline
        passes, so no response can force unbounded allocation.
        """
        proc = subprocess.Popen(args, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
                                stderr=subprocess.PIPE, env=_curl_env())
        assert proc.stdout is not None and proc.stderr is not None
        err = bytearray()
    
        def _drain_err() -> None:
            while True:
                chunk = proc.stderr.read(65536)
                if not chunk:
                    break
                err.extend(chunk)
                del err[:-65536]
    
        err_thread = threading.Thread(target=_drain_err, daemon=True)
        err_thread.start()
        timer = threading.Timer(timeout_s, proc.kill)
        timer.start()
        out = bytearray()
        try:
            while True:
                chunk = proc.stdout.read(65536)
                if not chunk:
                    break
                out += chunk
                if len(out) > CURL_TOTAL_CAP:
                    raise ToolDeniedError(
                        "tool_error",
                        f"response exceeded {CURL_TOTAL_CAP} bytes; "
                        "killed before buffering")
        finally:

    def build_docker_cmd(image: str, cname: str, src_ro: str, input_ro: str,
                         command: list[str]) -> list[str]:
        # No --rm: the container is removed explicitly in a finally block so
        # `docker cp` can extract bounded outputs after stop. No writable host
        # mounts exist at all: /src and /input are read-only, /work and /tmp
        # are size-bounded tmpfs.
        return ["docker", "run", "--name", cname,
                "--network", "none",
                "--user", "65532:65532",
                "--cap-drop", "ALL",
                "--security-opt", "no-new-privileges",
                "--cpus", "1.0", "--memory", "256m",
                "--pids-limit", "64",
                "--workdir", "/work",
                "--read-only",
                "--tmpfs", "/work:rw,size=64m",
                "--tmpfs", "/tmp:rw,size=64m,noexec",
                "-v", f"{src_ro}:/src:ro",
                "-v", f"{input_ro}:/input:ro",
                image, *command]
    
    
    def docker_cp(container: str, src_path: str, host_dir: str) -> None:
        """Copy container outputs to host_dir (bounded by tmpfs size + caps)."""
        proc = subprocess.run(["docker", "cp", f"{container}:{src_path}",
                               host_dir], capture_output=True, timeout=60)
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            raise ToolDeniedError(
                "tool_error",
                f"output collection failed: "
                f"{(proc.stderr or b'')[:300].decode(errors='replace')}")
    
    
    def docker_rm(container: str) -> None:
        subprocess.run(["docker", "rm", "-f", container], capture_output=True,
                       timeout=30)
    
    
    def _popen_bounded(cmd: list[str], timeout_s: float,
                       cancelled) -> tuple[int, str, str]:
        """Run cmd, streaming stdout/stderr with caps while it runs.
    
        Returns (returncode, stdout_tail, stderr_tail). Raises
        subprocess.TimeoutExpired on timeout; checks `cancelled` while polling.
        """
        proc = subprocess.Popen(cmd, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
                                stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
        out_chunks: list[bytes] = []
        err_chunks: list[bytes] = []
        out_len = 0
        err_len = 0
    
        def _drain(stream, chunks: list[bytes], cap: int, counter: str):
            nonlocal out_len, err_len
            while True:
                data = stream.read(65536)
                if not data:
                    break
                chunks.append(data)
                if counter == "out":
                    out_len += len(data)

    // Home identity binding (portable, pure, UI-agnostic).
    //
    // Threat addressed: local profile switching (demo household profiles) must
    // never relabel or reveal another home user's cached private data. In home
    // mode, displayed conversations are bound to the authenticated paired user
    // (from the enrollment/session lookup), not to the selected demo profile.
    // Demo mode keeps profile switching fully functional.
    //
    // Rules enforced by these helpers and their MeContext integration:
    // - Home-mode visibility requires a resolved identity; before the enrollment
    //   is known (e.g. right after restart) no home conversation is shown, so no
    //   previous-user data can flash.
    // - Any user/device/installation/endpoint change (re-enrollment, logout,
    //   revocation) drops home-mode conversations, links, tasks, and pending
    //   state. Demo state is never wiped by this path (no blanket storage clear).
    
    export interface IdentityTuple {
      userId: string;
      deviceId: string;
      installationId: string;
      homeBaseUrl: string;
    }
    
    export interface ConversationRef {
      id: string;
      profileId?: string;
      assistantMode?: 'demo' | 'home';
    }
    
    export interface HomeLinkRef {
      homeId: string;
      homeOwner?: string;
      requestKey?: string;
    }
    
    export interface VisibleOptions {
      mode: 'demo' | 'home';
      activeProfileId: string;
      homeUserId: string | null;
      identityResolved: boolean;
    }
    
    /**
     * Which conversations the UI may display. Home mode ignores the demo
     * profile entirely: only conversations linked to the authenticated home
     * user are visible, and nothing is visible until the identity resolves.
     */
    export function visibleConversations<T extends ConversationRef>(
      conversations: T[],
      links: Record<string, HomeLinkRef>,
      options: VisibleOptions,
    ): T[] {
      if (options.mode === 'demo') {
        return conversations.filter(
          (c) =>
            (c.assistantMode ?? 'demo') === 'demo' &&
            (c.profileId === undefined || c.profileId === options.activeProfileId),
        );
      }
      if (!options.identityResolved || !options.homeUserId) return [];
      return conversations.filter(
        (c) =>
          (c.assistantMode ?? 'demo') === 'home' &&
          links[c.id]?.homeId &&
          links[c.id]?.homeOwner === options.homeUserId,
      );
    }
    
    export interface ReconcileResult {
      keepConversationIds: Set<string>;
      droppedLocalIds: string[];
      links: Record<string, HomeLinkRef>;
    }
    
    /**
     * Re-scope cached state on enrollment change. Any tuple change (user,
     * device, installation, endpoint) or logout (next === null) drops every
     * home-mode conversation and link; demo conversations are untouched.
     * Callers must additionally drop per-conversation UI state (tasks, typing,
     * errors, pending requests) for `droppedLocalIds`.
     */
    export function reconcileOnEnrollmentChange<T extends ConversationRef>(
      prev: IdentityTuple | null,
      next: IdentityTuple | null,
      conversations: T[],
      links: Record<string, HomeLinkRef>,
    ): ReconcileResult {
      const changed =
        (prev === null) !== (next === null) ||
        (prev !== null &&
          next !== null &&
          (prev.userId !== next.userId ||
            prev.deviceId !== next.deviceId ||
            prev.installationId !== next.installationId ||
            prev.homeBaseUrl !== next.homeBaseUrl));
      if (!changed) {
        return {
          keepConversationIds: new Set(conversations.map((c) => c.id)),
          droppedLocalIds: [],
          links,
        };
      }
      const droppedLocalIds: string[] = [];
      const nextLinks: Record<string, HomeLinkRef> = {};
      const keepConversationIds = new Set<string>();
      for (const c of conversations) {
        if ((c.assistantMode ?? 'demo') === 'home') {
          droppedLocalIds.push(c.id);
        } else {
          keepConversationIds.add(c.id);
          if (links[c.id]) nextLinks[c.id] = links[c.id]!;
        }
      }
      return { keepConversationIds, droppedLocalIds, links: nextLinks };
    }
    
    /** Stamp the authenticated owner on a home link after a verified sync/send. */
    export function recordHomeOwner(
      links: Record<string, HomeLinkRef>,
      localId: string,
      ownerUserId: string,
    ): Record<string, HomeLinkRef> {
      const existing = links[localId];
      if (!existing) return links;
      return { ...links, [localId]: { ...existing, homeOwner: ownerUserId } };
    }
    
    /**
     * Endpoint rotation guard: a backend-discovered endpoint may only rebind the
     * client when the live home's installation identity matches the registered
     * one. Missing or mismatched identities refuse — never silently pair a
     * different home.
     */
    export function verifyEndpointIdentity(
      recordedInstallationId: string | undefined | null,
      observedInstallationId: string | undefined | null,
    ): boolean {
      if (!recordedInstallationId || !observedInstallationId) return false;
      return recordedInstallationId === observedInstallationId;
    }
    }
    
    /** Message history cache: AsyncStorage, never for secrets. */
    export function createCacheStorage() {
      return createAsyncStorageCacheAdapter(AsyncStorage);
    }
    
    /** In-memory fallbacks for tests and the web preview (no pairing on web). */
    export function createMemoryStorages() {
      return {
        secure: createMemorySecureStorage(),
        cache: createMemoryCacheStorage(),
      };
    }
    
    export function createHomeClient(secure?: SecureStorage) {
      const secretStore = secure ?? createSecureStorage();
      return new PairedHomeClient(secretStore, createCacheStorage(), {
        allowInsecureLoopback: __DEV__,
      });
    }
    
    export function createBackendCoordinator(secure?: SecureStorage) {
      const secretStore = secure ?? createSecureStorage();
      return new BackendCoordinator(secretStore, {
        allowInsecureLoopback: __DEV__,
      });
    }
    
    export function isSecureStoreAvailable(): Promise<boolean> {
      if (typeof SecureStore.isAvailableAsync !== 'function') {
        return Promise.resolve(false);
      }
      return SecureStore.isAvailableAsync().catch(() => false);
    }

    """Human-in-the-loop tools on real harness interrupt semantics.
    
    `ask_user` pauses the LangGraph run with a `waiting_input` payload;
    `request_approval` pauses it with an `awaiting_approval` payload. Both
    resume through the persisted SqliteSaver checkpoint via Command(resume=...),
    so already-completed tool effects are never replayed. Decisions are bound
    to the exact pending action/args hash — verified here AND in the bridge.
    """
    from __future__ import annotations
    
    import hashlib
    import json
    from typing import Any
    
    from langchain_core.tools import tool
    from langgraph.types import interrupt
    
    from ..errors import ToolDeniedError
    
    
    def args_hash(args: dict) -> str:
        canonical = json.dumps(args or {}, sort_keys=True,
                               ensure_ascii=True, separators=(",", ":"))
        return hashlib.sha256(canonical.encode()).hexdigest()
    
    
    def make_interact_tools(run_id: str) -> list[Any]:
        @tool("ask_user")
        def ask_user(id: str, prompt: str) -> str:
            """Ask the user a question; resumes with their answer. Args: id, prompt."""
            payload = {"kind": "waiting_input", "id": id, "prompt": prompt,
                       "run_id": run_id}
            resume = interrupt(payload)
            if not isinstance(resume, dict) or not resume.get("answer"):
                raise ToolDeniedError("invalid_request",
                                      "resume missing answer for "
                                      f"{id!r}")
            return f"user answered: {resume['answer']}"[:2000]
    
        @tool("request_approval")
        def request_approval(id: str, action: str, params: dict | None = None,
                             reason: str = "") -> str:
            """Propose a gated action; resumes with the decision. Args: id, action, params, reason."""
            params = params or {}
            payload = {"kind": "awaiting_approval", "id": id, "action": action,
                       "args": params, "args_hash": args_hash(params),
                       "reason": reason, "run_id": run_id}
            resume = interrupt(payload)
            if not isinstance(resume, dict):
                raise ToolDeniedError("invalid_request",
                                      "resume missing decision")
            if resume.get("args_hash") != payload["args_hash"]:
                raise ToolDeniedError("invalid_request",
                                      "approval args changed since proposal")
            if resume.get("decision") != "approve":
                raise ToolDeniedError("approval_rejected",
                                      f"approval {id!r} rejected by user")
            return f"approved: {action}"
    
        return [ask_user, request_approval]
    """Agent loop owned by the maintained LangGraph prebuilt ReAct harness.
    
    `build_agent` wires exactly the brokered Me tools — no framework default
    filesystem/shell/subagent tools — into `create_react_agent`. The model
    (either a maintained chat adapter or the test-only fixture stub) drives
    standard tool-call round trips; this module contains no custom planner,
    no manual /chat/completions parsing, and no parallel task scheduler.
    """
    from __future__ import annotations
    
    import threading
    from typing import Any
    
    from langgraph.prebuilt import create_react_agent
    
    from .models import FixtureChatModel
    from .tools.animate import make_animate_tools
    from .tools.exec import make_exec_tools
    from .tools.files import make_files_tools
    from .tools.interact import make_interact_tools
    from .tools.web import make_web_tools
    from .workspace import Workspace
    
    SYSTEM_PROMPT = """You are Me, a home agent. You act ONLY through the tools
    provided by the home: scoped files, gated web fetch/browser, sandboxed
    code execution, animation building, and explicit user questions/approvals.
    Rules:
    - Never claim to have done work you did not do via tools; never fabricate
      file contents, fetch results, renders, or approvals.
    - Stay inside the granted capabilities. If a tool reports a denial or
      error you cannot recover from, end your reply with exactly:
      RUN-FAILED <code>: <message>
      using the code from the tool error.
    - Keep replies short; the home delivers your final text and artifacts.
    """
    
    EXPECTED_TOOL_NAMES = sorted([
        "files_read", "files_list", "files_write",
        "web_fetch", "browser_open",
        "run_code",
        "animation_build",
        "ask_user", "request_approval",
    ])
    
    
    class RunTools:
        """Per-run broker state shared by tool closures (no global state)."""
    
        def __init__(self, run_id: str, user_id: str, conversation_id: str,
                     cancelled: threading.Event) -> None:
            self.run_id = run_id
            self.user_id = user_id
            self.conversation_id = conversation_id
            self.cancelled = cancelled
            self.artifacts: list[dict] = []
    
        def record_artifact(self, path: str, data: bytes) -> None:
            import hashlib
            self.artifacts.append({
                "path": path, "bytes": len(data),
                "sha256": hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()})
    
    
    def build_tools(ws: Workspace, capabilities: dict, ctx: RunTools
                    ) -> list[Any]:
        tools = []
        tools += make_files_tools(ws, capabilities, ctx.record_artifact)
        tools += make_web_tools(ws, capabilities, ctx.record_artifact)
        tools += make_exec_tools(ws, capabilities, ctx.run_id,
                                 ctx.record_artifact, ctx.cancelled)
        tools += make_animate_tools(ws, capabilities, ctx.record_artifact)
        tools += make_interact_tools(ctx.run_id)
        names = sorted(t.name for t in tools)
        assert names == EXPECTED_TOOL_NAMES, f"tool allowlist drift: {names}"
        return tools
    
    
    def build_agent(model, tools: list[Any], checkpointer=None):
        """Compile the maintained prebuilt ReAct agent (harness-owned loop)."""
        scoped_prompt = (f"{SYSTEM_PROMPT}\n"
                         f"[run context: user and conversation are labelled by "
                         f"the home; only workspace files and supplied context "
                         f"are visible]")
        return create_react_agent(model, tools, prompt=scoped_prompt,
                                  checkpointer=checkpointer)
    
    
    def is_fixture_model(model) -> bool:
        return isinstance(model, FixtureChatModel)

    ## End-to-end with the home service
    
    The Node home service (`infra-server`) spawns this runtime per task; see
    the authoritative operator runbook at
    [`infra-server/docs/end-to-end-runbook.md`](../infra-server/docs/end-to-end-runbook.md)
    (§2 fixture demo, §6 exact per-repo commands, §7 live-model coordination).
    Sibling slice status at packaging time: R4 network/disk review, H5
    shutdown/artifacts, F3 phone identity/polling, S3 setup env/tunnel, and B3
    strict OIDC were still finishing — this README claims none of them.
    No full-production, native-app, or interactive-browser-automation claims.
    
    ## Product architecture and reuse work
    
    The agent executes on the user's separate home computer alongside `infra-server`,
    which hosts household data and multiple users/conversations. `backend-server`
    coordinates accounts and home access; setup should provision a protected tunnel
    endpoint and one-time phone enrollment. Direct versus relayed private traffic
    remains a transport decision. `setup-infra` installs and maintains the home environment.
    
    Start with [product architecture](docs/product-architecture.md), the
    [whole-product delivery plan](docs/product-delivery-plan.md), the
    [reuse audit](docs/reuse-audit.md), and the implemented
    [runtime bridge contract](docs/runtime-bridge-v1.md).

    ## 8. Implemented limitations (concrete)
    
    - Single-host SQLite (WAL); no replication, quotas, or hosted relay/buffer.
    - Pairing invitation + device secret travel as JSON bodies: safe on loopback
      only; LAN/WAN needs the provisioned protected endpoint (not implemented).
    - Sessions are opaque bearer tokens re-issued via device credential; no
      refresh rotation beyond re-issue.
    - Revocation is enforced per home request; offline-backend and edge-credential
      propagation windows are not handled.
    - Approval expiry uses far-future action TTLs; no administrative expiry UX.
    - Fair scheduling beyond the reused worker's 3-in-flight cap is out of scope.
    - Browser/mp4 prerequisites report honestly via the bridge; provisioning is
      S1's job. Fixture runs prove the subprocess path only — never model quality.

    export async function withDeadline(promise, ms) {

        child.once('exit', () => resolve(true));
      });
      try {

        return { outcome: 'already' };

      if (!(await withDeadline(exited, termGraceMs)).timedOut) return { outcome: 'term' };
      if (child.exitCode !== null || child.signalCode !== null) return { outcome: 'term' };

        child.kill('SIGKILL');
      } catch {
        return { outcome: 'already' };

            eligible.push(record);

    // Artifact ingest (H5). The declared path is untrusted runtime output, so
    // every step is defensive: lexical containment first, then realpath
    // containment (resolves intermediate and final symlinks — a link pointing at
    // another household user's workspace fails here), then open with O_NOFOLLOW
    // (a swapped-in final symlink fails instead of being followed), fstat type
    // and size checks BEFORE any read, and a bounded exact-size read loop.
    // Residual TOCTOU between realpath and open is documented: the only writer is
    // the task's own runtime inside its 0700 workspace, and O_NOFOLLOW + isFile +
    // size-first + bounded read close the practical holes.

      const maxTotalBytes = limits.maxTotalBytes ?? ARTIFACT_MAX_TOTAL_BYTES;

        if (error?.code === 'ELOOP') {

        def _drain(stream, chunks: list[bytes], cap: int, counter: str):
            nonlocal out_len, err_len
            while True:
                data = stream.read(65536)
                if not data:
                    break
                chunks.append(data)
                if counter == "out":
                    out_len += len(data)
                else:
                    err_len += len(data)
                # Drop oldest chunks past the cap (bounded memory).
                total = sum(len(c) for c in chunks)
                while total > cap and len(chunks) > 1:
                    total -= len(chunks.pop(0))

                                daemon=True)
        terr = threading.Thread(target=_drain,
                                args=(proc.stderr, err_chunks, STDERR_CAP, "err"),

    """Workspace jail: every file/code/artifact path stays inside the run workspace."""
    from __future__ import annotations
    
    from pathlib import Path
    
    
    class WorkspaceDenied(Exception):
        pass
    
    
    class Workspace:
        def __init__(self, root: str | Path) -> None:
            p = Path(root)
            if not p.is_absolute():
                raise WorkspaceDenied(f"workspace must be absolute: {root!r}")
            if not p.is_dir():
                raise WorkspaceDenied(f"workspace does not exist: {root!r}")
            self.root = p.resolve()
    
        def resolve(self, rel: str) -> Path:
            if not rel or not isinstance(rel, str):
                raise WorkspaceDenied("path must be a non-empty string")
            candidate = (self.root / rel).resolve()
            try:
                candidate.relative_to(self.root)
            except ValueError:
                raise WorkspaceDenied(f"path escapes workspace: {rel!r}")
            return candidate
    
        def read_text(self, rel: str, max_bytes: int = 1_000_000) -> str:
            target = self.resolve(rel)
            if not target.is_file():
                raise WorkspaceDenied(f"not a file: {rel!r}")
            data = target.read_bytes()[:max_bytes]
            return data.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    
        def list_dir(self, rel: str = ".", limit: int = 200) -> list[str]:
            target = self.resolve(rel)
            if not target.is_dir():
                raise WorkspaceDenied(f"not a directory: {rel!r}")
            return sorted(
                p.relative_to(self.root).as_posix()
                for p in list(target.iterdir())[:limit]
            )
    
        def write_bytes(self, rel: str, data: bytes) -> Path:
            target = self.resolve(rel)
            target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            target.write_bytes(data)
            return target
    
        def ensure_dirs(self, *names: str) -> None:
            for name in names:
                d = self.resolve(name)
                d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    
        def relative(self, path: Path) -> str:
            return path.resolve().relative_to(self.root).as_posix()

    """Scoped file tools: every action requires the `files` capability and the
    workspace jail. Read results are returned to the harness so the model can
    reason over real content across turns."""
    from __future__ import annotations
    
    from typing import Any
    
    from langchain_core.tools import tool
    
    from ..errors import ToolDeniedError
    from ..workspace import Workspace, WorkspaceDenied
    
    
    def make_files_tools(ws: Workspace, capabilities: dict,
                         record_artifact) -> list[Any]:
        if not isinstance(capabilities, dict):
            capabilities = {}
    
        def _require() -> None:
            if not capabilities.get("files"):
                raise ToolDeniedError("capability_denied", "files not granted")
    
        @tool("files_read")
        def files_read(path: str) -> str:
            """Read a UTF-8 text file inside the run workspace. Args: path."""
            _require()
            try:
                return ws.read_text(path)
            except WorkspaceDenied as exc:
                raise ToolDeniedError("workspace_denied", str(exc)) from exc
    
        @tool("files_list")
        def files_list(path: str = ".") -> str:
            """List workspace-relative entries under a directory. Args: path."""
            _require()
            try:
                items = ws.list_dir(path)
            except WorkspaceDenied as exc:
                raise ToolDeniedError("workspace_denied", str(exc)) from exc
            return "\n".join(items) if items else "(empty)"
    
        @tool("files_write")
        def files_write(path: str, content: str) -> str:
            """Write content to a workspace-relative path. Args: path, content."""
            _require()
            try:
                target = ws.write_bytes(path, content.encode("utf-8"))
            except WorkspaceDenied as exc:
                raise ToolDeniedError("workspace_denied", str(exc)) from exc
            record_artifact(ws.relative(target),
                            content.encode("utf-8"))
            return f"wrote {ws.relative(target)} ({len(content)} chars)"
    
        return [files_read, files_list, files_write]

    # --- service unit generation (files only, never installed) ----------------------
    
    def service_command(node_bin: str, entrypoint: Path, cfg: dict) -> tuple[list, dict, str]:
        """The exact managed command + env + workdir shared by start and service units.
    
        Returns (argv, env-delta, workdir). Env excludes secrets: generated unit
        files must never bake in ME_RUNTIME_MODEL_API_KEY; if the operator needs a
        remote model under a service manager they export the key in that service
        context themselves (warned at generation time).
        """
        db_path = cfg["service"]["db_path"]
        host, port = cfg["service"]["host"], int(cfg["service"]["port"])
        flags = me_setup.node_args_for(node_bin, entrypoint)[1:]
        argv = [node_bin, *flags, str(entrypoint), "start",
                f"--db={db_path}", f"--host={host}", f"--port={port}"]
        # Checkout root: entrypoint is <checkout>/src/cli.mjs. (Triple-parent
        # would land on the checkout's PARENT; the service and its relative
        # paths belong to the checkout itself.)
        workdir = str(entrypoint.parent.parent)
        env = {"HOME_DB": str(db_path), "HOME_HOST": host, "HOME_PORT": str(port)}
        env.update(build_home_env(cfg))
        for secret in RUNTIME_SECRET_ALLOWLIST:
            env.pop(secret, None)
        return argv, env, workdir

    def build_home_env(cfg: dict) -> dict:
        """Build the trusted home-service environment from generated config.
    
        Emits exactly the keys H3's runtime-config.mjs reads (verified read-only):
        ME_RUNTIME_ARGV (JSON array, space-safe) + ME_RUNTIME_CWD, HOME_MODEL_*,
        HOME_ALLOW_FIXTURE_MODEL, ME_RUNTIME_ALLOW_REMOTE, HOME_CAP_*, and
        ME_RUNTIME_ALLOW_CODE_EXEC. Absent/false host flags are omitted (H3 treats
        absent as false). Secret values are inherited from the operator's own
        environment only when present there, and are never persisted by setup.
        """
        env: dict[str, str] = {}
        bridge = cfg.get("runtime_bridge", {}) or {}
        if bridge.get("status") == "importable" and bridge.get("python"):
            env["ME_RUNTIME_ARGV"] = json.dumps([bridge["python"], "-m", "me_runtime.bridge"])

                env["ME_RUNTIME_CWD"] = bridge["import_cwd"]
        models = cfg.get("models", {}) or {}
        provider = str(models.get("provider", "local") or "local")
        env["HOME_MODEL_PROVIDER"] = provider
        if models.get("name"):
            env["HOME_MODEL_NAME"] = str(models["name"])
        if provider == "fixture":
            if models.get("allow_fixture"):
                env["HOME_ALLOW_FIXTURE_MODEL"] = "1"
        else:
            if models.get("endpoint"):
                env["HOME_MODEL_ENDPOINT"] = str(models["endpoint"])

    def make_web_tools(ws, capabilities: dict, record_artifact,
                       run_id: str = "", user_id: str = "",
                       conversation_id: str = "", cancelled=None) -> list[Any]:
        allowlist = capabilities.get("network_egress_allowlist", []) or []
    
        def _require_cap(name: str) -> None:
            if not capabilities.get(name):
                raise ToolDeniedError("capability_denied", f"{name} not granted")
    
        @tool("web_fetch")
        def web_fetch(url: str) -> str:
            """Fetch an allowlisted URL through the vetted broker. Args: url."""
            _require_cap("web_fetch")
            status, final_url, text = broker_fetch(url, allowlist)
            return f"[{status} {final_url}]\n{text[:8000]}"
    
        @tool("browser_open")
        def browser_open(url: str = "", session_id: str = "",
                         actions: list | str | None = None) -> str:
            """Isolated interactive browser (Docker-only, approval-gated writes).
    
            Requires browser + web_fetch. The page runs in a dedicated
            `--network none` container; every HTTP request is fulfilled via the
            vetted host broker (allowlist, pinned DNS/TLS, bounded). Returns
            real URL/title/body/actionable elements for iterative decisions.
            Readonly open/scroll/screenshot need no approval; click/fill/press
            pause with `awaiting_approval` (exact URL/action/target/value +
            page/target fingerprint) and execute only after approve, never on
            reject/stale/replay. Background POSTs are blocked until the
            approved window. Args: url (optional), session_id (optional),
            actions (optional list of {op,target,text,key,direction,pixels}).
            """
            from langgraph.types import interrupt as _interrupt
            from .browser_host import BrowserManager
            from . import browser_protocol as _proto
            from .interact import args_hash as _args_hash
    
            _require_cap("browser")
            _require_cap("web_fetch")
            clean = _parse_actions_arg(actions)
            mgr = BrowserManager(ws, capabilities, run_id or "norun",
                                 user_id or "nouser",
                                 conversation_id or "noconv",
                                 record_artifact, cancelled)
            needs_write = any(a.get("op") not in _proto.READONLY_ACT_OPS
                              for a in clean)
            try:
                if not clean:
                    if url and not session_id:
                        sid, snap = mgr.open(url, "")
                        return _format_snapshot(sid, snap)
                    if session_id and not url:
                        snap = mgr.snapshot(session_id)
                        return _format_snapshot(session_id, snap)
                    if url and session_id:
                        sid, snap = mgr.open(url, session_id)
                        return _format_snapshot(sid, snap)
                    if session_id and session_id.strip().lower() in (

                if url and not session_id:
                    sid, snap_before = mgr.open(url, "")
                elif session_id and not url:

                    snap_before = mgr.snapshot(sid)
                elif url and session_id:
                    sid, snap_before = mgr.open(url, session_id)
                    sid = sid
                else:

                                          "actions need a url or session_id")

    """Host controller for the isolated interactive browser.
    
    Production path is Docker ONLY: one `docker run -i` container per browser
    session with `--network none`, unprivileged uid, cap-drop, no-new-privs,
    read-only root, tmpfs caps, and a read-only worker-code mount. The worker
    has no NIC; every page request is fulfilled here via the vetted broker
    (`broker_fetch_raw`: allowlist + pinned DNS/TLS, per-hop validation,
    credential-strip on cross-origin redirect, bounded sizes, no proxy/curlrc).
    GET/HEAD are allowed by default; any other method is blocked unless the
    caller holds an approved-action window (`allow_write=True`).
    
    Test seam: `ME_RUNTIME_BROWSER_TEST_DIRECT=1` spawns the worker directly
    with the host system Chrome for synthetic harness smoke ONLY. Production
    never falls back to host Chrome: without Docker + provisioned image the
    tool fails closed with `prerequisite_missing`.
    """
    from __future__ import annotations
    
    import base64
    import json
    import os
    import re
    import select
    import shutil
    import subprocess
    import threading
    import time
    from pathlib import Path
    from typing import Any
    
    from ..errors import ToolDeniedError
    from ..workspace import Workspace
    from . import browser_protocol as proto
    from .web import broker_fetch_raw
    
    BROWSER_IMAGE_ENV = "ME_RUNTIME_DOCKER_IMAGE_BROWSER"
    DEFAULT_BROWSER_IMAGE = "me-browser-playwright:v1.49.1"
    WORKER_FILENAME = "browser_worker.py"
    CMD_TIMEOUT_S = 60.0
    
    _owned_lock = threading.Lock()
    _owned: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
    _managers_lock = threading.Lock()
    _managers: dict[str, list] = {}
    
    
    def register_manager(run_id: str, mgr) -> None:
        with _managers_lock:
            _managers.setdefault(run_id, []).append(mgr)
    
    
    def close_managers_for_run(run_id: str) -> None:
        with _managers_lock:
            mgrs = _managers.pop(run_id, [])
        for m in mgrs:
            try:
                m.close_all()
            except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
                pass
    
    
    def sanitize_name(run_id: str) -> str:
        return re.sub(r"[^a-zA-Z0-9_.-]", "-", run_id)[:32]
    
    
    def docker_available() -> bool:
        return shutil.which("docker") is not None
    
    
    def image_present(image: str) -> bool:
        try:
            r = subprocess.run(["docker", "image", "inspect", image],
                               capture_output=True, timeout=30)
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
            return False
        return r.returncode == 0
    
    
    def browser_container_name(run_id: str, session_tag: str) -> str:
        return f"me-br-{sanitize_name(run_id)}-{re.sub(r'[^a-zA-Z0-9_.-]', '-', session_tag)[:16]}"
    
    
    def _register(run_id: str, cname: str) -> None:
        with _owned_lock:
            _owned.setdefault(run_id, set()).add(cname)
    
    
    def _unregister(run_id: str, cname: str) -> None:
        with _owned_lock:
            s = _owned.get(run_id)
            if s is not None:
                s.discard(cname)
    
    
    def kill_run_browser_containers(run_id: str) -> None:
        """Best-effort cancel cleanup: kill + remove owned browser containers."""
        if not docker_available():
            return
        with _owned_lock:
            names = sorted(_owned.get(run_id, set()))
        for name in names:
            try:
                subprocess.run(["docker", "kill", name], capture_output=True,
                               timeout=15)
            except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
                pass
            try:
                subprocess.run(["docker", "rm", "-f", name], capture_output=True,
                               timeout=15)
            except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
                pass
    
    
    def build_browser_docker_cmd(image: str, cname: str,
                                 worker_dir_ro: str) -> list[str]:
        """Locked-down container invocation (no NIC, no writable host mounts)."""
        return ["docker", "run", "-i", "--rm", "--pull", "never",
                "--name", cname,
                "--network", "none",
                "--user", "65532:65532",
                "--cap-drop", "ALL",
                "--security-opt", "no-new-privileges",
                "--cpus", "1.0", "--memory", "512m",
                "--pids-limit", "128",
                "--read-only",
                "--tmpfs", "/tmp:rw,size=256m",
                "-e", "HOME=/tmp",
                "--workdir", "/tmp",
                "-v", f"{worker_dir_ro}:/worker:ro",
                image, "python", "/worker/browser_worker.py"]
    
    
    def worker_dir() -> str:
        return str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent)
    
    
    class _Proc:
        def __init__(self, popen: subprocess.Popen, cname: str,
                     run_id: str, direct: bool) -> None:
            self.popen = popen
            self.cname = cname
            self.run_id = run_id
            self.direct = direct
    
        def close(self) -> None:
            try:
                if self.popen.stdin:
                    try:
                        self.popen.stdin.close()
                    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
                        pass
            finally:
                try:
                    self.popen.wait(timeout=10)
                except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
                    try:
                        self.popen.kill()
                    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
                        pass
            if not self.direct:
                try:
                    subprocess.run(["docker", "rm", "-f", self.cname],
                                   capture_output=True, timeout=30)
                except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
                    pass
            _unregister(self.run_id, self.cname)
    
    
    class BrowserManager:
        """Per-bridge-process session manager (scoped to run/user/conversation)."""
    
        def __init__(self, ws: Workspace, capabilities: dict, run_id: str,

                     record_artifact, cancelled,
                     popen_factory=None) -> None:
    """Isolated-browser JSONL protocol (browser-worker-v1).
    
    Host <-> container worker speak bounded JSONL over stdio (`docker run -i`).
    The container has no NIC; every page HTTP request is intercepted in the
    worker and fulfilled via the host vetted broker. No arbitrary eval, no CDP,
    no host mounts; frames are size-bounded and actions per command are capped.
    """
    from __future__ import annotations
    
    import base64
    import hashlib
    import json
    
    PROTOCOL_VERSION = 1
    MAX_FRAME_BYTES = 2_000_000
    MAX_ACTIONS_PER_CMD = 8
    MAX_URL_LEN = 2048
    MAX_REF_LEN = 64
    MAX_TEXT_LEN = 4000
    MAX_KEY_LEN = 64
    MAX_BODY_TEXT = 8000
    MAX_ACTIONABLES = 50
    MAX_STORAGE_STATE_BYTES = 256_000
    SCREENSHOT_CAP_BYTES = 1_000_000
    
    HOST_OPS = ("open", "snapshot", "act", "screenshot", "close")
    ACT_OPS = ("click", "fill", "press", "scroll")

    def encode_frame(obj: dict) -> str:
        line = json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=True, separators=(",", ":"))
        if len(line.encode("utf-8")) > MAX_FRAME_BYTES:
            raise ValueError("frame exceeds bounded cap")
        return line
    
    
    def decode_frame(line: str) -> dict:
        if len(line.encode("utf-8")) > MAX_FRAME_BYTES:
            raise ValueError("inbound frame exceeds bounded cap")
        obj = json.loads(line)
        if not isinstance(obj, dict):
            raise ValueError("frame must be an object")
        return obj
    
    
    def validate_url(url: str) -> str:
        if not isinstance(url, str) or not url:
            raise ValueError("url must be a non-empty string")
        if len(url) > MAX_URL_LEN:
            raise ValueError("url too long; refused")
        return url
    
    
    def validate_actions(actions) -> list[dict]:
        if not isinstance(actions, list):
            raise ValueError("actions must be a list")
        if len(actions) > MAX_ACTIONS_PER_CMD:
            raise ValueError("too many actions; refused")
        clean: list[dict] = []
        for a in actions:
            if not isinstance(a, dict):
                raise ValueError("each action must be an object")
            op = a.get("op")
            if op not in ACT_OPS:
                raise ValueError(f"unsupported action op: {op!r}")
            target = a.get("target", "")
            if op in ("click", "fill"):
                if not isinstance(target, str) or not target:
                    raise ValueError(f"{op} needs a target ref")
                if len(target) > MAX_REF_LEN:
                    raise ValueError("target ref too long")
            if op == "fill":
                text = a.get("text", "")
                if not isinstance(text, str):
                    raise ValueError("fill text must be a string")
                if len(text) > MAX_TEXT_LEN:
                    raise ValueError("fill text too long; refused")
                clean.append({"op": op, "target": target, "text": text})
            elif op == "click":
                clean.append({"op": op, "target": target})
            elif op == "press":
                key = a.get("key", "")
                if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
                    raise ValueError("press needs a key")
                if len(key) > MAX_KEY_LEN:
                    raise ValueError("press key too long")
                t = a.get("target", "")
                if t and (not isinstance(t, str) or len(t) > MAX_REF_LEN):
                    raise ValueError("bad press target")
                clean.append({"op": op, "key": key, "target": t})
            elif op == "scroll":
                direction = a.get("direction", "down")
                if direction not in ("up", "down"):
                    raise ValueError("scroll direction must be up/down")
                try:
                    pixels = int(a.get("pixels", 800))
                except (TypeError, ValueError):
                    raise ValueError("scroll pixels must be an integer")
                pixels = max(100, min(pixels, 4000))
                clean.append({"op": op, "direction": direction,
                              "pixels": pixels})
        return clean
    
    
    def page_fingerprint(url: str, title: str, body_text: str) -> str:
        h = hashlib.sha256()
        h.update((url or "").encode("utf-8", errors="replace"))
        h.update(b"\n")
        h.update((title or "").encode("utf-8", errors="replace"))
        h.update(b"\n")
        h.update(hashlib.sha256(
            (body_text or "").encode("utf-8", errors="replace")).digest())
        return h.hexdigest()[:32]
    
    
    def target_fingerprint(page_fp: str, target: str) -> str:
        h = hashlib.sha256()
        h.update(page_fp.encode())
        h.update(b"\n")
        h.update((target or "").encode("utf-8", errors="replace"))
        return h.hexdigest()[:32]

        return base64.b64encode(data).decode("ascii")
