    # task-rpc-v1 — home subtask delegation RPC (home authoritative, for R8 runtime)
    
    Version: `task-rpc-v1` · Status: implemented on home side (H6) · Owner: `infra-server`
    Consumer: `agentic-framework` R8 worker (Python `me_runtime.bridge` successor).
    
    Home is the single durable authority: the reused upstream `TaskWorker`
    owns every claim/lease/settle. This RPC only creates normal task records
    through the same worker; there is no second job engine and no vendor patch.
    
    ## 1. Transport (stdin unchanged)
    
    - Node home spawns the bridge with `stdio: ['pipe','pipe','pipe','pipe']`
      and `env.ME_HOME_TASK_RPC_FD=3`.
    - Main stdin is still exactly one JSON object (`runtime-bridge-v1` request)
      read to EOF. The runtime must not change stdin framing.
    - fd 3 is a duplex JSONL stream owned by the child process (no auth secret:
      possession of the fd is the capability). Generated Docker code never
      inherits it (container has no home fds).
    - Legacy bridges that never open fd 3 are unaffected: home sees zero RPC
      requests and settles normally. Node `fixture-bridge.mjs` proves this.
    - Bounds (home-enforced, runtime must also bound its writer):
      `64 KiB` max RPC line, `512 KiB` max buffered without newline,
      `200` requests per run. Oversize/flooded input gets an error response or
      a destroyed pipe, never unbounded buffering. The pipe closes on run end,
      cancel, or child exit.
    
    ## 2. Envelope
    
    Request (runtime → home, `\n` terminated):
    
    ```json
    {"rpc":"task-rpc-v1","id":1,"method":"submit_child","params":{"key":"plan-1","request":"research X","title":"X","capabilities":{"files":true},"budgets":{"max_steps":4}}}
    {"rpc":"task-rpc-v1","id":2,"method":"list_children","params":{}}
    {"rpc":"task-rpc-v1","id":3,"method":"get_child","params":{"id":"task_..."}}
    ```
    
    Response (home → runtime):
    
    ```json
    {"rpc":"task-rpc-v1","id":1,"ok":true,"result":{"child":{"id":"task_...","status":"queued","parent_task_id":"task_...","root_task_id":"task_..."}}}
    {"rpc":"task-rpc-v1","id":2,"ok":true,"result":{"children":[{"id":"task_...","status":"succeeded"}]}}
    {"rpc":"task-rpc-v1","id":1,"ok":false,"error":{"code":"delegation_denied","message":"..."}}
    ```
    
    Error codes: `bad_request` (shape/validation), `capability_denied`
    (narrowing violation), `delegation_denied` (disabled/fanout/depth/root-count),
    `delegation_conflict` (same key, different payload), `not_found`
    (unknown child id), `wrong_state` (parent no longer running).
    
    ## 3. Methods
    
    ### `submit_child` — spawn one independent research subtask
    
    Params:
    
    - `key` (required, `1..128` chars): idempotency key scoped to
      `(parent_task_id, key)`. Same key + byte-identical
      `request/capabilities/budgets/title` hash returns the existing child
      (retry/resume safe). Same key + different hash is `409
      delegation_conflict`.
    - `request` (required, `1..8000` chars): child prompt.
    - `title` (optional, ≤200 chars).
    - `capabilities` (optional object): must narrow the parent. Every `true`
      must already be `true` on the parent; `network_egress_allowlist` must be a
      subset of the parent's. Strict booleans only; unknown keys rejected.
      No `model` field is accepted from the bridge or the phone — the home
      inherits `model` from the parent (trusted host selection).
    - `budgets` (optional object): each of `max_steps/max_wall_seconds/
      max_tool_calls` must be a positive int and `<=` the parent's value (and
      `<=` home maxima). This is per-run, not aggregated root accounting.
    
    Binding (home-enforced regardless of model):
    
    - `owner`, `conversation_id`, `model` inherit from the parent closure.
      Request `user_id/conversation_id/model/workspace/run_id` fields are never
      trusted and are not part of this RPC.
    - New child: `parent_task_id=parent`, `root_task_id=parent.root`,
      `depth=parent.depth+1`, same conversation (so existing phone
      `GET /v1/conversations/:id/tasks` lists children), independent workspace
      `tasks/<childId>`, independent `task_id`-namespaced approval IDs and
      artifact scope. No cross-owner/cross-conversation links possible;
      cycles impossible (child id is fresh).
    - Host bounds (small defaults, `0` disables spawning):
      `HOME_DELEGATION_MAX_FANOUT=5` per parent,
      `HOME_DELEGATION_MAX_DEPTH=2`,
      `HOME_DELEGATION_MAX_TASKS_PER_ROOT=25`.
      Exceeding any is `delegation_denied`. The runtime must not implement its
      own recursive bomb: if home denies, surface honestly and continue without
      that child.
    
    ### `list_children` — direct children of this parent only
    
    Returns `children[]` summaries (`id/status/parent_task_id/root_task_id/
    depth`). Never a global task lookup.
    
    ### `get_child` — one direct child only
    
    `params.id` must be a direct child of the calling parent and same owner;
    otherwise `not_found` (no oracle, no cross-task read).
    
    ## 4. Bridge result extension (`runtime-bridge-v1` compatible)
    
    New terminal `result.status`:
    
    - `waiting_children` with optional `children: [ids]` (or `child_ids`).
      Home verifies every declared id is a known direct child; unknown →
      `failed`. If no children exist → `failed`. If all children already
      terminal, home requeues immediately with `child_results` (no extra idle
      cycle). Otherwise the parent parks as `waiting_children` with
      `childIds` + `state.waitingChildren`.
    
    Completion policy (R8 must implement exactly this):
    
    1. Return `waiting_children` when pausing for delegated work. Do not return
       `completed` with active children — if you do, home holds the run as
       `waiting_children` anyway and withholds the conversation publish.
    2. A `completed` terminal publishes to the conversation **only** when zero
       active children remain. Active = any child in
       `queued/running/waiting_input/waiting_approval/waiting_children`.
    3. Wake resume is `op: resume` with the same `run_id/workspace` plus
       `child_results` (see §5). The harness checkpoint (`graph.db`/
       `pending.json`) continues; completed tool calls are never replayed.
       `child_results` are trusted home summaries, not user input.
    4. `waiting_input`/`awaiting_approval` parents may also have children.
       Children run independently; their settle never auto-resumes a human
       wait. Only `waiting_children` is woken by child settle.
    5. `failed`/`cancelled` terminals cascade-cancel own-descendants
       (owner-scoped BFS). Cancel via `POST /v1/tasks/:id/cancel` does the same.
    
    ## 5. Resume `child_results` shape (home → runtime on `op: resume`)
    
    ```json
    {
      "op": "resume",
      "run_id": "task_parent",
      "child_results": [
        {"id":"task_c1","status":"succeeded","output":"...≤2000 chars","artifacts":[{"id":"art_...","name":"output/x.md","sha256":"...","size":123}]},
        {"id":"task_c2","status":"failed","error":"...≤2000 chars"},
        {"id":"task_c3","status":"cancelled"}
      ]
    }
    ```
    
    Only short summaries + scoped artifact metadata. No workspace paths, no
    full logs. Private child logs stay home. The runtime aggregates these into
    its final output (LangGraph continue/checkpoint) and then returns a final
    `completed`/`failed`.
    
    ## 6. Wake guarantees (home-side, no LLM polling)
    
    - The worker's `settled` hook fires after every child settle. If the parent
      is `waiting_children` and every direct child is terminal
      (`succeeded/failed/cancelled`), home CAS-transitions the parent
      `waiting_children → queued` with `resume.childResults`.
    - Single-CAS wake: concurrent settling children race one CAS; exactly one
      wins, the other sees `queued` and does nothing. No duplicate resumes.
    - Startup reconciliation (`reconcileWaitingParents`) does the same CAS scan
      after `recoverInterrupted`. Restart fail-closes active (`running`) runs
      as `failed` (uncertain external effects, never replayed); waiting parents
      reconcile settled children (including newly-failed ones) without replaying
      completed tool calls. Queued children orphaned under a terminal
      failed/cancelled parent are cancelled closed.
    - `waiting_children` never occupies a worker in-flight slot, so parked
      parents cannot stall other jobs. The 3-in-flight cap still bounds
      concurrently running tasks (parent + children count while running).
    
    ## 7. What this RPC is not
    
    - No model override, no capability widening, no global task read, no cost
      aggregation. Budgets are per-run; fanout/depth/root-count bound recursion
      but do not claim root-cost accounting.
    - No fake primary planner: home never plans; the R8 agent loop (LangGraph
      prebuilt ReAct) owns planning. Fixture bridges prove transport only.
      have children; child settle never auto-resumes a human wait. Premature
      `completed` with active children is held as `waiting_children` (no
      conversation publish until truly final). Restart fail-closes `running`
      as today; `waiting_children` parents reconcile without replaying
      completed actions; orphans under failed parents cancel closed.
    - Explicit cancel cascade over own-descendants only (owner-scoped BFS,
      cycle-safe). Child ask/approval/cancel/artifacts reuse existing
      `task_id`-namespaced flows.
    - Views: `parent_task_id/root_task_id/depth/children[]/children_status[]/
      waiting_for` on task views; conversation task lists include children
      (same conversation). Budgets are per-run; fanout bounds recursion but
      there is no aggregated root-cost accounting. No primary-planner claim.
    
    ## For the consumers
    
    - `phone-app`: render `parent_task_id/root_task_id/children` when present;
      existing `GET /v1/conversations/:id/tasks` already lists children.
      `waiting_children` is a parked state like `waiting_input` (poll for
      `queued/running/succeeded`). No new auth.
    - `backend-server/setup-infra`: preserve SQLite + tasks root as before;
      optionally set the three `HOME_DELEGATION_*` vars (defaults apply).
    - `agentic-framework` R8: implement `docs/runtime-task-rpc-v1.md`
      verbatim — open fd from `ME_HOME_TASK_RPC_FD`, JSONL `submit_child`,
      return `waiting_children`, resume on `op: resume` with `child_results`,
      then final `completed`. Do not invent planning/scheduling outside the
      maintained LangGraph harness; do not widen caps; surface denials
      honestly. Docker code never inherits fd 3.
    
    ## What H6 does not claim
    
    - The current home fixture bridges prove transport/lifecycle only, not
      live-model delegation. Full runtime integration is R8's job against the
      published contract; this slice does not pretend the current Python
      runtime already delegates.
    - Single-host SQLite, loopback default, no quotas/backups beyond H2/H5.

    def do_restore(data_dir: Path, *, source: str, confirm_destructive: bool = False,
                   scope: str = "auto") -> int:
        if scope not in ("auto", "db", "full"):
            err(f"error: --scope must be auto, db, or full (got {scope!r})")
            return 2
        resolved = scope
        if resolved == "auto":
            low = str(source).lower()
            resolved = "full" if (low.endswith(".tar.gz") or low.endswith(".tgz")) else "db"
        else:
            low = str(source).lower()
            is_tar = low.endswith(".tar.gz") or low.endswith(".tgz")
            if resolved == "db" and is_tar:
                err("error: --scope db expects a SQLite snapshot (.sqlite), not a "
                    "full archive; re-run with --scope full")
                return 2
            if resolved == "full" and not is_tar:
                err("error: --scope full expects a full archive (.tar.gz); re-run with "
                    "--scope db for a SQLite snapshot")
                return 2
        if resolved == "full":
            return do_restore_full(data_dir, source=source,
                                   confirm_destructive=confirm_destructive)
        try:
            data_dir, cfg = load_cfg(data_dir)
        except me_setup.SetupError as exc:
            err(f"error: {exc}")
            return 2
        if not confirm_destructive:
            err("error: restore replaces the live home database; re-run with "
                "--confirm-destructive once you have a backup")
            return 2
        src = Path(source).expanduser()
        if not src.is_file():
            err(f"error: restore source not found: {src}")
        """Read-only integrity check for a runtime checkpoint SQLite file.
    
        Non-SQLite files pass (nothing to check); SQLite files must pass
        integrity_check. Never modifies.
        """
        try:
            with open(path, "rb") as f:
                magic = f.read(16)
        except OSError as exc:
            return False, f"unreadable: {exc}"
        if magic != b"SQLite format 3\0":
            return True, "not sqlite, skipped"
        try:
            with sqlite_conn(path, read_only=True, timeout=10) as conn:
                row = conn.execute("PRAGMA integrity_check").fetchone()
                if not row or row[0] != "ok":
                    return False, f"integrity_check failed: {row}"
        except sqlite3.Error as exc:
            return False, f"sqlite error: {exc}"
        return True, "ok"

            house_live = household_dir_for(cfg, data_dir)

    # Account auth v1 (phone login metadata + verification handoff)
    
    Status: implemented. Protocol `account-auth-v1`. This is the contract the
    phone worker (F7) implements against — backend is the source of truth for
    metadata shape, verification rules, and errors.
    
    Non-goals (explicit): the backend does NOT implement passwords, does NOT
    proxy provider credentials, and does NOT mint or refresh provider tokens.
    The phone performs PKCE directly against the trusted IdP with a maintained
    SDK (e.g. Expo `expo-auth-session`). The backend only (a) publishes public
    login metadata and (b) verifies the provider JWT access-token the phone
    presents. No chat payload storage or relay.
    
    ## Endpoints
    
    ### `GET /v1/auth/config` — public, no auth
    
    Returns how a phone must log in. No secrets are ever exposed (no client
    secrets, no token maps, no JWKS public/private keys).
    
    Dev mode (`authMode=dev`):
    
    ```json
    {
      "protocol": "account-auth-v1",
      "authMode": "dev",
      "devOnly": true,
      "oauthConfigured": false,
      "message": "Local-dev identity only. Sign in with a dev account token; no OAuth provider is configured and no browser login applies."
    }
    ```
    
    Hosted mode, ready (`200`):
    
    ```json
    {
      "protocol": "account-auth-v1",
      "authMode": "hosted",
      "issuer": "https://issuer.example.test",
      "audience": "me-backend-api",
      "clientId": "me-mobile-public-client",
      "scopes": ["openid", "profile", "email"],
      "redirectUris": ["myapp://auth/callback"],
      "appScheme": "myapp",
      "extraAudiences": ["extra-api-if-needed"],
      "expectedTokenUse": "access"
    }
    ```
    
    | Field | Meaning |
    | --- | --- |
    | `issuer` | Trusted HTTPS issuer. The backend verifies `iss` exactly. Loopback `http://` only in explicit test mode, never production. |
    | `audience` | API audience. The backend verifies `aud` contains this value. Provider JWT **access-tokens** are required with `aud` = this API audience. |
    | `clientId` | Public mobile client ID (no secret). MUST differ from `audience` so an ID token can never pass as an API access token. |
    | `scopes` | Minimal scope list to request (default `openid profile email`). |
    | `redirectUris` | Registered exact redirect allowlist. The phone MUST use one of these verbatim as the AuthSession redirect; arbitrary user-supplied redirects are never accepted. |
    | `appScheme` | Optional app scheme hint (e.g. `myapp`) matching the custom-scheme redirect. |
    | `extraAudiences` | Optional, only when the provider needs an extra `audience`/`resource` param. Controlled server config, never a phone-supplied value. |
    | `expectedTokenUse` | Optional, e.g. `access`. When set, the backend rejects tokens whose `token_use` differs (no ID-token fallback). |
    
    Hosted mode, metadata incomplete (`503`):
    
    ```json
    {
      "protocol": "account-auth-v1",
      "authMode": "hosted",
      "error": "configure_not_ready",
      "message": "Hosted auth is verifying tokens, but public login metadata is not configured ...",
      "issuer": "https://issuer.example.test",
      "audience": "me-backend-api"
    }
    ```
    
    Returned when `ME_BACKEND_OIDC_CLIENT_ID` or
    `ME_BACKEND_OIDC_REDIRECT_URIS` is missing. The operator must set them;
    the backend never fakes a provider. Token verification itself still works
    — only the public metadata is `503`.
    
    Errors: `503 configure_not_ready` (above). No `401` here (public route).
    
    ### `GET /v1/account` — authenticated
    
    Verifies the presented bearer credential with the current `jose` verifier
    and returns the stable server-derived accountId. Never trusts client body
    identity (there is no body contract; identity always comes from the
    credential).
    
    Dev: `Authorization: Bearer <dev-account-token>` → `200 { protocol,
    authMode: "dev", accountId }`.
    
    Hosted: `Authorization: Bearer <provider JWT access-token>` →
    
    ```json
    {
      "protocol": "account-auth-v1",
      "authMode": "hosted",
      "accountId": "acct_<32 hex>",
      "issuer": "https://issuer.example.test",
      "claims": { "email": "a@example.test", "name": "A", "preferred_username": "a" }
    }
    ```
    
    - `accountId` = `acct_<sha256("oidc-v1" || iss || sub)[0:32 hex]>`, stable
      across restarts, stateless.
    - `claims` is minimal and only present when the verified payload carries
      short-string `email`/`name`/`preferred_username` (+ boolean
      `email_verified`). Absent otherwise — callers MUST NOT require it.
    - An invalid JWT (wrong signature/issuer/audience, expired, missing
      `exp`/`sub`, `alg=none`, unknown `kid`, attacker `jku`/`x5u`, wrong
      `token_use`) is NOT an account login: `401 { error: "Account
      authorization required." }`. Same `401` for missing/garbage tokens.
    
    ## Verification rules (backend)
    
    - Maintained `jose` only. Algorithms: asymmetric allowlist (`RS*/PS*/ES*/EdDSA`);
      `HS*`/`none` rejected.
    - Key set: EITHER static JWKS (`ME_BACKEND_OIDC_JWKS[_FILE]`) OR fixed
      trusted JWKS HTTPS URL (`ME_BACKEND_OIDC_JWKS_URL`) via
      `jose.createRemoteJWKSet` with bounded fetch timeout (default 5s,
      `1000..15000` ms), 2s cooldown, 10-min cache — rotation-safe. Tests
      retain the static path; remote is opt-in server config.
    - No token-derived key URLs: `jku`/`x5u`/`jwk` headers are never honored;
      keys come only from server config. No phone-supplied URL is ever fetched.
    - `clockTolerance: 30s`; required claims `exp`, `sub`; `sub` non-empty ≤256 chars.
    - `aud` MUST be the API audience (not the clientId). `clientId !== audience`
      is enforced at startup.
    - Optional `ME_BACKEND_OIDC_EXPECT_TOKEN_USE` (e.g. `access`): when set,
      only tokens with matching `token_use` verify. ID tokens without it are
      rejected — there is no ID-token fallback.
    
    # task-rpc-v1 — home subtask delegation RPC (home authoritative, for R8 runtime)
    
    Version: `task-rpc-v1` · Status: implemented on home side (H6) · Owner: `infra-server`
    Consumer: `agentic-framework` R8 worker (Python `me_runtime.bridge` successor).
    
    Home is the single durable authority: the reused upstream `TaskWorker`
    owns every claim/lease/settle. This RPC only creates normal task records
    through the same worker; there is no second job engine and no vendor patch.
    
    ## 1. Transport (stdin unchanged)
    
    - Node home spawns the bridge with `stdio: ['pipe','pipe','pipe','pipe']`
      and `env.ME_HOME_TASK_RPC_FD=3`.
    - Main stdin is still exactly one JSON object (`runtime-bridge-v1` request)
      read to EOF. The runtime must not change stdin framing.
    - fd 3 is a duplex JSONL stream owned by the child process (no auth secret:
      possession of the fd is the capability). Generated Docker code never
      inherits it (container has no home fds).
    - Legacy bridges that never open fd 3 are unaffected: home sees zero RPC
      requests and settles normally. Node `fixture-bridge.mjs` proves this.
    - Bounds (home-enforced, runtime must also bound its writer):
      `64 KiB` max RPC line (UTF-8 bytes), `512 KiB` max buffered without
      newline, `200` requests per run, `32 KiB` max params object,
      `128 KiB` max response, `256 KiB` max pending socket writes.
      IDs must be short strings (`1..128` chars) or safe integers; methods
      `1..64` chars; params must be objects. The request budget is terminal:
      the 201st request gets one `delegation_denied` error and the pipe
      closes — a runaway runtime cannot wedge the home with unlimited errors.
      Oversize/flooded input closes the pipe, never unbounded buffering. The
      pipe closes on run end, cancel, lease takeover, or child exit. Split
      UTF-8 sequences across chunks are decoded safely; partial lines buffer
      until newline and batched lines parse in order. Error responses carry
      only `code` + short message — never request contents, credentials, or
      logs. Lease binding: every call re-validates the spawning lease
      (`status=running` + `leaseId` match + not aborted); a stale fd after a
      worker takeover is denied with `wrong_state`.
    
    ## 2. Envelope
    
    Request (runtime → home, `\n` terminated):
    
    ```json
    {"rpc":"task-rpc-v1","id":1,"method":"submit_child","params":{"key":"plan-1","request":"research X","title":"X","capabilities":{"files":true},"budgets":{"max_steps":4}}}
    {"rpc":"task-rpc-v1","id":2,"method":"list_children","params":{}}
    {"rpc":"task-rpc-v1","id":3,"method":"get_child","params":{"id":"task_..."}}
    ```
    
    Response (home → runtime):
    
    ```json
    {"rpc":"task-rpc-v1","id":1,"ok":true,"result":{"child":{"id":"task_...","status":"queued","parent_task_id":"task_...","root_task_id":"task_..."}}}
    {"rpc":"task-rpc-v1","id":2,"ok":true,"result":{"children":[{"id":"task_...","status":"succeeded"}]}}
    {"rpc":"task-rpc-v1","id":1,"ok":false,"error":{"code":"delegation_denied","message":"..."}}
    ```
    
    Error codes: `bad_request` (shape/validation), `capability_denied`
    (narrowing violation), `delegation_denied` (disabled/fanout/depth/root-count),
    `delegation_conflict` (same key, different payload), `not_found`
    (unknown child id), `wrong_state` (parent no longer running).

     * Trusted provider discovery: fetches the IdP metadata for the configured
     * issuer and refuses anything that is not the trusted issuer with HTTPS
     * endpoints (loopback http only when explicitly allowed for local dev).
     */
    export async function discoverTrustedProvider(
      issuer: string,
      allowInsecureLoopback: boolean,
    ): Promise<ProviderDiscovery> {
      let issuerUrl: URL;
      try {
        issuerUrl = new URL(issuer);
      } catch {
        throw new Error('The configured login issuer is invalid.');
      }
      const trusted =
        issuerUrl.protocol === 'https:' ||
        (allowInsecureLoopback && issuerUrl.protocol === 'http:' && isLoopbackHost(issuerUrl.hostname));
      if (!trusted) {
        throw new Error('The configured login issuer is not trusted.');
      }
      WebBrowser.maybeCompleteAuthSession();
      const discovery = (await AuthSession.fetchDiscoveryAsync(issuer)) as unknown as Record<
        string,
        string | undefined
      >;
      const authorizationEndpoint = typeof discovery['authorizationEndpoint'] === 'string'
        ? (discovery['authorizationEndpoint'] as string)
        : undefined;
      const tokenEndpoint = typeof discovery['tokenEndpoint'] === 'string'
        ? (discovery['tokenEndpoint'] as string)
        : undefined;
      const revocationEndpoint = typeof discovery['revocationEndpoint'] === 'string'
        ? (discovery['revocationEndpoint'] as string)
        : undefined;
      if (!authorizationEndpoint || !tokenEndpoint) {
        throw new Error('The login provider metadata is incomplete.');
      }
      if (
        !isTrustedHttpUrl(authorizationEndpoint, allowInsecureLoopback) ||
        !isTrustedHttpUrl(tokenEndpoint, allowInsecureLoopback) ||
        (revocationEndpoint && !isTrustedHttpUrl(revocationEndpoint, allowInsecureLoopback))
      ) {
        throw new Error('The login provider endpoints are not trusted.');
      }
      return { authorizationEndpoint, tokenEndpoint, ...(revocationEndpoint ? { revocationEndpoint } : {}) };
    }
    
    export interface PromptResult {
      code: string;
      redirectUri: string;
    }
    
    /**
     * Open the system browser for AuthorizationCode + PKCE. The SDK holds the
     * code verifier in memory only; this returns the authorization code for
     * direct IdP exchange. Throws on cancel/dismiss/error (no token fallback).
     */
    export async function promptAuthorizationCode(
      config: HostedAuthConfig,
      discovery: ProviderDiscovery,
      redirectUri: string,
    ): Promise<PromptResult> {
      WebBrowser.maybeCompleteAuthSession();
      const extraParams: Record<string, string> = { audience: config.audience };
      if (config.extraAudiences && config.extraAudiences.length > 0) {
        extraParams['resource'] = config.extraAudiences.join(' ');
      }
      const request = new AuthSession.AuthRequest({
        clientId: config.clientId,
        redirectUri,
        scopes: config.scopes,
        responseType: AuthSession.ResponseType.Code,
        usePKCE: true,
        extraParams,
      });
      const result = await request.promptAsync(
        { authorizationEndpoint: discovery.authorizationEndpoint },
        { showInRecents: true },
      );

    // Portable approval summarization + task-relationship parsing (pure, zero deps).
    //
    // F6: approval cards must be reviewable — action/summary/reason,
    // destination URL or selector/action sequence, expiry — never a blind
    // Approve/Reject pair. The H6 contract is not yet published, so this parses
    // defensively: known keys in camelCase and snake_case, unknown shapes fall
    // back to safe generic text. Nothing here performs I/O, opens URLs, or
    // renders HTML — callers render the returned strings as native Text.
    //
    // Privacy: sensitive arg values (password/token/secret/auth/...) are masked
    // by default. Callers show a bounded masked preview and reveal the full
    // (still masked for truly sensitive keys) detail only on explicit user
    // action. args_hash / effective_caps are optional technical metadata shown
    // only when useful, never required.
    
    export interface ApprovalSummary {
      /** Opaque server-issued approval id (use verbatim in decide calls). */
      id: string;
      /** What the home wants to do (e.g. "browser.open", "file.write"). */
      action: string;
      /** Human-readable one-line summary. */
      summary: string;
      /** Why the home needs approval, when provided. */
      reason?: string;
      /** Destination URL / target, when provided. Never auto-opened. */
      destination?: string;
      /** Element selector / target description, when provided. */
      selector?: string;
      /** Action sequence / plan steps, when provided (bounded). */
      steps: string[];
      /** Expiry label (raw server value rendered as text), when provided. */
      expiresAt?: string;
      /** Bounded masked args preview for the card. */
      argsPreview: string;
      /** True when any arg key looked sensitive (masked in preview). */
      hasSensitiveArgs: boolean;
      /** True when the approval carried an args object at all. */
      hasArgs: boolean;
      /** Optional integrity hash, shown only as technical metadata. */
      argsHash?: string;
      /** Optional effective capability grants, shown only as metadata. */
      effectiveCaps?: string;
    }
    
    export interface TaskRelations {
      parentTaskId?: string;
      rootTaskId?: string;
      /** Known child task ids (opaque server ids). */
      childTaskIds: string[];
      /** Subset (or separate list) still waiting — other work can continue. */
      waitingChildren: string[];
    }
    
    const SENSITIVE_KEY_RE =
      /password|passwd|secret|token|api[_-]?key|auth|bearer|credential|private[_-]?key|session[_-]?token|cookie/i;
    
    const MAX_ARGS_PREVIEW_CHARS = 500;
    const MAX_STEPS = 8;
    const MAX_STEP_CHARS = 160;
    const MAX_SUMMARY_CHARS = 280;
    
    function isRecord(value: unknown): value is Record<string, unknown> {
      return !!value && typeof value === 'object' && !Array.isArray(value);
    }
    
    function firstString(
      obj: Record<string, unknown>,
      keys: string[],
    ): string | undefined {
      for (const key of keys) {
        const value = obj[key];
        if (typeof value === 'string' && value.trim()) return value.trim();
      }
      return undefined;
    }
    
    function firstUnknown(
      obj: Record<string, unknown>,
      keys: string[],
    ): unknown {
      for (const key of keys) {
        const value = obj[key];
        if (value !== undefined && value !== null) return value;
      }
      return undefined;
    }
    
    function truncate(text: string, max: number): string {
      if (text.length <= max) return text;
      return `${text.slice(0, Math.max(0, max - 1))}…`;
    }
    
    /** Mask sensitive keys recursively; non-sensitive leaves pass through. */
    export function maskSensitiveValue(
      key: string | null,
      value: unknown,
      depth = 0,
    ): unknown {
      if (depth > 4) return '…';
      if (key && SENSITIVE_KEY_RE.test(key)) {
        if (value === undefined || value === null || value === '') return value;
        return '•••masked•••';
      }
      if (Array.isArray(value)) {

      for (const entry of value.slice(0, MAX_STEPS)) {

          out.push(truncate(String(entry), MAX_STEP_CHARS));
        }
      }
      return out;
    }

      if (typeof value === 'string' && value.trim()) return [value.trim()];

        if (typeof entry === 'string' && entry.trim()) out.push(entry.trim());

          out.push(entry['id'].trim());
        }
      }

    ### `POST /v1/notifications/register` → 200 | 400 | 401 | 403 | 429
    
    Request (device-me; no IDs accepted):

    - `expo_push_token`: required, strict `ExponentPushToken[...]` /
      `ExpoPushToken[...]`, max 256 chars.
    - `provider`: optional, must be `"expo"` when present (only provider supported).
    - `permission_enabled`: required boolean — the phone's current OS permission
      state. `false` stores the binding as disabled (no delivery) until the user
      grants permission and re-registers with `true`.
    - `project_id` (optional, ≤128 chars) is accepted for forward-compat and ignored
      by the home; never a credential.

      "enabled": true,
      "provider": "expo",

    fields, non-boolean permission) · `401 unauthorized` (bad session) ·
    `403 notifications_disabled` (operator has not enabled pushes on this home) ·
    `429 registration_limit` (max 10 active bindings per user; `Retry-After: 60`).
    The raw token is **never** returned; status exposes only a `token_suffix`.

    ## Outbox semantics (home-side, phone-visible behavior)
    
    - SQLite outbox with `UNIQUE(event_id, device_id)` — at-least-once, crash-safe.
      Stable `event_id = <taskId>:<status>:<updatedAt>`; the phone **must dedupe**
      on `event_id` (duplicate deliveries are possible after a home restart).
    - Events fire for **root tasks only**: `waiting_input`, `waiting_approval`,
      and root completion (`completed`/`failed`/`cancelled`). Delegated **children
      never notify** (no completion-storm; the parent aggregates).
    - Enqueue happens in the worker `settled` hook chain (H6 cancel/wake behavior
      preserved) and on explicit root cancel. Enqueue is synchronous SQLite;
      **network failure never fails the task**.
    - Before **send**, the home revalidates: registration still active +
      permission on, device still paired/unrevoked/owned, and the task still in
      the **same** pending/terminal status. Answered or revoked rows **drop**
      silently (generic payload means even a stale delivery leaks nothing).
    - Bounded delivery: lease/batch (default 10), retry with backoff + jitter
      (default 8 attempts, base 5 s, cap 15 min), per-row expiry (default 24 h),
      global pending cap (500, oldest dropped first). `DeviceNotRegistered`
      (ticket or receipt) disables the binding immediately. No unbounded loops,
      no request logging (method + path + status only).
    - Bounded timeouts (default 8 s) and bounded shutdown: cancel stops delivery;
      restart resumes pending rows.

    // H7 opt-in private task notifications (Expo push, metadata-only).
    //
    // Design constraints (from work order):
    // - Defaults disabled / no outbound network. Per-phone consent (permission_enabled)
    //   + operator opt-in (HOME_NOTIFICATIONS_ENABLED=1) both required before any fetch.
    // - Fixed Expo endpoints only; no arbitrary user webhook URLs (no SSRF surface).
    // - Payload is metadata only: installation_id/task_id/device_id/kind/event_id.
    //   Generic title/body only; never conversation titles, user text, output,
    //   errors, browser data, or credentials. Home hosts private history.
    // - Identity always derives from the session (device-me); client-supplied
    //   user/device IDs are never trusted.
    // - Tokens live in the 0600 SQLite file only, never in logs or API responses.
    // - Outbox is at-least-once with stable event IDs so the phone can dedupe.
    // - Network failure never fails a task; stale (answered/revoked) alerts drop.
    
    import { createHash, randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
    
    export const EXPO_PUSH_URL = 'https://exp.host/--/api/v2/push/send';
    export const EXPO_RECEIPT_URL = 'https://exp.host/--/api/v2/push/getReceipts';
    
    export const NOTIFICATION_KINDS = new Set([
      'waiting_input',
      'waiting_approval',
      'completed',
      'failed',
      'cancelled',
    ]);
    
    // Official Expo push token shape: ExponentPushToken[...] / ExpoPushToken[...]
    const EXPO_TOKEN_RE = /^(ExponentPushToken|ExpoPushToken)\[[A-Za-z0-9\-_]{1,128}\]$/;
    export const MAX_TOKEN_CHARS = 256;
    export const MAX_ACTIVE_REGISTRATIONS_PER_USER = 10;
    export const MAX_PENDING_OUTBOX = 500;
    
    export function isExpoTokenFormat(value) {
      return typeof value === 'string' && value.length >= 20 && value.length <= MAX_TOKEN_CHARS && EXPO_TOKEN_RE.test(value);
    }
    
    export function tokenSuffix(token) {
      const s = String(token ?? '');
      return s.length <= 8 ? `…${s}` : `…${s.slice(-8)}`;
    }
    
    export function tokenHash(token) {
      return createHash('sha256').update(String(token), 'utf8').digest();
    }
    
    export function resolveNotificationConfig(env = process.env) {
      const raw = env.HOME_NOTIFICATIONS_ENABLED;
      const enabled = raw === '1' || String(raw ?? '').toLowerCase() === 'true';
      if (!enabled) return { enabled: false };
      const num = (v, fallback, min, max) => {
        if (v === undefined || v === null || String(v).trim() === '') return fallback;
        const n = Number(v);
        if (!Number.isInteger(n) || n < min || n > max) {
          throw new Error(`Invalid notification tuning value: ${v}`);
        }
        return n;
      };
      return {
        enabled: true,
        // Public project identifier the phone app was built with (operator config).
        projectId: typeof env.HOME_EXPO_PROJECT_ID === 'string' && env.HOME_EXPO_PROJECT_ID.trim()
          ? env.HOME_EXPO_PROJECT_ID.trim().slice(0, 128)
          : null,

        // in SQLite, never returned over HTTP, never logged.
        accessToken: typeof env.HOME_EXPO_ACCESS_TOKEN === 'string' && env.HOME_EXPO_ACCESS_TOKEN.trim()
          ? env.HOME_EXPO_ACCESS_TOKEN.trim()
          : null,
        maxAttempts: num(env.HOME_NOTIF_MAX_ATTEMPTS, 8, 1, 20),
        baseDelayMs: num(env.HOME_NOTIF_BASE_DELAY_MS, 5000, 100, 60000),

        pumpIntervalMs: num(env.HOME_NOTIF_PUMP_MS, 15000, 1000, 120000),

    // ---- Providers -------------------------------------------------------------
    
    function withTimeout(promise, ms) {
      let timer;
      const timeout = new Promise((_, reject) => {
        timer = setTimeout(() => reject(new Error(`push send timed out after ${ms}ms`)), ms);
      });
      return Promise.race([promise, timeout]).finally(() => clearTimeout(timer));
    }
    
    // Official Expo push HTTP protocol over the single fixed endpoint. No SDK
    // dependency (no new npm packages, no lockfile churn); same wire result as the
    // maintained server SDK. Never called unless the operator opted in.
    export function createExpoHttpProvider({ accessToken = null, fetchImpl = globalThis.fetch, timeoutMs = 8000 } = {}) {
      const headers = { 'content-type': 'application/json', accept: 'application/json' };
      if (accessToken) headers.authorization = `Bearer ${accessToken}`;
      return {
        name: 'expo-http',
        async sendBatch(messages) {
          const res = await withTimeout(
            fetchImpl(EXPO_PUSH_URL, { method: 'POST', headers, body: JSON.stringify(messages) }),
            timeoutMs,
          );
          const json = await res.json().catch(() => null);
          const items = json?.data ?? json?.data?.data ?? null;
          const list = Array.isArray(json) ? json : Array.isArray(items) ? items : Array.isArray(json?.data) ? json.data : null;
          // Expo returns {data:[{status:'ok',id}|{status:'error',message,details}]}.
          const data = Array.isArray(json?.data) ? json.data : Array.isArray(json) ? json : [];
          if (!Array.isArray(data) || data.length !== messages.length) {
            throw new Error(`Unexpected Expo push response (status ${res.status})`);
          }
          return data.map((t) => {
            if (t?.status === 'ok') return { ticketStatus: 'ok', ticketId: typeof t.id === 'string' ? t.id : null };
            return {
              ticketStatus: 'error',
              message: String(t?.message ?? 'push rejected').slice(0, 300),
              details: t?.details ?? null,
            };
          });
        },
        async getReceipts(ids) {
          if (!ids.length) return {};
          const res = await withTimeout(
            fetchImpl(EXPO_RECEIPT_URL, { method: 'POST', headers, body: JSON.stringify({ ids }) }),
            timeoutMs,
          );
          const json = await res.json().catch(() => null);
          const data = json?.data ?? {};
          if (!data || typeof data !== 'object') throw new Error('Unexpected Expo receipt response');
          return data;
        },
      };
    }
    
    // Disabled default: any accidental send attempt throws instead of touching the network.
    export function createDisabledProvider() {
      const err = () => { throw Object.assign(new Error('Notifications are disabled on this home'), { code: 'notifications_disabled' }); };
      return { name: 'disabled', sendBatch: async () => { err(); }, getReceipts: async () => { err(); } };
    }

    ## Native phone flow (F8, Expo Notifications SDK 58)
    
    1. On first launch (and after account logout/login), request OS permission via
       the SDK. If denied, register with `permission_enabled:false` (or skip) and
       do not schedule local handlers that assume delivery.
    2. Get the Expo push token with the **app's configured public Project ID**
       (`getExpoPushTokenAsync({ projectId })` — project ID is app config, never
       a home credential).
    3. `POST /v1/notifications/register` on the **currently paired home** with the
       session token: `{expo_push_token, provider:"expo", permission_enabled}`.
       Persist nothing sensitive beyond the suffix for debug UI.
    4. On notification tap: **do not navigate from push data**. First verify the
       tap's `installation_id` matches the currently paired home **and**
       `device_id` matches this device; if either mismatches, drop the tap
       (stale install / remapped address — prevents private leaks after logout or
       re-pair). Then `GET /v1/tasks/:task_id` on the current home and render
       from the **fetched task + conversation** (which includes `conversation_id`),
       never from push text.
    5. Dedupe by `event_id` (in-memory + persisted cache): ignore repeats.
    6. On account logout: call `POST /v1/notifications/disable` best-effort (the
       home may be offline — treat as untrusted), clear local handlers and the
       duplicate cache, and re-register only after the next successful pair.
    7. Model tools never configure tokens; push addresses never pass through task
       inputs/approvals.

    HOME_NOTIF_MAX_ATTEMPTS=8 HOME_NOTIF_BASE_DELAY_MS=5000

    With the flag off, register returns `403 notifications_disabled` and the home
    makes zero outbound connections (verified by the disabled-mode test).
    
    ## What this slice does not do
    
    - No APNs key provisioning, no real Expo/public push resources, no cloud relay.
    - No per-task content in pushes; task detail (`GET /v1/tasks/:id`, which
      includes `conversation_id`) remains the single source of truth.
    - No changes to the frozen `task-rpc-v1` / FD3 parent-child contract (R8
      worker untouched).

    ## 2. Known advisories on pinned versions (OSV + GitHub primary)
    
    OSV queried per pinned package; only two hits, both LangGraph-ecosystem:
    
    **A. GHSA-g48c-2wqr-h844 / CVE-2026-28277 — unsafe msgpack checkpoint
    deserialization (Moderate, CVSS 6.8). AFFECTS pinned `langgraph 0.6.11`.**
    Primary: [advisory](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/security/advisories/GHSA-g48c-2wqr-h844).
    Affected `<=1.0.9`, patched in `1.0.10` (2026-02-27); OSV range confirms
    `introduced: 0, fixed: 1.0.10`. There is **no 0.6.x patch** — PyPI shows
    0.6.11 as the final 0.6 release, so the fix requires the 0.6 → 1.x major
    upgrade. Threat model (per the advisory itself): post-exploitation /
    defense-in-depth — exploitation needs write access to checkpoint bytes at
    rest, which in this deployment means the home host / `<workspace>/.me_runtime/graph.db`
    is already compromised. Not remotely reachable in a correctly configured
    deployment; no known exploitation in the wild.
    Home relevance is therefore low-severity but real (runtime secrets live in the
    same process), and the fix path is a planned migration, not an emergency.
    
    Mitigation available WITHOUT the major upgrade (verified in the installed
    0.6.11 tree: `langgraph/checkpoint/serde/jsonplus.py` + `_msgpack.py` already
    honor it): set **`LANGGRAPH_STRICT_MSGPACK=true`** in the runtime environment
    — allowlist-based strict deserialization, schema-derived for compiled graphs
    per the advisory. Nothing in `agentic-framework` sets or documents it today
    (grep for `STRICT_MSGPACK`/`LANGGRAPH` across src/scripts/docs/`.env.example`
    is empty). See MUSTFIX 1.
    
    **B. `langgraph-sdk` 0.6.x-line pin 0.2.15 — GHSA-fvww-7h3r-vfhp (fixed 0.4.4)
    + GHSA-w39p-vh2g-g8g5 (fixed 0.3.15). NOT REACHABLE here.** The runtime never
    imports `langgraph_sdk` (grep over `src/me_runtime/**` shows only
    `langgraph.prebuilt`, `langgraph.errors`, `langgraph.types`,
    `langgraph.checkpoint.sqlite`); it is a transitive pin talking to no remote
    endpoint in this design (local `SqliteSaver` only). No action beyond letting
    the 1.x migration float it forward; do not chase separately.
    
    Everything else queried is OSV-clean at pinned versions: langgraph-prebuilt
    0.6.5, checkpoint 4.3.1, checkpoint-sqlite 3.1.3, langchain-core/openai/ollama/
    anthropic adapters, openai, anthropic, ollama, pillow, httpx, httpx2,
    httpcore2, aiosqlite, jiter, langchain-protocol, playwright, npm jose/expo/
    react-native. Bounded note: clean today ≠ certified; re-query on upgrade.
    
    `create_react_agent` deprecation check (the "old prebuilt API" question):
    **not deprecated.** Upstream tags `prebuilt==1.1.1` and `1.2.19` still export

    ## 3. Privacy transport: local Ollama proxy exposure — CONFIRMED, MUSTFIX
    
    `models.py:85-90` builds `ChatOllama(base_url="http://127.0.0.1:11434")` with
    no `client_kwargs`. Installed `langchain-ollama 1.1.0` forwards those into
    `ollama-python 0.6.3` `Client/AsyncClient`, which forward `**kwargs` into
    `httpx.Client` (`ollama/_client.py`, `BaseClient.__init__`). Installed
    `httpx 0.28.1` defaults **`trust_env=True`** (`httpx/_client.py:201`), i.e.
    `HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY/ALL_PROXY` are honored unless `NO_PROXY` covers
    loopback — which a home host cannot assume. Result: with a proxy set in the
    bridge environment, local prompt bytes addressed to loopback can leave the
    home. Concrete fix (one line, no behavior change otherwise): pass
    `sync_client_kwargs={"trust_env": False}, async_client_kwargs={"trust_env":
    False}` (or `proxy=None`) for provider `local`. This is an inconsistency, not
    a design decision: `tools/web.py:137-140` already strips all `*_PROXY` and
    passes `--noproxy '*'` for curl fetches precisely because "a proxy would
    bypass `--resolve` DNS pinning" — the Ollama path missed the same treatment.
    Remote providers (`openai`/`anthropic`) are unaffected by this finding: they
    require `ME_RUNTIME_ALLOW_REMOTE=1` plus an env-held key (`models.py:66-77`),
    keys never travel in the request, and proxy use there is policy-consistent
    because the traffic is explicitly remote.
    
    ## 4. Reuse justification, licenses, proprietary deps avoided
    
    - One harness, no doubles: agent loop is owned by maintained
    `langgraph-prebuilt.create_react_agent` (`agent.py:1-8,88-95`); no custom
    planner, no manual `/chat/completions` parsing. Browser isolation reuses the
    official Playwright Python image + SDK 1.64.1 (both current, §1) with
    operator-built, `--pull never` Docker runs. Animation reuses Pillow 13.0.0
    (current, OSV-clean). OIDC reuses npm `jose` 6.2.15 (current, OSV-clean, MIT).
    - Upstream code reuse is vendored, not forked: OpenMuse worker+log helper at
    immutable commit `a4944f4c…b521ab6` with SHA-256 inventory
    (`infra-server/vendor/openmuse/upstream.json`) and original MIT `LICENSE`
    preserved; compatibility CI + weekly candidate workflow documented in
    `infra-server/docs/upstream-updates.md`. No blanket-clearance claims; matches
    `agentic-framework/docs/reuse-audit.md` (OpenMuse donor / OpenClaw trial /
    DeepAgents alternative framing stands).
    - Python dep licenses (local dist-info METADATA): langgraph, prebuilt,
    checkpoint, checkpoint-sqlite, langchain-*, ollama, langgraph-sdk = MIT;
    openai = Apache-2.0; httpx = BSD-3-Clause; pillow = MIT-CMU; aiosqlite = MIT.
    npm `jose` = MIT. Me repos are Apache-2.0. No copyleft in the runtime path.
    - Proprietary dependencies avoided: local-first default (Ollama loopback, no
    key); remote model use is explicit opt-in; no LangSmith/hosted control plane,
    no vendor browser cloud, no proprietary DB (SQLite via aiosqlite).
    
    ## 5. Upstream-update coverage vs not-yet-public runs
    
    - `agentic-framework`: Dependabot `pip` + `github-actions` weekly, PR
    dependency-review (`fail-on-severity: high`), CI pins exact

    fleet. Gap: nothing watches `browser` extra / base-image tag drift except the

        root=pathlib.Path('/private/tmp/me-opencode-live-20261103'); root.chmod(0o700)

        saved=0;n=0

         dest=f.with_suffix(f.suffix+'.gz'); tmp=dest.with_suffix(dest.suffix+'.tmp'); old=f.stat().st_size
         with f.open('rb') as src, gzip.open(tmp,'wb',compresslevel=6) as dst: shutil.copyfileobj(src,dst,64*1024)

    # Home activation v1 (home ↔ Me Backend one-time activation + recovery)
    
    Status: implemented. Protocol `home-activation-v1` (wire) + `home-coordinator-v1`
    (private credentials file). Backend is source of truth; home (H8), setup (S7),
    and phone (F9) implement against this document. Existing B3
    `POST /v1/homes/registration-tickets` + `POST /v1/homes/register` (account JWT
    required at register time) is retained unchanged for compat. The activation
    pair below is distinct: the home redeems with the ticket alone, no account
    JWT ever leaves the phone.
    
    Privacy rule (load-bearing): the cloud account can help a caller discover
    *which* home record is theirs (coordinator metadata: `homeId`,
    `installationId`, `endpointHint`, liveness), but it can NEVER mint, rotate,
    or read HomeAPI private auth (H1 device secrets / session tokens). The
    physical one-time setup invitation binds the URL; the cloud `endpointHint`
    is a discovery hint only. Phone F8 MUST NOT auto-rebind device credentials
    from a changed backend `endpointHint`; an endpoint change requires a fresh
    local setup invitation from the trusted home. Old private-URL credentials
    stay unchanged. Cloud account recovery therefore cannot capture family home
    device secrets. No app-layer crypto or second server trust system is
    invented here.
    
    No brokered private chat storage, no SSH credentials, no provider secrets
    anywhere in this flow.
    
    ## Roles
    
    | Side | Holds | Never sees |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | Phone F9 (owner account) | Me account JWT (OIDC/dev), backend URL | `homeToken`, H1 device secrets |
    | Home H8 / setup S7 | Activation ticket (one-time), then `homeToken` | Me account JWT, provider tokens |
    | Backend | sha256 verifiers only (tickets + home tokens) | Ticket secrets, homeTokens, account JWTs (verified then dropped) |
    
    ## 1. Mint: POST /v1/homes/activation-tickets (account auth)
    
    Owner phone calls with its normal account bearer (dev token or OIDC JWT —
    verified B4 path, identity derived server-side, body identity rejected
    `400`).
    
    Request:
    
    ```json
    {
      "installationId": "123e4567-e89b-42d3-a456-426614174000",
      "displayName": "Cabin Home (optional, new-only)",
      "existingHomeId": "home_abc123 (optional, recovery-only)"
    }
    ```
    
    Rules:
    
    - `installationId` required, printable ASCII 1–128 (H1 `installation_id`
      verbatim, e.g. uuid). Binds the ticket to that physical home.
    - Omit `existingHomeId` → mode `new`. Optional `displayName` (1–100)
      stored for the to-be-created home.
    - Present `existingHomeId` → mode `recovery`. Caller must currently be
      `owner` of that home (`404` if not a member to hide existence, `403` if
      member but not owner). Request `installationId` must match the home's
      stored `installationId` when set, else `403`.
    - `homeId` / `accountId` / `ownerId` fields in the body are rejected `400`;
      `homeId` comes from the ticket (recovery) or is server-generated (new).
    - Fixed TTL 5 minutes. Max 15 live tickets per account (`429` beyond).
      Expired (>1h past expiry) tickets are pruned; only sha256 verifiers are
      stored, secrets shown once and never logged. Ticket namespace is scoped
      and unique (`act_…`); join (`ticket_…`) and registration (`regticket_…`)
      secrets are never accepted here (conflation → `403`).
    
    Response `201` (capability only — no `homeToken`, no other account data):
    
    ```json
    {
      "ticketId": "act_…",
      "activationSecret": "<256-bit base64url, shown ONCE>",
      "installationId": "123e4567-…",
      "mode": "new | recovery",
      "homeId": "home_abc123 | null (new)",
      "expiresAt": "2026-…Z"
    }
    ```
    
    Display/copy for S7: F9 shows a one-time activation JSON containing
    `{ backend_url, ticketId, activationSecret, installationId, mode,
    homeId?, expiresAt }`. It includes the known backend URL, NEVER a provider
    secret or account JWT.
    
    ## 2. Redeem: POST /v1/homes/activate (ticket ONLY, no account JWT)
    
    Home/setup calls over HTTPS (protected transport) with NO `Authorization`
    header. The ticket IS the authorization.
    
    Request:
    
    ```json
    {
      "ticketId": "act_…",
      "activationSecret": "<from mint step>",
      "installationId": "123e4567-e89b-42d3-a456-426614174000 (exact own)",
      "endpointHint": "https://home.example.test (public base URL)",
      "protocolVersion": "home-api-v1 (optional, default \"1\")"
    }
    ```
    
    (`ticketSecret` accepted as alias for `activationSecret`. `homeId`,
    `existingHomeId`, `homeToken`, `accountId` fields rejected `400` — the
    homeId comes from the ticket, never the request.)
    
    Rules:
    
    - Ticket must exist in the activation namespace, secret must verify
      (timing-safe), else `403`. Consumed/expired → `410`.
    - `installationId` must exactly equal the ticket's bound installation,
      else `403`. Recovery additionally re-checks caller still owns the home
      and the home's stored installation still matches, else `403`.
    - `endpointHint` required: public `https://` in production; plain `http://`
      accepted ONLY for loopback hosts (`127.0.0.1`, `localhost`, `::1`) for
      explicit dev/test. Anything else → `400`. The backend NEVER fetches this
      URL — stored opaquely as a discovery hint.
    - `protocolVersion` 1–32 chars. Invalid shape → `400`.
    - Invalid requests NEVER burn the ticket: validation runs before consume,
      so a `400`/`403` leaves the ticket usable. Only a persisted success (or
      a correctly reported `410` replay) consumes.
    - Atomicity: consume + home create/rotate + membership + verifier update
      are applied in memory then persisted once. Persist failure rolls back
      every in-memory mutation (ticket un-consumed, no half home, old
      verifiers restored) and surfaces `500`.
    - New: fresh server-generated `homeId` (`home_<18 lowercase hex>`),
      `installationId` from ticket, `displayName` from ticket, `endpointHint` /
      `protocolVersion` from redeem body; owner membership created for the
      minting account.
    - Recovery: SAME `homeId` from the ticket; old `me_home_…` verifiers for
      that home are invalidated, a fresh `homeToken` is issued, endpointHint
      (coordinator metadata only) is updated. Owner membership preserved /
      re-asserted. HomeAPI private auth is untouched.
    
    Response `201` (shown ONCE — persist to the private file, never to git):
    
    ```json
    {
      "homeId": "home_…",
      "installationId": "123e4567-…",
      "homeToken": "me_home_…",
      "endpointHint": "https://…",
      "protocolVersion": "home-api-v1",
      "mode": "new | recovery"
    }
    ```
    
    ## 3. Private credentials file (H8 reads, S7 writes)
    
    Path: outside git, outside shared config, mode `0600`, e.g.
    `~/.me-home/coordinator.json` (operator-chosen, secret-separated).
    
    ```json
    {
      "protocol": "home-coordinator-v1",
      "backend_url": "https://backend.example.test",
      "home_id": "home_…",
      "installation_id": "123e4567-…",
      "home_token": "me_home_…",
      "endpoint_hint": "https://home.example.test"
    }
    ```
    
    Defaults: all absent until activation succeeds (no defaults that fake a
    home). H8 starts disabled without this file.
    
    S7 flow: redeem over HTTPS (follow redirects only to `https://` or loopback
    `http://`; send NO account JWT from the home), write the file `0600`
    outside git, never log the secret, never ship it to the phone. The phone
    gets coordinator discovery reads with its own account credential — never
    this file.
    
    ## 4. Existing HomeToken API (exact contract the activated home uses)
    
    Unchanged behavior, documented here so H8/S7 don't guess:
    
    - `POST /v1/homes/:homeId/heartbeat` — home-self auth ONLY
      (`Authorization: Bearer <homeToken>` for that exact `homeId`).
      Body `{ status?: "online"|"degraded"|"offline", endpointHint?,
      installationId? }`. Account bearers → `403`; missing creds → `401`;
      wrong home's token → `403`. Updates `lastSeenAt`/`lastStatus`, optionally
      rebinds `endpointHint` / `installationId`. Returns
      `{ ok, homeId, lastSeenAt, lastStatus }`. `endpointHint` here stays
      opaque ≤500 chars (legacy compat); the `https://` strictness applies at
      activation time.
    - `GET /v1/homes/:homeId/status` — member (account) or home-self.
      Returns `{ homeId, lastSeenAt, lastStatus, online, staleAfterSeconds }`.
      `online` is computed server-side (heartbeat within
      `ME_BACKEND_STALE_AFTER_SECONDS`, default 300s, bounded 30–3600s).
      Never-heartbeated / stale homes report `online:false`; clients MUST NOT
      infer liveness from `lastStatus` alone.
    - Endpoint updates require the home token for the SAME home — registration
      can never overwrite a live home (`409` on duplicate `homeId` without
      burning any ticket). Auth failure returns no home data (`401` anonymous,
      `403` wrong credential, `404` non-member to hide existence).
    
    ## 5. Failure handling (unknown activate outcome)
    
    If S7 gets a transport error / timeout after `POST …/activate` with an
    unknown server outcome, it MUST NOT retry with the same ticket (replay
    would correctly report `410` without revealing whether the first attempt
    persisted a credential S7 never saw). Instead:
    
    1. Phone (owner account) discovers the home record via `GET /v1/homes`
       (members-only) to confirm `homeId`.
    2. Owner mints a FRESH recovery ticket
       (`POST /v1/homes/activation-tickets { installationId, existingHomeId }`).
    3. Home redeems the fresh ticket once, persists the fresh `homeToken`.
    
    NEVER recover a `homeToken` by replaying an old ticket. Rotations always
    invalidate prior verifiers.
    
    ## 6. Errors
    
    `400` validation / body identity / `homeId` smuggled into activation
    bodies (never consumed); `401` missing account (mint) credential;
    `403` wrong secret / wrong installation / cross-home / non-owner recovery
    mint / conflated old ticket type (never consumed); `404` unknown home
    (non-member view); `409` n/a here (new homeIds server-generated);
    `410` expired/consumed replay (consumed); `429` per-account cap;
    `500` persist failure (rolled back, ticket NOT burned).
    
    ## 7. Non-goals
    
    No private chat/message storage or relay. No SSH credentials. No
    user/provider credential resources. No app-layer crypto beyond the
    one-time ticket + `me_home_…` bearer over HTTPS. No second server trust
    system — the physical setup invitation binds the URL; the cloud is a
    discovery hint.
    # H8 integration handoff — actual home ↔ hosted-backend coordination
    
    Companion to `contracts/home-coordination-v1.md` (authoritative for the home
    file + loop) and `contracts/home-api-v1.md` (private API, unchanged).
    Backend wire is owned by `backend-server/docs/home-activation-v1.md` (B7) +
    `docs/backend-api-v1.md` (B4); do not re-implement it here.
    
    ## What H8 delivers (infra-server only)
    
    - `src/coordinator.mjs`: private-file loader/validator + periodic HomeToken
      heartbeat loop. Disabled by default (zero network unless
      `HOME_COORDINATOR_CREDENTIALS_FILE` is set). Initial heartbeat is async +
      nonblocking; period default 60s with backoff/jitter (max 5 min); per-attempt
      timeout + bounded `64 KiB` body; `redirect: 'error'` with final-origin
      checks; `401`/`403` suspends until the file changes; transient failures stay
      `offline`-rescheduled and never pause the agent; generation-fenced rotations;
      abort + bounded drain on stop (no orphans).
    - Wired into `createHomeServer`: `coordinator.start()` on home start,
      `coordinator.stop()` on shutdown, redacted `GET /v1/coordinator/status`
      (session-authenticated; never token/prefix/raw errors/account claims).
      `/healthz`/`/readyz` unchanged. Private conversations/tasks/pairing work
      identically with the coordinator disabled, misconfigured, suspended, or
      cloud-offline.
    - `buildRuntimeEnv` exclusion extended with `HOME_COORDINATOR_*`: the
      credentials-file reference and any cloud/home token material never enter
      runtime bridge children. Sentinel tests assert no `me_home_*`,
      `HOME_COORDINATOR_*`, Expo push, `SSH_*`, or `AWS_*` in child env beyond the
      single trusted model key.
    
    ## For setup (S7: writes the file)
    
    1. Phone (owner account) mints an activation ticket:
       `POST /v1/homes/activation-tickets {installationId, displayName? |
       existingHomeId?}` (account auth). Copy the one-time JSON
       `{backend_url, ticketId, activationSecret, installationId, mode, homeId?,
       expiresAt}` to the home operator (never an account JWT or provider secret).
    2. Home redeems ticket-only (NO `Authorization` header):
       `POST {backend_url}/v1/homes/activate
       {ticketId, activationSecret, installationId (exact own), endpointHint,
       protocolVersion}`. `endpointHint` MUST be public `https://`, or
       `http://` loopback only for explicit dev/test. Backend never fetches it.
    3. On `201 {homeId, installationId, homeToken, endpointHint,
       protocolVersion, mode}`, write the private file EXACTLY:
    
    ```json
    {
      "protocol": "home-coordinator-v1",
      "backend_url": "https://backend.example.test",
      "home_id": "home_…",
      "installation_id": "123e4567-…",
      "home_token": "me_home_…",
      "endpoint_hint": "https://home.example.test"
    }
    ```
    
    plus `"protocol_version": "home-api-v1"`. Absolute path outside git/shared
    config, `0600`, regular file, `≤16 KiB`, no final symlink. Never log the
    secret or ship it to the phone.
    
    4. Set `HOME_COORDINATOR_CREDENTIALS_FILE=<absolute file>` (+
       `HOME_COORDINATOR_ALLOW_HTTP_LOOPBACK=1` ONLY for loopback dev/test) and
       (re)start the home. `installation_id` MUST match `GET /healthz`.
    5. Unknown activate outcome (timeout/disconnect): do NOT retry the same
       ticket. Discover via `GET /v1/homes` (owner account), mint a FRESH recovery
       ticket with `existingHomeId`, redeem once, persist the fresh `homeToken`.
    6. Full restore / file deleted: reactivation needed (fresh ticket, same flow).
       Old tickets correctly replay `410`.
    
    ## For the consumers
    
    - `phone-app`: keep using the direct protected home URL from the local setup
      invitation. Treat backend `endpointHint` as a discovery hint only; NEVER
      auto-rebind device credentials from a changed hint (F8) — a new URL requires
      a fresh local invitation. No fake heartbeat is needed from the phone; the
      home heartbeats itself.
    - `backend-server/setup-infra`: preserve the SQLite file + tasks root as
      before; preserve the coordinator file across upgrades (or reactivate). No
      provider cloud resources, no new framework/deps (built-in fetch only).
    - `agentic-framework`: no changes. Coordinator secrets never enter
      `buildRuntimeEnv`; `ME_RUNTIME_*` filtering (H7.1) is unchanged.
    
    ## What H8 does not claim
    
    - Single-host SQLite, loopback-default bind, no quotas/backups beyond H2/H5.
    - No brokered private chat storage/relay, no SSH, no provider-secret handling.
    - No app-layer crypto, no second server trust system, no server pin policy.
    - No cloud-driven private-URL/model/auth reconfiguration: heartbeat responses
      are liveness observations only.

    # setup-infra
    
    Local installation and infrastructure bootstrap for Me Home AI.
    
    Part of [Me Home AI](https://github.com/mehomeai), a privacy-first home agentic system.
    Learn about the vision at [Me — Your intelligence. Yours.](https://mehomeai.replit.app/me/).
    ## Status
    
    This repository provides the rerunnable development setup and managed lifecycle
    for the Me home service: `scripts/me_setup.py` (prerequisites, config,
    non-secret environment) and `scripts/me_lifecycle.py` (managed
    start/status/stop, home-CLI bootstrap, scoped backup/restore (`--scope db`
    SQLite snapshot, `--scope full` stopped-service household archive),
    fail-closed named-tunnel adapter, service-unit generation with a shared
    pre-exec guard). Verified: `69 tests` pass
    (`python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py' -v`),
    including live end-to-ends against the real home API: pairing/conversation
    plus a fixture agent task through the real runtime bridge, and a cross-path
    waiting-input backup/restore/resume round-trip (home A -> home B, rebased
    checkpoint binding, re-pair + answer -> completion). Start injects the exact trusted env
    the home reads (`ME_RUNTIME_ARGV` JSON array + `ME_RUNTIME_CWD`,
    `HOME_MODEL_PROVIDER/NAME/ENDPOINT`, `HOME_ALLOW_FIXTURE_MODEL`,
    `ME_RUNTIME_ALLOW_REMOTE`, `HOME_CAP_*`, `ME_RUNTIME_ALLOW_CODE_EXEC`,
    `ME_RUNTIME_SANDBOX=docker` when code execution is explicitly enabled;
    secrets inherited from the operator shell only, never persisted). Local
    endpoint is the ChatOllama-correct `http://127.0.0.1:11434` (no `/v1`).
    Household data and execution stay on the home host; an explicitly enabled
    remote provider receives prompts/tool context. `backup`/`restore --scope db`
    (default) cover the SQLite database only (online-safe API + verification);
    `--scope full` archives the database (backup API) plus per-task workspaces
    including `.me_runtime` checkpoints, household files, and a manifest —
    config/logs/secrets excluded, local-only, never uploaded. Full restore
    validates before mutating, swaps by same-filesystem rename under a durable
    write-ahead journal (NOT one atomic transaction) with rollback, and revokes
    restored sessions/devices/invitations (pair fresh devices afterwards), so a
    rolled-back backup cannot revive a revoked phone. Generated launchd/systemd
    units exec the shared guard (config/me-home.exec.py), which refuses to boot
    on an interrupted restore and only then execs Node. Default tunnel mode
    is `home-pairing` (HTTPS via the named tunnel, phone-app compatible); the
    optional `cloudflare-access` mode enforces Access JWTs at the edge and needs
    separate edge auth (native phone clients cannot complete it). No root, no
    global install, no public endpoint; service units and tunnel launches are
    explicit operator actions.
    
    ```sh
    python3 scripts/me_setup.py setup [--data-dir DIR] [--port N]
    python3 scripts/me_setup.py check [--data-dir DIR]
    python3 scripts/me_lifecycle.py start|status|stop|bootstrap|backup|restore|tunnel|service ...
    python3 scripts/me_lifecycle.py backup --scope full [--output OUT.tar.gz]      # service stopped only
    python3 scripts/me_lifecycle.py restore --scope full --from OUT.tar.gz --confirm-destructive
    python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py' -v
    ```
    
    See [`docs/development-setup.md`](docs/development-setup.md) for the full flow
    and [`docs/production-tunnel-boundary.md`](docs/production-tunnel-boundary.md)
    for the tunnel adapter and parked provider checks. The home entrypoint needs
    `--experimental-transform-types`; lifecycle retries once with it automatically.
    
    ## Scope
    
    Installation, local prerequisites, configuration, upgrades, and recovery.
    
    The setup flow provisions a protected home endpoint through a named tunnel
    and starts one-time phone pairing. Provider connector credentials stay with
    the home/provisioning service; each enrolled phone gets separate, revocable
    application access. The cross-repository design is recorded in
    `infra-server/docs/connection-and-pairing.md`.
    
    ## Contributing

    # home-coordination-v1 — home ↔ hosted-backend coordination contract
    
    Version: `home-coordinator-v1` (file) over `home-api-v1` (wire) · Status: implemented (H8) · Owner: `infra-server`
    
    Source reality: the hosted backend owns the wire (`backend-server/docs/home-activation-v1.md` B7 + `docs/backend-api-v1.md` B4). This file owns only the home side: credential-file schema, env keys, heartbeat payloads, and failure states. Where they disagree on backend behavior, the backend docs win; where they disagree on the home file, this markdown wins.
    
    Backend B7 publishes ticket-only `POST /v1/homes/activate` + account activation tickets. The home never sees an account JWT. Existing B1 `POST /v1/homes/register` heartbeat path is retained for local-dev compat and is used by tests the same way.
    
    ## 1. Private credentials file (S7 writes, H8 reads)
    
    Path: operator-chosen absolute file outside git and outside shared config, e.g. `~/.me-home/coordinator.json`. Env: `HOME_COORDINATOR_CREDENTIALS_FILE=<absolute private file>`. Default unset = DISABLED with zero outbound network.
    
    S7 redeems the one-time activation ticket over HTTPS (follow redirects only to `https://` or loopback `http://`; send NO account JWT from the home), then writes this file `0600` outside git, never logs the secret, never ships it to the phone.
    
    ```json
    {
      "protocol": "home-coordinator-v1",
      "backend_url": "https://backend.example.test",
      "home_id": "home_…",
      "installation_id": "123e4567-…",
      "home_token": "me_home_…",
      "endpoint_hint": "https://home.example.test",
      "protocol_version": "home-api-v1"
    }
    ```
    
    Schema (exact, frozen):
    
    | Field | Type | Rule |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | `protocol` | string | MUST equal `home-coordinator-v1` |
    | `backend_url` | string 1..500 | valid URL, no userinfo/query/fragment. `https:` always; `http:` ONLY for loopback hosts (`127.0.0.1`, `localhost`, `::1`) with explicit `HOME_COORDINATOR_ALLOW_HTTP_LOOPBACK=1`. Path normalization allowed. |
    | `home_id` | string | `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{2,63}$` (backend homeId) |
    | `installation_id` | string | printable ASCII 1..128, MUST equal the actual home DB `installation_id` (`GET /healthz`), else `wrong_home` |
    | `home_token` | string | `^me_home_[A-Za-z0-9_-]{32,128}$` (opaque, shown once at activation) |
    | `endpoint_hint` | string 1..500 | public home base URL, same `https:` / loopback-`http:` gate as `backend_url`, no userinfo/query/fragment. Trusted local config only; sent as `endpointHint` in heartbeats. |
    | `protocol_version` | string | MUST equal `home-api-v1` |
    
    No extra keys. File gates: absolute path, final component MUST NOT be a symlink, MUST be a regular file, size `1..16 KiB`, mode owner-only (`(mode & 0o077) === 0`, i.e. `0600`-style). Violations, JSON errors, or `installation_id` mismatch = configured component error, NO network. Error codes are generic (`invalid_credentials_format`, `invalid_credentials_permissions`, `wrong_home`, …); values/secrets/paths/contents are never echoed or logged.
    
    Deletion: if the file is deleted (e.g. after a full restore), the coordinator reports `configuration_error` and stops all network. A fresh activation (new ticket → new `home_token` → new file) is required. Replaying an old ticket MUST report `410` and MUST NOT resurrect the old credential.
    
    No account JWT, SSH, provider secrets, or global Me credentials live at the home.
    
    ## 2. Env keys
    
    | Key | Default | Meaning |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | `HOME_COORDINATOR_CREDENTIALS_FILE` | unset (DISABLED) | absolute private file above |
    | `HOME_COORDINATOR_INTERVAL_MS` | `60000` | heartbeat period, bounded `5000..600000`, plus backoff/jitter (max backoff 5 min) |
    | `HOME_COORDINATOR_TIMEOUT_MS` | `8000` | per-attempt fetch+body timeout, bounded `1000..30000` |
    | `HOME_COORDINATOR_ALLOW_HTTP_LOOPBACK` | unset (false) | `1`/`true` allows `http://` loopback `backend_url`/`endpoint_hint` for explicit dev/test only |
    
    `HOME_*` (including `HOME_COORDINATOR_*`) never crosses into runtime bridge children (`buildRuntimeEnv` exclusion, H7.1). The only model secret a child ever sees is the home-selected `model.api_key_env` value.
    
    ## 3. HTTP payloads (HomeToken auth only)
    
    Heartbeat (existing backend route, home-self only):
    
    ```http
    POST {backend_url}/v1/homes/:homeId/heartbeat
    Authorization: Bearer <home_token>
    Content-Type: application/json
    
    {"status":"online","endpointHint":"<from file>","installationId":"<from file>"}
    ```
    
    - `Authorization: Bearer <home_token>` for that exact `homeId`. Account bearers → `403`; missing → `401`; wrong home's token → `403`.
    - `redirect: 'error'` — redirects are failures, never followed; no cached tokens forwarded cross-origin. Final origin MUST equal the configured `backend_url` origin.
    - Timeout + `AbortController` covers headers AND bounded response body (`64 KiB` max).
    - Success `200`: `{ok, homeId, lastSeenAt, lastStatus}`. The backend response NEVER changes the private home URL, model, or auth config; liveness observations only.
    - Endpoint updates use this same route (`endpointHint`/`installationId` rebind, home-token-gated). No separate endpoint-update route is invented here.
    - Status read (phone/operator discovery, not used by the home loop): `GET /v1/homes/:homeId/status` (member or home-self) → `{homeId, lastSeenAt, lastStatus, online, staleAfterSeconds}`. `online` is server-computed (heartbeat within `ME_BACKEND_STALE_AFTER_SECONDS`); never-heartbeated/stale = `offline`.
    
    Local coordinator status (authenticated, redacted):
    
    ```http
    GET /v1/coordinator/status  (Bearer session token)
    → 200 {configured, enabled, status, homeId:"home_abc…wxyz"|null,
           lastHeartbeat:{at,lastSeenAt,lastStatus}|null,
           lastCheckAt, nextAttemptAt, suspended, configError}
    ```
    
    `status` ∈ `disabled|config_error|suspended|online|offline|unknown`. Never `home_token`, prefixes, raw errors, or account claims. `/healthz`/`/readyz` are unchanged.
    
    // Backend coordination adapter (B1): account/home membership distinct from
    // home user identity. The hosted backend coordinates accounts, home
    // registration/discovery, join tickets, and presence — it never sees private
    // traffic, H1 device credentials, or session tokens. Identity always derives
    // from the presented credential; this client never sends account/user ids.
    
    import { HomeClientError } from './errors.ts';
    import { redactHeaders } from './secure-storage.ts';
    import type { SecureStorage } from './secure-storage.ts';
    
    export const BACKEND_URL_KEY = 'me.backend.url.v1';
    export const BACKEND_ACCOUNT_TOKEN_KEY = 'me.backend.account-token.v1';
    
    export interface MemberHome {
      homeId: string;
      displayName?: string;
      installationId?: string;
      endpointHint?: string;
      protocolVersion?: string;
      createdAt?: number;
      lastSeenAt?: number;
      lastStatus?: string;
      role?: string;
    }
    
    export interface BackendCoordinatorOptions {
      fetchImpl?: typeof fetch;
      now?: () => number;
      requestTimeoutMs?: number;
      allowInsecureLoopback?: boolean;
    }
    
    export class BackendCoordinator {
      private readonly fetchImpl: (
        input: string,
        init?: {
          method?: string;
          headers?: Record<string, string>;
          body?: string;
          signal?: AbortSignal;
          redirect?: 'error' | 'follow' | 'manual';
        },
      ) => Promise<{ status: number; url?: string; json(): Promise<unknown> }>;
      private readonly secure: SecureStorage;
      private readonly requestTimeoutMs: number;
      private readonly allowInsecureLoopback: boolean;
    
      constructor(secureStorage: SecureStorage, options: BackendCoordinatorOptions = {}) {
        this.secure = secureStorage;
        this.fetchImpl = (options.fetchImpl ?? fetch) as unknown as BackendCoordinator['fetchImpl'];
        this.requestTimeoutMs = options.requestTimeoutMs ?? 20_000;
        this.allowInsecureLoopback = options.allowInsecureLoopback ?? false;
      }
    
      normalizeBaseUrl(value: string): string {
        let parsed: URL;
        try {
          parsed = new URL(value.trim());
        } catch {
          throw new HomeClientError('INVALID_INPUT', 'Enter a valid backend address.');
        }
        const isLoopback =
          parsed.hostname === 'localhost' ||
          parsed.hostname === '127.0.0.1' ||
          parsed.hostname === '::1';
        if (
          (parsed.protocol !== 'https:' &&
            !(this.allowInsecureLoopback && parsed.protocol === 'http:' && isLoopback)) ||
          parsed.username ||
          parsed.password ||
          parsed.search ||
          parsed.hash ||
          (parsed.pathname !== '' && parsed.pathname !== '/')
        ) {
          throw new HomeClientError(
            'INVALID_INPUT',
            'Use a trusted backend address without a path, query, or password.',
          );
        }
        return parsed.origin;
      }
    
      /** Persist backend coordination config (account token stays in SecureStorage). */
      async configureBackend(backendUrl: string, accountToken: string): Promise<string> {
        const origin = this.normalizeBaseUrl(backendUrl);
        const token = accountToken.trim();
        if (!token) {
          throw new HomeClientError('INVALID_INPUT', 'Enter an account token for this backend.');
        }
        await this.secure.setItem(BACKEND_URL_KEY, origin);
