    name: CI
    
    on:
      push:
        branches: [main]
      pull_request:
      workflow_dispatch:
    
    permissions:
      contents: read
    
    concurrency:
      group: ci-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
      cancel-in-progress: true
    
    jobs:
      repository-health:
        name: Repository health
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 5
        steps:
          - name: Check out repository
            uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
            with:
              persist-credentials: false
          - name: Check repository hygiene
            run: python3 scripts/check_repository.py
          - name: Check whitespace
            run: git show --format= --check HEAD
    
      # Offline fixture suite only. No live keys, no model endpoints, no Docker
      # pulls, no browser downloads: test_live_optin.py is never invoked here
      # (it skips by default) and the tests fail closed on absent backends.
      fixture-tests:
        name: Fixture runtime tests
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 15
        steps:
          - name: Check out repository
            uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
            with:
              persist-credentials: false
          - name: Create virtual environment
            run: python3 -m venv .venv
          - name: Install exact pinned requirements
            run: .venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt
          - name: Install runtime package (editable, no deps)
            run: .venv/bin/pip install --no-deps -e .
          - name: Run offline fixture + mocked transport/sandbox tests
            run: .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests --ignore=tests/test_live_optin.py -v
            env:
              ME_RUNTIME_LIVE_TESTS: ""
    version: 2
    updates:
      - package-ecosystem: github-actions
        directory: /
        schedule:
          interval: weekly
          day: monday
        open-pull-requests-limit: 5
        groups:
          github-actions:
            patterns: ['*']

        name: Repository health
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 5
        steps:
          - name: Check out repository
            uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
            with:
              persist-credentials: false
          - name: Check repository hygiene
            run: python3 scripts/check_repository.py
          - name: Check whitespace
            run: git show --format= --check HEAD
    
      setup-tests:
        name: Setup unit tests + dev smoke
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 10
        steps:
          - name: Check out repository
            uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
            with:
              persist-credentials: false
          - name: Set up Node.js (matches home-api-v1 local requirement)
            uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1faee2d65b9227c12c00848 # v4.4.0
            with:
              node-version: 24.18.0
          - name: Run setup unit tests
            run: python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_me_setup.py' -v
          - name: Run lifecycle unit tests
            # Integration cases needing ../infra-server skip with a transient note;
            # unit, guardrail, backup/restore, and tunnel fail-closed tests run here.
            run: python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_me_lifecycle.py' -v
          - name: Smoke-test rerunnable setup and check
            run: |
              DEST="$(mktemp -d)/me-home"
              python3 scripts/me_setup.py setup --data-dir "$DEST"
              python3 scripts/me_setup.py setup --data-dir "$DEST"
              python3 scripts/me_setup.py check --data-dir "$DEST"
              python3 scripts/me_setup.py config-show --data-dir "$DEST" > /dev/null
              test -f "$DEST/config/service.env"
    name: CI
    
    on:
      push:
        branches: [main]
      pull_request:
      workflow_dispatch:
    
    permissions:
      contents: read
    
    concurrency:
      group: ci-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
      cancel-in-progress: true
    
    jobs:
      repository-health:
        name: Repository health
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 5
        steps:
          - name: Check out repository
            uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
            with:
              persist-credentials: false
          - name: Check repository hygiene
            run: python3 scripts/check_repository.py
          - name: Check whitespace
            run: git show --format= --check HEAD
    
      # Portable unit/fixture tests. Always run: zero runtime dependencies, no
      # sibling checkouts, no devices, no tunnels.
      unit-tests:
        name: Portable client tests
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 10
        steps:
          - name: Check out repository
            uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
            with:
              persist-credentials: false
          - name: Set up Node
            uses: actions/setup-node@5c79832639c874aef5db836a6f0ef7f26540b45 # v6.1.0
            with:
              node-version: "24.18.0"
          - name: Run portable unit tests
            run: npm test
    
      # Real-services lifecycle (H1 home + B1 backend + real client) is
      # MANUAL ONLY via workflow_dispatch, and it tests whatever is on the
      # siblings' default branches at that moment. Sibling B3/F3/H5 features
      # are still uncommitted, so this job MUST NOT be read as validating
      # unmerged work: a coordinated merge of all repos is required before any
      # release claim. Missing siblings fail the job with an explicit message
      # (never a silent pass or skip-as-success).
      real-services-manual:
        name: Real-services integration (manual)
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 20
        if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
        steps:
          - name: Check out phone-app
            uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
            with:
              persist-credentials: false
              path: phone-app
          - name: Check out infra-server sibling (default branch)
            uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
            with:
              repository: mehomeai/infra-server
              persist-credentials: false
              path: infra-server
          - name: Check out backend-server sibling (default branch)
            uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
            with:
              repository: mehomeai/backend-server
              persist-credentials: false
              path: backend-server
          - name: Set up Node
            uses: actions/setup-node@5c79832639c874aef5db836a6f0ef7f26540b45 # v6.1.0
            with:
              node-version: "24.18.0"
          - name: Verify sibling checkouts present

        """Explicit strict checkpoint serializer (no pickle, allowlist only).
    
        Documented maintainer approach: JsonPlusSerializer with
        allowed_msgpack_modules=None (only SAFE_MSGPACK_TYPES) and
        pickle_fallback=False. Complements LANGGRAPH_STRICT_MSGPACK=true set
        at import time for any default-constructed serializer.
        """
        from langgraph.checkpoint.serde.jsonplus import JsonPlusSerializer
        return JsonPlusSerializer(pickle_fallback=False,
                                  allowed_msgpack_modules=None)

    name: Evaluate OpenMuse upstream update
    
    on:
      schedule:
        - cron: '17 9 * * 1'
      workflow_dispatch:
        inputs:
          revision:
            description: 'Optional full upstream commit SHA; empty checks main'
            required: false
            type: string
    
    permissions:
      contents: read
    
    concurrency:
      group: upstream-openmuse
      cancel-in-progress: false
    
    jobs:
      candidate:
        name: Test upstream without publishing credentials
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 10
        outputs:
          changed: ${{ steps.update.outputs.changed }}
          revision: ${{ steps.update.outputs.revision }}
          previous_revision: ${{ steps.update.outputs.previous_revision }}
          base_revision: ${{ steps.baseline.outputs.revision }}
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}
              persist-credentials: false
          - name: Record the exact baseline tested
            id: baseline
            run: printf 'revision=%s\n' "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          - uses: actions/setup-node@249970729cb0ef3589644e2896645e5dc5ba9c38 # v6
            with:
              node-version: 24.18.0
          - name: Verify updater before downloading code
            run: python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py' -v
          - name: Prepare fixed-path upstream candidate
            id: update
            env:
              REQUESTED_REVISION: ${{ inputs.revision }}
            shell: bash
            run: |
              args=()
              if [ -n "$REQUESTED_REVISION" ]; then
                args+=(--revision "$REQUESTED_REVISION")
              fi
              python3 scripts/upstream.py update "${args[@]}" --bundle "$RUNNER_TEMP/upstream-candidate"
          - name: Verify and test candidate
            if: steps.update.outputs.changed == 'true'
            run: |
              python3 scripts/upstream.py verify
              npm run test:spike
              npm run demo:spike
          - name: Save only candidate source data
            if: steps.update.outputs.changed == 'true'
            uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4
            with:
              name: openmuse-candidate
              path: ${{ runner.temp }}/upstream-candidate
              if-no-files-found: error
              retention-days: 7
    
      propose:
        name: Open a review PR without executing candidate code
        needs: candidate
        if: needs.candidate.outputs.changed == 'true'
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 5
        permissions:
          contents: write
          pull-requests: write
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
            with:
              ref: ${{ needs.candidate.outputs.base_revision }}
              persist-credentials: false
          - uses: actions/download-artifact@634f93cb2916e3fdff6788551b99b062d0335ce0 # v5
            with:
              name: openmuse-candidate
              path: ${{ runner.temp }}/upstream-candidate
          - name: Validate candidate data with the approved updater
            env:
              REVISION: ${{ needs.candidate.outputs.revision }}
            run: python3 scripts/upstream.py promote --bundle "$RUNNER_TEMP/upstream-candidate" --revision "$REVISION"
          - name: Propose a source-pin update
            env:
              GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
              REVISION: ${{ needs.candidate.outputs.revision }}
              BASE_BRANCH: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}
              PREVIOUS_REVISION: ${{ needs.candidate.outputs.previous_revision }}
            shell: bash
            run: |
              branch="upstream/openmuse-$REVISION"
              if gh pr view "$branch" --json number >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo 'An update PR already exists for this revision.'
                exit 0
              fi
              git config user.name 'github-actions[bot]'
              git config user.email '41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com'
              git checkout -b "$branch"
              git add -- vendor/openmuse
              git diff --cached --quiet && exit 0
              git commit -m "chore: evaluate OpenMuse $REVISION"
              gh auth setup-git
              git push origin "$branch"
              cat > "$RUNNER_TEMP/upstream-pr.md" <<'BODY'
              Refresh the fixed, unpatched OpenMuse worker subset and its source hashes.
    
              The candidate passed the model-free home integration suite and demonstration
              before publishing. Candidate tests run separately from this write-token job.
    
              This refresh imports only the listed worker files. New upstream UI,
              tools, and features need explicit adoption and their own acceptance checks.
    
              Review the source/license diff, household isolation implications, missing
              imports, and API changes. These tests do not cover a live model, browser,
              phone/backend transport, production authorization, or upstream's full build.
    
              This PR does not merge or deploy automatically. GitHub-token-created PRs
              may not trigger push/PR workflows: manually dispatch CI on this branch
              or use a dedicated GitHub App if independently triggered PR checks are required.
              BODY
              printf '\nFull upstream comparison: https://github.com/CopilotKit/openmuse/compare/%s...%s\n' "$PREVIOUS_REVISION" "$REVISION" >> "$RUNNER_TEMP/upstream-pr.md"
              printf '\nCandidate run: %s/%s/actions/runs/%s\n' "$GITHUB_SERVER_URL" "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" >> "$RUNNER_TEMP/upstream-pr.md"
              gh pr create --base "$BASE_BRANCH" --head "$branch" --title "chore: evaluate OpenMuse $REVISION" --body-file "$RUNNER_TEMP/upstream-pr.md"

    # runtime-delegation — R8 durable non-blocking delegation (runtime half)
    
    Version: `runtime-bridge-v1` + `task-rpc-v1` · Status: implemented (R8) ·
    Owner: `agentic-framework` · Home contract frozen:
    `../infra-server/docs/runtime-task-rpc-v1.md` + `home-h6-handoff.md` (read-only).
    
    The agent loop stays owned by the maintained LangGraph prebuilt ReAct
    harness with persisted SqliteSaver checkpoint. No custom AI planner, no
    second job engine. Home is the single durable authority (leases, limits,
    fanout/depth/root, wake CAS, cancel cascade); the runtime only requests
    narrowing and surfaces denials honestly.
    
    ## 1. task-rpc-v1 client (`src/me_runtime/task_rpc.py`)
    
    - fd from `ME_HOME_TASK_RPC_FD` (default 3), duplex JSONL, possession is the
      capability. Main stdin stays exactly one JSON object read to EOF.
    - Validates fd is socket/FIFO (not regular file/dir/device); dups + sets
      non-inheritable so Docker/curl/browser children never inherit it.
      `sanitize_child_env()` strips `ME_HOME_TASK_RPC_FD` + `*_PROXY` from every
      spawned transport (exec/curl/browser).
    - Bounds (both sides): 64KiB line, 32KiB params, 128KiB response, 512KiB
      buffered without newline, 256KiB pending writes, 200 requests/run (201st
      local `delegation_denied`), IDs 1..128 chars or safe ints, methods 1..64,
      params objects only. Split UTF-8 via incremental decoder, batched lines in
      order, no unbounded `readline`. Thread-safe: single write lock + reader
      thread routing by ID for concurrent ToolNode calls.
    - Cancellation/deadline honoured; missing RPC → honest `prerequisite_missing`
      (legacy runs unaffected); home errors (`bad_request/capability_denied/
      delegation_denied/delegation_conflict/not_found/wrong_state`) propagate
      with code + short message only — never request contents/credentials/logs.
      Unknown/cross-scope child IDs are denials, no fallback local tasks.
    
    ## 2. Brokered tools (`src/me_runtime/tools/delegate.py`)
    
    Explicit allowlist only (asserted in `agent.py`):
    `delegate_task/list_children/get_child/await_children` plus the nine R7 tools.
    
    - `delegate_task(key, request, title?, capabilities?, budgets?)` — submits one
      independent child via `submit_child`. Key is the stable idempotency key
      (1..128) scoped to parent; same key + identical hash returns existing child,
      different hash is `delegation_conflict`. Home inherits owner/conversation/
      model and narrows caps/budgets; the tool can only request narrowing.
      Immediate return lets the parent continue other work then `ask_user`; no
      LLM polling loop. Denials (disabled/fanout/depth/root) surface honestly,
      no recursive bomb.
    - `list_children()` / `get_child(id)` — direct children only, never global
      lookup. Unknown IDs are `not_found`.
    - `await_children(child_ids?)` — lists direct children; when any target is
      active (`queued/running/waiting_*/`) interrupts with
      `{kind:waiting_children, children:[...], mode:interrupt}`; resumes with
      trusted home `child_results` when all terminal. All-terminal returns
      immediately with summaries (no interrupt). Results are bounded trusted DATA
      (success output ≤2000 chars + artifact metadata; failures/cancels included
      honestly), never treated as instructions.
    
    Home selects owner/conversation/model/caps/budgets; fanout 3/depth 1/root 4
    defaults (configurable, any 0 disables) are home-enforced.
    
    ## 3. Bridge (`src/me_runtime/bridge.py`, runtime-bridge-v1 compatible)
    
    - New terminal `waiting_children` with `children:[ids]` (plus `child_ids`
      compat). Validates pending run/user/conv/workspace + expected child IDs;
      persistence via SqliteSaver `graph.db` (strict serde, [R9]) + private `pending.json` metadata
      (`kind/mode/children/seen/budgets/active_wall_seconds`). For Graph interrupts,

      publishes. The bridge stores private handoff (`mode:completed_early`,

      bounded child DATA into the SAME checkpoint and invokes a continuation
      (same `thread_id`), not a rerun of the original goal/tools. Unseen
      terminal outputs are collected once (tracked `seen` IDs, checkpoint-
      idempotent); continuations honour cumulative `max_steps/recursion`,
      `max_tool_calls`, and active wall budgets (`active_wall_seconds` carried in pending, no
      silent reset; paused waits excluded, legacy `wall_start` migrates one-time). Child outputs are DATA, errors included honestly.

    """Chat-model adapters on maintained SDK interfaces.
    
    - `local`     → langchain-ollama ChatOllama (local-first, no key).
    - `openai`    → langchain-openai ChatOpenAI against an explicitly configured
      remote OpenAI-compatible endpoint, only with ME_RUNTIME_ALLOW_REMOTE=1.
      Supports `use_responses_api: true` where the installed SDK accepts it.
    - `anthropic` → langchain-anthropic ChatAnthropic, same opt-in rule.
    - `fixture`   → deterministic offline FixtureChatModel implementing the
      LangChain chat-model interface (tool-call round trips through the real
      harness). TEST-ONLY: instantiated only for provider=fixture; its
      ASK:/APPROVE:/etc. directives are never a production planner.
    
    Secrets come only from environment variables named by `api_key_env`; the
    request itself must never carry a key, and keys are never logged or echoed
    into events.
    """
    from __future__ import annotations
    
    import itertools
    import os
    import sys
    from dataclasses import dataclass
    from typing import Any
    
    from langchain_core.callbacks import CallbackManagerForLLMRun
    from langchain_core.language_models.chat_models import BaseChatModel
    from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage, BaseMessage, HumanMessage
    from langchain_core.outputs import ChatGeneration, ChatResult
    
    RUN_FAILED_PREFIX = "RUN-FAILED"
    
    
    class ModelError(Exception):
        def __init__(self, code: str, message: str) -> None:
            super().__init__(message)
            self.code = code
    
    
    @dataclass
    class ModelConfig:
        provider: str
        model: str
        endpoint: str | None = None
        api_key_env: str | None = None
        use_responses_api: bool = False
    
    
    def model_config_from(obj: dict[str, Any]) -> ModelConfig:
        if not isinstance(obj, dict):
            raise ModelError("invalid_request", "model must be an object")
        provider = obj.get("provider")
        model = obj.get("model")
        if not provider or not isinstance(provider, str):
            raise ModelError("invalid_request", "model.provider is required")
        if not model or not isinstance(model, str):
            raise ModelError("invalid_request", "model.model is required")
        return ModelConfig(
            provider=provider,
            model=model,
            endpoint=obj.get("endpoint"),
            api_key_env=obj.get("api_key_env"),
            use_responses_api=bool(obj.get("use_responses_api", False)),
        )
    
    
    def _require_remote_opt_in(provider: str, api_key_env: str | None) -> str:
        if os.environ.get("ME_RUNTIME_ALLOW_REMOTE") != "1":
            raise ModelError(
                "model_not_configured",
                f"remote provider {provider!r} requires "
                "ME_RUNTIME_ALLOW_REMOTE=1 (explicit opt-in)")
        env_name = api_key_env or "ME_RUNTIME_MODEL_API_KEY"
        key = os.environ.get(env_name)
        if not key:
            raise ModelError("model_not_configured",
                             f"remote provider {provider!r} needs {env_name} set")
        return key
    
    
    def build_chat_model(cfg: ModelConfig):
        """Return a LangChain chat model for the configured provider."""
        provider = cfg.provider
        if provider == "fixture":
            return FixtureChatModel()
        if provider == "local":
            from langchain_ollama import ChatOllama
            base_url = (cfg.endpoint or os.environ.get(
                "ME_RUNTIME_LOCAL_ENDPOINT", "http://127.0.0.1:11434"))
            # Privacy: Ollama python client forwards kwargs to httpx (trust_env
            # defaults True, so HTTP_PROXY could route loopback prompts off-host).
            # Pin loopback transport to ignore ambient proxy env. Remote providers
            # stay explicit opt-in and unchanged.
            return ChatOllama(model=cfg.model, base_url=base_url,
                              temperature=0.2,
                              sync_client_kwargs={"trust_env": False},
                              async_client_kwargs={"trust_env": False})
        if provider == "openai":
            # Any provider=openai use — even a localhost URL — requires the
            # explicit remote opt-in so a remote URL can never be mislabelled
            # to skip privacy checks.
            key = _require_remote_opt_in("openai", cfg.api_key_env)
            from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
            kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {
                "model": cfg.model, "api_key": key, "temperature": 0.2}
            if cfg.endpoint:
                kwargs["base_url"] = cfg.endpoint
            if cfg.use_responses_api:
                try:
                    kwargs["use_responses_api"] = True
                    return ChatOpenAI(**kwargs)
                except TypeError:
                    del kwargs["use_responses_api"]
                    print("[runtime] installed langchain-openai does not "
                          "accept use_responses_api; using Chat Completions",
                          file=sys.stderr)
            return ChatOpenAI(**kwargs)
        if provider == "anthropic":
            key = _require_remote_opt_in("anthropic", cfg.api_key_env)
            from langchain_anthropic import ChatAnthropic
            kwargs = {"model": cfg.model, "api_key": key, "temperature": 0.2}
            if cfg.endpoint:
                kwargs["base_url"] = cfg.endpoint
            return ChatAnthropic(**kwargs)
        raise ModelError("invalid_request",
                         f"unknown model.provider {provider!r}")
    """Agent loop owned by the maintained LangGraph prebuilt ReAct harness.
    
    `build_agent` wires exactly the brokered Me tools — no framework default
    filesystem/shell/subagent tools — into `create_react_agent`. The model
    (either a maintained chat adapter or the test-only fixture stub) drives
    standard tool-call round trips; this module contains no custom planner,
    no manual /chat/completions parsing, and no parallel task scheduler.
    
    R9: `create_react_agent` is deprecated upstream since 1.0 in favour of
    `langchain.agents.create_agent` (LangGraphDeprecatedSinceV10, to be removed
    in V2). The alias remains supported in the pinned 1.x line and preserves
    0.6 checkpoint resume compat, so it is kept here with truthful docs; the
    ToolNode is constructed explicitly with handle_tool_errors=True to restore
    0.6 semantics where broker denials (ToolDeniedError) become error
    ToolMessages for the model instead of aborting the run (1.x default only
    handles ToolInvocationError).
    """
    from __future__ import annotations
    
    import threading
    from typing import Any
    
    from langgraph.prebuilt import create_react_agent
    
    from .models import FixtureChatModel
    from .tools.animate import make_animate_tools
    from .tools.delegate import make_delegate_tools
    from .tools.exec import make_exec_tools
    from .tools.files import make_files_tools
    from .tools.interact import make_interact_tools
    from .tools.web import make_web_tools
    from .workspace import Workspace
    
    SYSTEM_PROMPT = """You are Me, a home agent. You act ONLY through the tools
    provided by the home: scoped files, gated web fetch/browser, sandboxed
    code execution, animation building, and explicit user questions/approvals.
    Rules:
    - Never claim to have done work you did not do via tools; never fabricate
      file contents, fetch results, renders, or approvals.
    - Stay inside the granted capabilities. If a tool reports a denial or
      error you cannot recover from, end your reply with exactly:
      RUN-FAILED <code>: <message>
      using the code from the tool error.
    - Keep replies short; the home delivers your final text and artifacts.
    """
    
    EXPECTED_TOOL_NAMES = sorted([
        "files_read", "files_list", "files_write",
        "web_fetch", "browser_open",
        "run_code",
        "animation_build",
        "ask_user", "request_approval",
        "delegate_task", "list_children", "get_child", "await_children",
    ])
    
    
    class RunTools:
        """Per-run broker state shared by tool closures (no global state)."""
    
        def __init__(self, run_id: str, user_id: str, conversation_id: str,
                     cancelled: threading.Event,
                     task_rpc=None, capabilities: dict | None = None,
                     budgets: dict | None = None) -> None:
            self.run_id = run_id
            self.user_id = user_id
            self.conversation_id = conversation_id
            self.cancelled = cancelled
            self.artifacts: list[dict] = []
            self.task_rpc = task_rpc
            self.capabilities = dict(capabilities or {})
            self.budgets = dict(budgets or {})
    
        def record_artifact(self, path: str, data: bytes) -> None:
            import hashlib
            self.artifacts.append({
                "path": path, "bytes": len(data),
                "sha256": hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()})
    
    
    def build_tools(ws: Workspace, capabilities: dict, ctx: RunTools
                    ) -> list[Any]:
        tools = []
        tools += make_files_tools(ws, capabilities, ctx.record_artifact)
        tools += make_web_tools(ws, capabilities, ctx.record_artifact,
                                ctx.run_id, ctx.user_id, ctx.conversation_id,
                                ctx.cancelled)
        tools += make_exec_tools(ws, capabilities, ctx.run_id,
                                 ctx.record_artifact, ctx.cancelled)
        tools += make_animate_tools(ws, capabilities, ctx.record_artifact)
        tools += make_interact_tools(ctx.run_id)
        tools += make_delegate_tools(ctx, capabilities, ctx.budgets)
        names = sorted(t.name for t in tools)
        assert names == EXPECTED_TOOL_NAMES, f"tool allowlist drift: {names}"
        return tools
    
    
    def build_agent(model, tools: list[Any], checkpointer=None):
        """Compile the maintained prebuilt ReAct agent (harness-owned loop)."""
        from langgraph.prebuilt import ToolNode
        scoped_prompt = (f"{SYSTEM_PROMPT}\n"
                         f"[run context: user and conversation are labelled by "
                         f"the home; only workspace files and supplied context "
                         f"are visible]")
        # Explicit ToolNode restores 0.6 tool-error semantics (denials as error
        # ToolMessages) on LangGraph 1.x; create_react_agent accepts ToolNode.
        tool_node = ToolNode(tools, handle_tool_errors=True)
        return create_react_agent(model, tool_node, prompt=scoped_prompt,
                                  checkpointer=checkpointer)
    
    
    def is_fixture_model(model) -> bool:
        return isinstance(model, FixtureChatModel)

    # Me product architecture
    
    Canonical product understanding, based on the user's clarification on 2026-11-02. This document supersedes contradictory hosting assumptions in the earlier personal-agent plans. It describes intended boundaries; the runtime repositories are currently bootstrap repositories.
    
    Implementation must follow the [whole-product delivery plan](product-delivery-plan.md). Agent framework choices, home infrastructure, hosted services, installation, and the phone experience must be developed and validated together.
    
    The existing phone frontend is being prototyped in
    `/Users/kgensupertramp/Downloads/Personal-AI-Showcase-3/artifacts/me-mobile`
    (Expo/React Native). Preserve that frontend as the UI baseline. Its inspected
    surface and integration assumptions are documented in the `phone-app`
    repository's `docs/frontend-prototype.md`; alternative agent products are not
    the default replacement for this UI.
    
    ## Confirmed deployment model
    
    Me is a personal/family agent that runs on a separate computer in the user's home. The user can buy that computer or use a suitable spare computer they already own. The phone is the interface to the agent. Me operates a hosted backend that connects the phone experience with the user's home infrastructure.
    
    The home computer also hosts household user data, including conversations and their history. One installation must serve multiple family members/users and multiple chat sessions, including concurrent sessions. It is a persistent household service, rather than a single-user agent process with one conversation.
    
    Independent execution means the home computer can continue work when the phone app is closed or offline. It does not mean the agent is hosted in Me's cloud, and it does not require controlling the user's everyday laptop or desktop. A spare computer intentionally provisioned as the home host becomes the agent's dedicated execution environment.
    
    ```mermaid
    flowchart TD
      User[User] --> Phone[phone-app: agent interface]
      Phone <-->|Accounts and home coordination| Backend[backend-server: hosted by Me]
      Phone <-->|Proposed paired-device API route| Tunnel[Protected public endpoint and tunnel]
      Tunnel <-->|Outbound home connector| Home[infra-server: user's home computer]
      Backend <-->|Authenticated coordination or selected relay| Home
      Setup[setup-infra: installer and maintenance tooling] --> Home
      Home --> Agent[agentic-framework: agent runtime]
      Agent --> Models[Model inference]
      Agent --> Tools[Browser, isolated code and render workers, integrations]
      Home --> Data[Local users, conversations, memory, tasks, files and artifacts]
      Tools --> External[External services within approved scope]
    ```
    
    The connection shown is logical. The 2026-11-03 clarification adds a protected
    public home endpoint through a tunnel and one-time phone pairing. The hosted
    backend remains responsible for account/home coordination. Paired phones may
    use that endpoint directly; always relaying private traffic through our backend
    is no longer a fixed assumption. Transport, edge admission, encryption, and the
    final routing mode remain engineering decisions. The proposed handshake is
    recorded in `infra-server/docs/connection-and-pairing.md`.
    
    ## Repository responsibilities
    
    | Repository | Where it runs | Responsibility |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | `phone-app` | User's phone | Agent conversations, tasks, progress, clarification answers, approvals, results, household controls, and home pairing |
    | `backend-server` | Me's hosted infrastructure | Application API, user/account identity, home registration and access, phone-to-home coordination, and notification delivery; exact relay/storage boundaries require design |
    | `infra-server` | User's separate home computer | Home service/API, authenticated connection with our backend, household membership/access enforcement, multi-user conversation and data persistence, lifecycle of local agent and execution services, resource management, and health |
    | `agentic-framework` | Within the user's home environment | Agent planning, model/tool integration, capability execution, task dependencies, clarification behavior, memory access, permissions, and task recovery |
    | `setup-infra` | During installation/maintenance on the home computer | Prerequisite/hardware checks, installation, configuration, registration/pairing, service startup, upgrades, diagnostics, and recovery tooling |
    | `web-app` | Public website hosting | Explain the product and provide the existing showcase/waitlist; later onboarding links can connect to the phone/setup experience |
    | `feed-algorithm` | Placement to be finalized | Feed ranking, goal controls, and ranking evaluation; access to personal context must be explicit |
    
    `setup-infra` prepares and maintains the home deployment; `infra-server` operates it. `agentic-framework` is the execution engine used there, rather than another public hosted backend. Browser, coding, and animation capabilities should run in isolated environments on the home host by default.
    
    ## Household data and multiple sessions
    
    Confirmed requirements: the home stores users' conversations and other personal data, supports multiple household users, and supports multiple chat sessions. The structure and isolation rules below are proposed implementation defaults.
    
    ```text
    Home installation
      Household membership and shared resources
      User A
        Private profile, memories, files and connected accounts
        Conversation 1 -> messages, attachments, tasks and results
        Conversation 2 -> messages, attachments, tasks and results
      User B
    # Me whole-product delivery plan
    
    Status: proposed cross-repository implementation plan, 2026-11-02. Product requirements and deployment boundaries are recorded in [product architecture](product-architecture.md). This plan does not select a final agent framework or claim an implemented system.
    
    ## Working principle
    
    The user's implementation preference is reuse first: use as much suitable existing code as possible. Prefer adapting an existing application or embedding maintained components over building equivalent subsystems. The repository boundaries describe responsibility; they do not require seven independently written implementations.
    
    Develop one integrated product across the repositories. A feature is complete when the user can install the required home services, access it from the phone through our hosted backend, use it with the correct identity and permissions, recover from interruptions, and retrieve its persisted result.
    
    Evaluate open-source agent reuse against that complete path. A successful standalone framework demo is useful evidence, but it is not a completed Me feature. Treat `infra-server` as a first-class product service throughout runtime development, rather than deployment work deferred until afterward.
    
    ## Reuse before implementation
    
    The user-provided Expo application in `Personal-AI-Showcase-3/artifacts/me-mobile`
    is the existing phone frontend baseline. Preserve its screens and interactions;
    reuse external applications for missing runtime/tools and specific UI gaps.
    The inspected frontend map is recorded in `phone-app/docs/frontend-prototype.md`.
    
    First evaluate an existing product as the baseline, rather than assembling a new platform from unrelated libraries by default. OpenMuse is a candidate for application/UI/workflow reuse; OpenClaw is a candidate for a home-hosted assistant baseline. Their inspected limitations still apply: OpenMuse's service dependencies and single-owner model need adaptation, and OpenClaw's shared gateway trust boundary does not automatically provide private family-user isolation. Neither is selected without an integrated run.
    
    If no complete application fits, use an embeddable harness such as Deep Agents/LangGraph and adopt existing client, worker, and infrastructure components around it. Do not implement a custom agent loop or dependency scheduler merely because the system design names those responsibilities. Define the required semantics, then map them to an existing implementation before writing code.
    
    | Product need | Default reuse approach | Custom work only where needed |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | Phone/web agent interface | Adapt existing mobile/chat/task/approval components, with OpenMuse as an inspected candidate | Me navigation, home pairing, household UX, and home/backend API integration |
    | Agent planning, context and tools | Configure/embed one maintained agent runtime | Me capability adapters, policy integration, and validated behavior |
    | Durable work, input waits and recovery | Reuse the selected product/runtime's worker and persistence; evaluate another workflow engine only for a demonstrated gap | Mapping Me task states/events and any missing durable semantics |
    | Models | Existing inference servers and model adapters | Hardware profiles, resource configuration, model selection/evaluation |
    | Browser execution | Existing browser automation or browser-agent library | User/profile scopes, approved access, home lifecycle, and result delivery |
    | Coding and debugging | Existing file/terminal tools or a proven coding-agent SDK | Isolated workspaces, permissions, artifacts, and phone presentation |
    | Animation | Existing render engines, templates, and authoring tools | Agent workflow, resource budgets, output checking, preview/export |
    | Data and identity | Established database, authentication, migration, retrieval, and storage libraries | Household/conversation ownership, access rules, retention and sharing |
    | Home installation/operation | Existing packaging, service management, isolation, health and backup tooling | Me installer configuration, pairing, compatibility checks, upgrade orchestration |
    | Phone-to-home connectivity | Existing authenticated transport and connection-management components | Me identity binding, routing, privacy decisions, and delivery semantics |
    
    Custom work should concentrate on the product's distinct boundary: our hosted backend connects authorized phones to a user-owned home server that serves multiple private users and conversations. Reuse existing approval, memory, event, and persistence primitives where possible rather than rebuilding each behind a new name.
    
    The first research deliverable is a reuse inventory: exact repository/package and pinned revision, license/service dependencies, demonstrated working behavior, modifications needed, update strategy, and which Me repository owns its configuration/adapter. Compare a full-baseline adaptation against component assembly using the same end-to-end scenario. Prefer the path with less custom code and lower ongoing maintenance that still satisfies privacy, isolation, and hardware constraints; do not optimize for code reuse percentage alone.
    
    Keep upstream history and notices when importing code. Use configuration/extensions or a thin maintained fork rather than rewriting a working subsystem. Keep an upstream patch ledger so future updates are practical. Begin with a working integrated baseline and move/extract code across Me repositories incrementally; repository neatness should not delay proving the product.
    
    ## Responsibilities that must stay distinct
    
    | Area | Primary owner | Collaborators |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | Account identity, home registration, authenticated routing | `backend-server` | `phone-app`, `infra-server`, `setup-infra` |
    | Household membership enforcement, conversation/history service, local data and artifact access | `infra-server` | `backend-server`, `phone-app`, `agentic-framework` |
    | Accepted-job lifecycle, durable dispatch, worker supervision, resource scheduling, home health | `infra-server` | `agentic-framework`, `setup-infra` |
    | Agent plan, step dependencies, model context, tool selection, task-specific completion checks | `agentic-framework` | `infra-server`, `phone-app` |
    | Household policy administration and durable approval records | `infra-server` | `phone-app`, `backend-server`, `agentic-framework` |
    | Enforcement immediately before a tool runs | Home tool broker, defined with `infra-server` and `agentic-framework` | Execution workers |
    | Installation, prerequisites, service configuration, upgrade/recovery tooling | `setup-infra` | `infra-server`, `agentic-framework`, `backend-server` |
    | Conversation/task experience, onboarding, questions, approvals, results and controls | `phone-app` | All runtime services |
    | Goal-driven feed ranking and evaluation | `feed-algorithm` | `infra-server`, `phone-app` |
    | Public explanation, waitlist, supported-hardware/setup guidance | `web-app` | `setup-infra`, product |
    
    The home job manager owns whether a run is accepted, queued, active, cancelled, or recovered. The agent owns the plan and execution state inside that run. Use one durable authority for each transition; do not create independent schedulers that both believe they can retry or dispatch the same action.
    
    Conversations and personal data are home-service records accessed through authorized interfaces. A selected framework may keep its own versioned internal checkpoints, but must not become the only way to read/export a person's conversation history. The hosted backend owns delivery/routing state, not an independent copy of the home task lifecycle.
    
    ## Interfaces to define before implementation fans out
    
    Connection clarification (2026-11-03): setup should provision a protected public
    home endpoint through a tunnel and enroll phones with a one-time invitation.
    # End-to-end runbook — Me home service (infra-server)
    
    How to install, configure, pair, run, and verify the household home service
    across the sibling repositories. Authoritative API contract:
    `contracts/home-api-v1.md` (+ `.openapi.json`). This runbook coordinates
    commands and manual gates; it does not duplicate the contract.
    
    Conventions: `<me>` is the directory holding the sibling checkouts
    (`infra-server`, `agentic-framework`, `backend-server`, `phone-app`,
    `setup-infra`, …). All home commands run from `<me>/infra-server` unless noted.
    Do not run home commands from another repository.
    
    ## 0. Prerequisites (local-first)
    
    - Node.js 24.18.x: `node --version` must print `v24.18.x`. Any install method
      works; one option is nvm (`nvm install 24.18.0`).
    - Python 3 for repository hygiene scripts (`python3 --version`).
    - The home service needs Node's type-stripping for the vendored worker import,
      so **every** home entrypoint carries the flag (already baked into
      `package.json` scripts):
      `node --experimental-transform-types …`
    - No `npm install` is required inside `infra-server` (stdlib only, no
      dependencies). Do not download heavy packages for home verification
      (environment budget is ~1 GiB free).
    - R1/R2 runtime lives in the sibling checkout `<me>/agentic-framework` with
      its own venv at `<me>/agentic-framework/.venv`. The home never installs or
      modifies it; it only spawns `<venv>/bin/python -m me_runtime.bridge`.
    - Local-first model default requires Ollama on the home host
      (`http://127.0.0.1:11434`); without it, task runs honestly report
      `model_not_configured` until a model is configured (see §2).
    
    ## 1. Start the home service
    
    ```sh
    node --version            # v24.18.x required
    npm run start:home -- --db=data/home.sqlite --host=127.0.0.1 --port=7070
    # or explicitly:

        """Extract model-authored display text from a chat message.
    
        Prefers the maintained `AIMessage.text` API (handles `str` + standard
        text blocks; excludes reasoning/images/tool calls), then scans raw
        list content for provider text styles (`text`, `output_text`) the
        installed SDK leaves non-standard. Never stringifies reasoning,
        refusal, image, tool-call, or metadata blocks.
        """
        try:
            text = m.text
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
            text = ""
        if isinstance(text, str) and text.strip():
            return str(text)
        content = getattr(m, "content", None)
        if isinstance(content, str):
            return content
        if isinstance(content, list):
            parts: list[str] = []
            for block in content:
                if isinstance(block, str):
                    if block.strip():
                        parts.append(block)
                elif isinstance(block, dict):
                    if block.get("type") in _TEXT_BLOCK_TYPES:
                        t = block.get("text")
                        if isinstance(t, str) and t.strip():
                            parts.append(t)
            if parts:
                return "".join(parts)
        return "" if not isinstance(text, str) else str(text)
    
    
    def _final_text(messages: list) -> str:
        # Graph-final semantics: the terminal AIMessage carries the answer. An
        # intermediate message may hold narration alongside tool_calls, so pure
        # final text (no tool calls) wins; narration next to tool calls is only
        # a fallback when no pure final exists. An empty tool-call message never
        # contributes text, so extraction can no longer mask a structured final
        # as "" (which previously collapsed to "done").
        fallback = ""
        for m in reversed(messages):
            if not isinstance(m, AIMessage):
                continue
            text = _message_text(m)
            if not text.strip():
                continue
            if getattr(m, "tool_calls", None):
                if not fallback:
                    fallback = text
                continue
            return text
        return fallback

    def parse_ticket_stdin(*, max_bytes: int = TICKET_MAX_BYTES) -> dict:
        """Read the bounded one-time ticket JSON from STDIN. Never from argv."""
        data = sys.stdin.read(max_bytes + 1)
        if not data:
            raise CoordinatorError(
                "no ticket JSON on STDIN: pipe the one-time activation JSON "
                "(backend_url, ticketId, activationSecret, installationId) "
                "from the owner phone; never pass secrets via argv")
        if len(data) > max_bytes:
            raise CoordinatorError(
                f"ticket JSON exceeds {max_bytes} bytes; refusing to parse")
        try:
            ticket = json.loads(data)
        except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
            raise CoordinatorError(f"ticket JSON is not valid JSON ({exc})")
        if not isinstance(ticket, dict):
            raise CoordinatorError("ticket JSON must be an object")
        for secret_carrier in ("accountToken", "accountJwt", "authorization",
                               "homeToken", "home_token"):
            if secret_carrier in ticket:
                raise CoordinatorError(
                    f"ticket must not carry {secret_carrier!r}: activation is "
                    "ticket-only, never an account JWT or home token")
        return ticket
    
    
    def _ticket_str(ticket: dict, *names: str) -> str:
        for name in names:
            val = ticket.get(name)
            if isinstance(val, str) and val.strip():
                return val.strip()
        return ""
    
    
    class _NoRedirect(urllib.request.HTTPRedirectHandler):
        """Redirects are failures (never followed, no token forwarding)."""
    
        def redirect_request(self, req, fp, code, msg, headers, newurl):
            raise ActivationError(
                "backend redirect refused (redirects are failures; check "
                "backend_url; no credentials forwarded)")
    
    
    def _build_opener() -> urllib.request.OpenerDirector:
        return urllib.request.build_opener(_NoRedirect)
    
    
    def post_activate(*, backend_url: str, payload: dict,
                      timeout_ms: int) -> tuple[int, bytes]:
        """Single ticket-only POST. No Authorization header, no retries.
    
        Returns (status, bounded body). Transport failures raise ActivationError
        with unknown_outcome=True (the server may have persisted a credential
        this client never saw).
        """
        base = backend_url.rstrip("/")
        url = f"{base}/v1/homes/activate"
        try:
            body = json.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8")
        except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
            raise CoordinatorError(f"cannot encode activation request ({exc})")
        req = urllib.request.Request(
            url, data=body, method="POST",
            headers={"Content-Type": "application/json",
                     "Accept": "application/json"})
        # Deliberately NO Authorization header: the ticket IS the authorization.
        if "authorization" in {k.lower() for k in req.header_items()}:
            raise AssertionError("unreachable: Authorization must never be set")
        opener = _build_opener()
        timeout_s = timeout_ms / 1000.0
        try:
            with opener.open(req, timeout=timeout_s) as resp:
                status = int(getattr(resp, "status", 200) or 200)
                raw = resp.read(RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES + 1)
        except ActivationError:
            raise
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
            # HTTP error statuses still carry a bounded backend body; they are
            # KNOWN outcomes (validation/auth/replay), not unknown ones.
            try:
                raw = exc.read(RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES + 1)
            except OSError:
                raw = b""
            return int(exc.code or 0), bytes(raw[:RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES + 1])
        except (urllib.error.URLError, TimeoutError, OSError) as exc:
            raise ActivationError(
                "activation transport failed with UNKNOWN server outcome "
                f"({exc}); do NOT retry the same ticket (replay would report 410 "
                "without revealing whether the first attempt persisted). Mint a "
                "FRESH owner recovery ticket (existingHomeId) and redeem once.",
                unknown_outcome=True)
        except Exception as exc:  # defensive: never leak internals unredacted
            raise ActivationError(
                f"activation failed with UNKNOWN server outcome ({exc}); do NOT "
                "retry the same ticket; mint a FRESH owner recovery ticket "
                "(existingHomeId) and redeem once.",
                unknown_outcome=True)
        if len(raw) > RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES:
            raise ActivationError("backend response exceeds 64 KiB; refusing to parse")
        return status, bytes(raw)

    #!/usr/bin/env python3
    """S7 cloud-coordination activation (setup-infra ownership).
    
    Setup-side only: prepare/activate/status/check for home-coordinator-v1
    (file) over home-api-v1 (wire). The home (H8, infra-server/src/coordinator.mjs)
    owns the credential file + automatic heartbeat loop; the backend (B7,
    backend-server/docs/home-activation-v1.md) owns the ticket/activation wire.
    This module never edits siblings, never duplicates the heartbeat loop, and
    performs network I/O ONLY in `activate` (single ticket-only POST, no retries).
    
    Discipline (load-bearing):
    - Ticket JSON arrives via STDIN only (bounded, one-time). NEVER via argv
      (process listings leak argv), and NEVER an account JWT: activate sends NO
      `Authorization` header (the ticket IS the authorization).
    - Own installation_id is matched BEFORE any network. Mismatch => no fetch,
      ticket untouched.
    - endpointHint comes from LOCAL setup config (public_home_url / tunnel
      hostname), never from the ticket or any backend hint.
    - backend_url comes from the ticket JSON; validated HTTPS (explicit
      loopback-http opt-in only), no userinfo/query/fragment; redirects are
      failures (never followed); request/response/body/time all bounded; exactly
      one attempt, NO automatic redeem retries.
    - Unknown redemption outcome (timeout/disconnect) => do NOT replay the same
      ticket. Mint a FRESH owner recovery ticket and redeem once (rotation
      invalidates prior verifiers).
    - The persisted file matches home-coordinator-v1 EXACTLY (7 keys incl.
      protocol_version home-api-v1), written atomically to the protected
      secrets path (parent 0700, file 0600, no final symlink). Token/path
      contents are NEVER printed or logged. Destination writability is
      preflighted BEFORE the fetch to avoid a response-before-safe-storage gap;
      when storage still fails after a 201, the credential is lost locally and
      the operator must recover via a fresh ticket (documented in the message).
    
    Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 operation/state failure, 2 usage/validation.
    """
    
    from __future__ import annotations
    
    import io
    import json
    import os
    import re
    import stat
    import sys
    import tempfile
    import urllib.error
    import urllib.parse
    import urllib.request
    from pathlib import Path
    
    sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
    
    import me_setup
    
    PROTOCOL = "home-coordinator-v1"
    PROTOCOL_VERSION = "home-api-v1"
    TICKET_MAX_BYTES = 16 * 1024
    RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES = 64 * 1024
    FILE_MAX_BYTES = 16 * 1024
    REQUEST_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT_MS = 10_000
    REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MIN_MS = 1_000
    REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MAX_MS = 30_000
    
    HOME_ID_RE = re.compile(r"^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{2,63}$")
    INSTALLATION_ID_RE = re.compile(r"^[\x20-\x7E]{1,128}$")
    HOME_TOKEN_RE = re.compile(r"^me_home_[A-Za-z0-9_-]{32,128}$")
    EXPECTED_FILE_KEYS = ("protocol", "backend_url", "home_id", "installation_id",
                          "home_token", "endpoint_hint", "protocol_version")
    
    LOOPBACK_NAMES = ("127.0.0.1", "localhost", "::1")
    
    
    class CoordinatorError(Exception):
        """Usage/validation failure (exit 2)."""
    
    
    class ActivationError(Exception):
        """Operation/state failure (exit 1). Carries a redacted message."""
    
        def __init__(self, message: str, *, unknown_outcome: bool = False):
            super().__init__(message)
            self.unknown_outcome = unknown_outcome
    
    
    def log(msg: str) -> None:
        print(me_setup.redact(msg), flush=True)
    
    
    def err(msg: str) -> None:
        print(me_setup.redact(msg), file=sys.stderr, flush=True)

    // Minimal ambient types for the maintained Expo Clipboard API surface the
    // app uses (write-only copy of the one-time activation handoff). Kept narrow
    // on purpose: the app never reads the OS clipboard back. Fully typed, no
    // `any`; Metro resolves the real declared package on device installs.
    declare module 'expo-clipboard' {
      export function setStringAsync(text: string): Promise<boolean>;
    }
    // Typed clipboard boundary (F9 one-time activation handoff copy).
    //
    // The app copies the one-time activation JSON via the maintained Expo
    // Clipboard API (`expo-clipboard`, declared in apps/mobile/package.json).
    // This module owns the MINIMAL typed surface the app needs so the call site
    // stays honest (success/failure/unavailable) without importing the native
    // module directly:
    //
    // - `setStringAsync` parity: resolves true when the OS accepted the text.
    // - No read API is exposed: the one-time secret is write-only here and is
    //   never read back from the OS clipboard.
    //
    // Ambient declaration: the SDK types mirror used for verification does not
    // ship `expo-clipboard` types, so the exact minimal surface is declared here
    // (fully typed, no `any`). On a real install Metro resolves the declared
    // package; when the native module is missing the copy fails closed with an
    // honest "copy unavailable" state instead of a fake success.
    
    export interface ClipboardLike {
      setStringAsync(text: string): Promise<boolean>;
    }
    
    async function loadClipboard(): Promise<ClipboardLike | null> {
      try {
        const mod = (await import('expo-clipboard')) as unknown as Partial<ClipboardLike>;
        if (mod && typeof mod.setStringAsync === 'function') {
          return mod as ClipboardLike;
        }
        return null;
      } catch {
        return null;
      }
    }
    
    export type CopyResult =
      | { ok: true }
      | { ok: false; reason: string };
    
    /**
     * Copy text to the OS clipboard. Single attempt, no retries: reports the
     * real outcome so the UI can show an honest copied/failed state.
     */
    export async function copyTextToClipboard(
      text: string,
      loader: () => Promise<ClipboardLike | null> = loadClipboard,
    ): Promise<CopyResult> {
      if (!text) {
        return { ok: false, reason: 'Nothing to copy.' };
      }
      const clipboard = await loader();
      if (!clipboard) {
        return {
          ok: false,
          reason: 'Copy is unavailable in this build (clipboard module missing). Long-press to select the text manually.',
        };
      }
      try {
        const accepted = await clipboard.setStringAsync(text);
        if (accepted !== true) {
          return { ok: false, reason: 'The system did not accept the copy.' };
        }
        return { ok: true };
      } catch (error) {
        return {
          ok: false,
          reason: error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Copy failed.',
        };
      }
    }

    def persist_credentials_file(path: Path, *, backend_url: str,
                                 home_id: str, installation_id: str,
                                 home_token: str,
                                 endpoint_hint: str) -> None:
        """Atomically write the EXACT home-coordinator-v1 file (0600, no symlink).
    
        Raises ActivationError when storage fails. Callers treat a post-201
        storage failure as a lost credential: the server rotated/issued a token
        this home never stored, so recovery requires a FRESH ticket (rotation
        invalidates the lost one).
        """
        if os.path.islink(path):
            raise ActivationError(
                "refusing to write: credentials destination is a symlink")
        parent = path.parent
        try:
            parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            os.chmod(parent, 0o700)
        except OSError as exc:
            raise ActivationError(
                "cannot prepare credentials parent (lost credential: the server "
                f"may have issued a token never stored locally): {exc}")
        doc = {
            "protocol": PROTOCOL,
            "backend_url": backend_url,
            "home_id": home_id,
            "installation_id": installation_id,
            "home_token": home_token,
            "endpoint_hint": endpoint_hint,
            "protocol_version": PROTOCOL_VERSION,
        }
        text = json.dumps(doc, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n"
        if len(text.encode("utf-8")) > FILE_MAX_BYTES:
            raise ActivationError("credential document exceeds 16 KiB; refusing")
        fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=str(parent), prefix=path.name + ".")
        try:
            with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                f.write(text)
                try:
                    f.flush()
                    os.fsync(f.fileno())
                except OSError:
                    pass
            os.chmod(tmp, 0o600)
            if os.path.islink(path):
                raise ActivationError("refusing to write: destination became a symlink")
            os.replace(tmp, path)
            os.chmod(path, 0o600)
            try:
                dirfd = os.open(parent, os.O_DIRECTORY)

    def load_status_record(path: Path, *, expected_installation_id: str = "",
                           allow_http_loopback: bool = False) -> tuple[dict | None, str | None]:
        """Validate the persisted file like H8. Returns (record, error_code)."""
        try:
            if not path.is_absolute():
                return None, "invalid_credentials_path"
            if os.path.islink(path):
                return None, "invalid_credentials_file"
            try:
                st = os.stat(path)
            except OSError:
                return None, "credentials_unreadable"
            if not stat.S_ISREG(st.st_mode):
                return None, "invalid_credentials_file"
            if st.st_size <= 0 or st.st_size > FILE_MAX_BYTES:
                return None, "invalid_credentials_file"
            if st.st_mode & 0o077:
                return None, "invalid_credentials_permissions"
            try:
                parsed = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError):
                return None, "invalid_credentials_format"
            if not isinstance(parsed, dict):
                return None, "invalid_credentials_format"
            if set(parsed.keys()) != set(EXPECTED_FILE_KEYS):
                return None, "invalid_credentials_format"
            for key in EXPECTED_FILE_KEYS:
                if not isinstance(parsed[key], str):
                    return None, "invalid_credentials_format"
            if parsed["protocol"] != PROTOCOL:
                return None, "invalid_credentials_format"
            if parsed["protocol_version"] != PROTOCOL_VERSION:
                return None, "invalid_credentials_format"
            if not HOME_ID_RE.match(parsed["home_id"]):
                return None, "invalid_credentials_format"
            if not INSTALLATION_ID_RE.match(parsed["installation_id"]):
                return None, "invalid_credentials_format"
            if not HOME_TOKEN_RE.match(parsed["home_token"]):
                return None, "invalid_credentials_format"
            try:
                me_setup.validate_https_url(
                    parsed["backend_url"], field="backend_url",
                    allow_http_loopback=allow_http_loopback)
                me_setup.validate_https_url(
                    parsed["endpoint_hint"], field="endpoint_hint",
                    allow_http_loopback=allow_http_loopback)
            except me_setup.SetupError:
                return None, "invalid_credentials_format"
            if expected_installation_id and parsed["installation_id"] != expected_installation_id:
                return None, "wrong_home"
            return parsed, None
        except OSError:
            return None, "credentials_unreadable"

                   allow_http_loopback: bool = False,
                   update_config: bool = True) -> int:

        try:
            allow_lb = bool(allow_http_loopback) or allow_http_loopback_effective(
                (cfg.get("coordinator", {}) or {}))
            resolved_public = resolve_public_url(cfg, explicit=public_url)
            resolved_public = validate_endpoint_hint(
                resolved_public, allow_http_loopback=allow_lb)
            if backend_url:
                backend_url = validate_backend_url(
                    backend_url, allow_http_loopback=allow_lb)
            cred_path = credentials_file_for(cfg, data_dir, explicit=credentials_file)
            installation_id = own_installation_id(data_dir, cfg)
            preflight_destination(cred_path)
        except (CoordinatorError, me_setup.SetupError) as exc:
            err(f"error: {me_setup.redact(str(exc))}")
            return 2
        if update_config:

                fresh = me_setup.load_config(data_dir)

                    "public_home_url": resolved_public,

                fresh["coordinator"] = coord
                fresh["updated_at"] = __import__("datetime").datetime.now(
                    __import__("datetime").timezone.utc).isoformat()
                me_setup.write_atomic(

                env_text = me_setup.render_service_env(

            except (OSError, me_setup.SetupError, KeyError, ValueError) as exc:
                err(f"error: cannot record coordinator prepare: {me_setup.redact(str(exc))}")
                return 1
        log(f"coordinator prepare ok: installation_id={installation_id}")

        return 0

    def own_installation_id(data_dir: Path, cfg: dict) -> str:
        """Authoritative installation: home DB first, config reservation second."""
        try:
            db_path = Path(cfg["service"]["db_path"])
        except (KeyError, TypeError):
            db_path = data_dir / "data" / "home.sqlite"
        db_id = me_setup.read_db_installation_id(db_path)
        if db_id:
            return db_id
        cfg_id = (cfg.get("installation_id") or "").strip()
        if not cfg_id:
            raise CoordinatorError("config has no installation_id; run `setup` first")
        return cfg_id

    // Ephemeral one-time-secret request guard (F9 review).
    //
    // A screen that mints a one-time secret must never publish a late response
    // after the user backgrounded, discarded, unmounted, or changed account:
    // the cleared secret would otherwise reappear. This module is the single
    // reusable mechanism the native ticket UI and the contract tests share:
    //   - tryAcquire() grants at most one in-flight request (double-tap safe:
    //     the second tap before the first settles gets null, never a second
    //     mint). Release is generation-scoped, so a late finally cannot free a
    //     newer request's slot.
    //   - invalidate() retires the current generation (clear / discard /
    //     background / account change incl. logout→login to the SAME identity /
    //     unmount) and frees any in-flight slot.
    //   - isCurrent(gen) MUST be checked after EVERY await before publishing UI
    //     state (ticket, handoff, or copy feedback). Expired arrivals are never
    //     published (see shouldPublishTicketArrival).
    // Wiping the OS clipboard on scope clear is deliberately NOT done here:
    // ownership of the clipboard cannot be proven afterwards, and clearing it
    // would destroy text the user copied themselves.
    
    import { isActivationTicketExpired } from './backend-client.ts';
    import type { ActivationTicket } from './backend-client.ts';
    
    export class EphemeralRequestGuard {
      private generation = 0;
      private owner: number | null = null;
    
      /** Current generation; capture before an await, verify after. */
      current(): number {
        return this.generation;
      }
    
      /**
       * Claim the single in-flight slot. Returns the generation to fence the
       * request with, or null when a request is already in flight (double-tap).
       */
      tryAcquire(): number | null {
        if (this.owner !== null) return null;
        this.owner = this.generation;
        return this.generation;
      }
    
      /** Free the slot, but only when the caller still owns it. */
      release(generation: number): void {
        if (this.owner === generation) this.owner = null;
      }
    
      /** Retire the generation: cleared, discarded, backgrounded, account moved. */
      invalidate(): void {
        this.generation += 1;
        this.owner = null;
      }
    
      /** True when no invalidate() happened since the generation was captured. */
      isCurrent(generation: number): boolean {
        return generation === this.generation;
      }
    }
    
    /** Stable fingerprint for the account scope a ticket request belongs to. */
    export function activationScopeFingerprint(input: {
      accountId: string | null;
      issuer: string | null;
      backendUrl: string | null;
      status: string;
    }): string {
      return `${input.accountId ?? ''}|${input.issuer ?? ''}|${input.backendUrl ?? ''}|${input.status}`;
    }
    
    /** A just-arrived ticket may be published only when current AND unexpired. */
    export function shouldPublishTicketArrival(
      ticket: ActivationTicket,
      generation: number,
      guard: EphemeralRequestGuard,
    ): boolean {
      return guard.isCurrent(generation) && !isActivationTicketExpired(ticket);
    }
    
    /** Stale copy feedback must never appear after a scope change or discard. */
    export function shouldPublishCopyFeedback(
      generation: number,
      guard: EphemeralRequestGuard,
    ): boolean {
      return guard.isCurrent(generation);
    }

    def _final_text(messages: list, initial_count: int = 0) -> str:
        # Graph-final semantics: the terminal AIMessage carries the answer. An
        # intermediate message may hold narration alongside tool_calls, so pure
        # final text (no tool calls) wins; narration next to tool calls is only
        # a fallback when no pure final exists. An empty tool-call message never
        # contributes text, so extraction can no longer mask a structured final
        # as "" (which previously collapsed to "done").
        #
        # initial_count is the count of injected conversation-history turns at
        # the head of `messages` (op=run only). History can NEVER substitute
        # for the new model reply: scanning starts after the boundary, so a
        # stale historical assistant answer is never returned. When this run
        # produced no new text, "" is returned honestly (caller emits "done").
        seq = list(messages[initial_count:] if initial_count else messages)
        fallback = ""
        for m in reversed(seq):
            if not isinstance(m, AIMessage):
                continue
            text = _message_text(m)
            if not text.strip():
                continue
            if getattr(m, "tool_calls", None):
                if not fallback:
                    fallback = text
                continue
            return text
        return fallback

    def _list_children_safe(rpc) -> tuple[list[dict] | None, str | None]:
        """Best-effort direct-children listing via fd-3 RPC.
    
        Returns (children, error_code). Missing RPC -> (None, 'missing').
        Home errors propagate honestly; unknown ids are denials upstream.
        """
        if rpc is None:
            return None, "missing"
        try:
            res = rpc.call("list_children", {})
        except ToolDeniedError as exc:
            return None, exc.code
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
            return None, "tool_error"
        if not isinstance(res, dict):
            return [], None
        kids = res.get("children", [])
        if not isinstance(kids, list):
            kids = []
        out = [k for k in kids if isinstance(k, dict)]
        return out, None

    # Bounded conversation-context contract (existing home field, consumed here).
    # Home already scopes to owner + same conversation (latest 10, each <=2k);
    # the runtime re-enforces identical hard bounds and never reads history by
    # message IDs from the filesystem. Textual history is untrusted conversation
    # data (same policy as the user request): it is passed as Human/AIMessage
    # conversation turns only, never promoted to system/developer/tool roles.
    # No semantic-memory retrieval/scheduler: only this bounded window.
    MAX_CONTEXT_MESSAGES = 10
    MAX_CONTEXT_TEXT_CHARS = 2000
    MAX_CONTEXT_TOTAL_CHARS = 20000
    _CONTEXT_ROLES = ("user", "assistant")
    
    
    def _sanitize_context_refs(raw) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
        """Validate untrusted home `context_refs` into bounded (role, text).
    
        Malformed caller fields never crash or widen: non-list is rejected by
        the caller as invalid_request; non-dict entries, unknown kind/role, and
        empty/non-string text are ignored consistently. Each text is truncated
        to MAX_CONTEXT_TEXT_CHARS; at most MAX_CONTEXT_MESSAGES are kept (most
        recent wins); aggregate is capped at MAX_CONTEXT_TOTAL_CHARS by keeping
        the most recent turns within budget.
        """
        if raw is None:
            return []
        if not isinstance(raw, list):
            raise ValueError("context_refs must be a list")
        valid: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
        for entry in raw:
            if not isinstance(entry, dict):
                continue
            if entry.get("kind") != "message":
                continue
            role = entry.get("role")
            if role not in _CONTEXT_ROLES:
                continue
            text = entry.get("text")
            if not isinstance(text, str):
                continue
            if not text.strip():
                continue
            valid.append((role, text[:MAX_CONTEXT_TEXT_CHARS]))
        # Most recent wins when the caller exceeds the bound.
        if len(valid) > MAX_CONTEXT_MESSAGES:
            valid = valid[-MAX_CONTEXT_MESSAGES:]
        # Aggregate cap: keep most recent turns within budget.
        total = sum(len(t) for _, t in valid)
        while total > MAX_CONTEXT_TOTAL_CHARS and valid:
            dropped_role, dropped_text = valid.pop(0)
            total -= len(dropped_text)
        return valid
    
    
    def _message_text(m) -> str:
        """Extract model-authored display text from a chat message.
    
        Joins ALL recognized provider text blocks (`text`, `output_text`) in
        list order so mixed standard + Responses styles preserve both portions
        (the maintained `AIMessage.text` API only joins `type: "text"` on the
        installed SDK and would drop the provider portion on early return).
        Reasoning/refusal/image/tool-call/metadata blocks are never text.

    def _validate_request(obj: object) -> dict:
        if not isinstance(obj, dict):
            raise ValueError("request must be a JSON object")
        if obj.get("bridge") != BRIDGE:
            raise ValueError("bridge must be 'runtime-bridge-v1'")
        op = obj.get("op", "run")
        if op not in ("run", "resume"):
            raise ValueError("op must be 'run' or 'resume'")
        for f in ("run_id", "user_id", "conversation_id"):
            v = obj.get(f)
            if not v or not isinstance(v, str):
                raise ValueError(f"{f} is required")
        ws = obj.get("workspace")
        if not ws or not isinstance(ws, str):
            raise ValueError("workspace is required")
        if op == "run" and not obj.get("request"):
            raise ValueError("request text is required for op=run")
        caps = obj.get("capabilities")
        if not isinstance(caps, dict):
            raise ValueError("capabilities object is required")
        # Cheap defense-in-depth: capability flags are strict bools (the home
        # service is the owner of enforcement; non-bool truthy values such as
        # "true"/1 must not widen access through JSON coercion).
        for flag in ("files", "web_fetch", "browser", "code_exec", "animation"):
            if flag in caps and not isinstance(caps[flag], bool):
                raise ValueError(f"capabilities.{flag} must be a boolean")
        allowlist = caps.get("network_egress_allowlist", [])
        if allowlist is not None and not isinstance(allowlist, list):
            raise ValueError("capabilities.network_egress_allowlist must be a list")
        if not isinstance(obj.get("model"), dict):
            raise ValueError("model object is required")
        budgets = obj.get("budgets") or {}
        if not isinstance(budgets, dict):
            raise ValueError("budgets must be an object")
        if "context_refs" in obj and obj.get("context_refs") is not None \
                and not isinstance(obj.get("context_refs"), list):

        return obj
